open.title: MAJOR ARCHITECTURE FINDING, now operator-directed to build — there is no feat-effects engine anywhere in the compute pipeline.
open.body: QA verified concretely, not reasoned abstractly: built a real `CharacterInput` from the GE-06 fixture (already `Computed`), added `feat:toughness` to `selected_feats` alongside the required trio, ran it through the real `build_pilot_headless_receipt` entry point, compared before/after. Status stayed `Computed` both times (the combat-posture gate only checks Dodge/Weapon Focus *presence*, no exact-feat-set restriction, so an extra feat doesn't risk breaking the build). Toughness genuinely present in `selected_feats` (checked directly). **HP was 12 both with and without Toughness** — checked via both `class_chassis.fighter.level_1_hit_points` and `durability::compute_max_hp` independently. Real PF1 Toughness is a flat +3 HP at level 1; the real value should be 15. Zero explanations anywhere mention "toughness." **Confirmed system-wide, not Toughness-specific**: grepped `pilot_compute.rs` for any `selected_feats` reference beyond the two hardcoded presence-checks (Dodge, Weapon Focus) in the posture gate — zero hits. There is no general feat-effects computation anywhere in this file; Power Attack, Dodge, and Weapon Focus are the only 3 feats with any mechanical consequence at all, and even those are hardcoded into one fixed deterministic posture, not a general mechanism. Every other selectable feat (of the 185-record CRB catalog the picker exposes) is purely recorded data with zero computed effect. **Correctly sized, not understated or overstated**: QA explicitly declined to presume the sizing call, but flagged this is architecturally the same shape as the already-deferred AC/attack-bonus/skill-posture item (this doc's item 1) — "the correct math doesn't exist yet, not just disconnected." **Not assigned to backend, not attempted this wave** — a general feat-effects engine is squarely future-epic scope, same bucket as the headless/corpus-aware architecture question. Flagged here for the operator's eventual review alongside item 1, since it materially affects how far v0.6 alpha actually is from bar item 3's "select feats" affordance being mechanically meaningful, not just UI-present. **Un-deferred and landed (backend, 2026-07-24) — operator directive: "easy enough, you need to create a feats engine," scoped to one real feat first.** New module `src/rules_core/feat_effects.rs`: `hp_bonus_from_feats(selected_feats: &[String]) -> i16` scans for grounded feat effects and sums them, scoped to exactly Toughness's real flat +3 HP for now (not a 185-feat resolver in one pass, per the operator's own scoping) — shaped to extend one feat/match-arm at a time later. **A real string-convention trap caught before it could ship silently wrong**: QA's original finding used `"feat:toughness"` (matching the three hardcoded fixed-loadout feats' bespoke `"feat:<name>"` id space), but traced the real live pipeline before writing the fix and found the actual value a live user's `selected_feats` entry contains is the raw catalog key, `"Toughness"` (verified through the full chain: `feat_data/general.rs`'s `FeatTableEntry.key`, `FeatCatalogEntryDto`'s verbatim passthrough with no transform, `CharacterSheet.tsx`'s `entry.key` sent directly as `featId`). Keying on `"feat:toughness"` (QA's test string, not a real production shape) would have compiled, passed a same-shaped unit test, and never fired for a single real user. `durability.rs`'s `compute_max_hp` signature is untouched (avoiding blast radius into the parity-comparator's own call site); `load_character_durability_at_root` (`character_hub.rs`) now adds the feat bonus on top of `compute_max_hp`'s result as a separate, explicit step. Genuine RED→GREEN: the wiring was temporarily disabled, the new test failed with the exact expected 12-vs-15 mismatch, then restored and confirmed green. 5 new lib tests (including one that explicitly proves the old `"feat:toughness"` string does NOT match, pinning the correct convention) + 1 new desktop test. 233/233 lib, 201/201 desktop. Widening to more feats is real future scope, not attempted here — the pattern is proven, not yet generalized. **Widened to 3 more feats (backend, 2026-07-24): Great Fortitude, Iron Will, Lightning Reflexes — each a real flat +2 to one named save.** Picked over Skill Focus (the other obvious candidate) after checking its catalog record directly: its `effect` qualifiers carry a `%LIST` placeholder, PCGen's own marker for a player-chosen target, so it needs to know *which* skill was picked — `selected_feats` has no slot to record that (the same shape of gap Weapon Focus's hardcoded compound id only works around for the one fixed-loadout case, not a general catalog pick). Left for a future slice rather than forced into this bounded pass. Unlike Toughness (wired into `durability.rs`'s separate, non-claim-gated command), these 3 extend `pilot_compute.rs`'s `compute_total_saves` directly — the claim-gated `total_saves` pillar itself. This does not reopen the item-1 architecture question: the non-claim-gated DTO-enrichment pattern (shape (c)) exists specifically for corpus-blocked math; feats are headless-accessible (`selected_feats` needs no corpus), so wiring straight into the claim-gated computation is the direct, correct fix — the same category as fixing items 14/20's silently-wrong values, not a workaround. `feat_effects::save_bonuses_from_feats` returns a small local `SaveBonusesFromFeats` struct (deliberately not reusing `pilot_compute::BaseSaves`, keeping `feat_effects.rs` a dependency-free leaf module). Genuine RED→GREEN: 7 new `feat_effects.rs` tests (each feat isolated, all three stacking, the real "Improved" variant feats correctly not matching) plus 2 new end-to-end `pilot_compute.rs` tests against the real Fighter fixture, wiring temporarily disabled to confirm the exact expected failure before restoring. 254/254 lib, 203/203 desktop. **Independently re-verified, clean, real ID chain re-traced end to end (QA, 2026-07-24).** Confirmed `"Toughness"` (not `"feat:toughness"`) is genuinely what a live pick sends by re-tracing the full chain themselves: `feat_data/general.rs`'s `key` field → `feat_catalog.rs`'s verbatim passthrough → `CharacterSheet.tsx`'s `entry.key` sent as `featId` in both `handleAddFeat` and `handleLevelUpFeatPick`. Confirmed additivity (exactly one call site for `hp_bonus_from_feats`, zero feat-related logic anywhere else in `compute_max_hp`/`explain_fighter_level1_hit_points` — no double-counting risk). Reproduced RED themselves (disabled the bonus term, watched the exact 12-vs-15 mismatch, restored). **3-feat widening (f38e9f33) independently re-verified, clean (QA, 2026-07-24).** Catalog keys re-confirmed directly against `feat_data/general.rs` rather than trusted from the commit message: `"Great Fortitude"`→`["SAVE","Fortitude","2"]`, `"Iron Will"`→`["SAVE","Will","2"]`, `"Lightning Reflexes"`→`["SAVE","Reflex","2"]`, all matching the code's constants and +2 magnitude exactly; the "Improved" variant feats used in the non-match test confirmed as real, distinct catalog entries (`effect: None`), not strawmen. Stacking confirmed non-double-counting: `save_bonuses_from_feats` has exactly one call site, applying each field to its own save only. No claim-gating risk: the bonus sits after `compute_total_saves`'s existing early-return, pure arithmetic on an already-decided path. RED→GREEN reproduced independently (swapped in `SaveBonusesFromFeats::default()`, got the exact expected `left: 4 / right: 6` failures on both new tests, restored). Ran clean: 7/7 new `feat_effects.rs` tests, 2/2 new `pilot_compute.rs` tests, 254/254 full lib suite. **Item 17 fully independently verified end to end, both slices, nothing outstanding.** **RESOLVED (frontend, `7360fe4a`) — the Defense tab doesn't refetch durability after a feat pick.** Was: `CharacterSheet.tsx`'s `durability` state only refetched on a `useEffect` keyed to `[props.row.characterId]`; neither `handleAddFeat` nor `handleLevelUpFeatPick` triggered a refetch. **Fixed**: a shared `refreshDurability()` helper now called after a successful feat grant on both paths, falling back to `null` on failure (same honest treatment as the initial per-character load). Live-verified both paths (HP 22/22→25/25 via the Feats-tab picker, then live update again via a level-up feat pick), no reselect needed. **Independently verified (QA, 2026-07-24)**: confirmed both call sites invoke `refreshDurability()`, correctly placed strictly after the `Blocked` early-return so it never fires on a rejected mutation; confirmed the failure-path fallback matches the initial-load pattern exactly (`catch { setDurability(null) }`, identical shape); confirmed no ordering/race risk (`await addFeatSelection` resolves, including its synchronous save, before the refetch fires). Live-UI leg attempted but inconclusive on an unrelated environment rendering issue (`libEGL`/DRI3 error, screenshots came back black despite a correctly-launched window) — correctly not chased further per standing practice, called clean on the strength of the code read, regression suite (69/69, typecheck clean), and the commit's own live-verified numbers. **OPERATOR DIRECTIVE (Todd Hintzmann, 2026-07-24) — build it, no longer deferred.** Explicit call: "easy enough, you need to create a feats engine." Un-deferred and added to the actionable backlog. Scope, per `future-epic-scoping.md`'s own sizing note (gap B): a per-feat effect resolver wired into HP/attack/skill/save totals for the CRB feat catalog — starting with a real, bounded slice (the feats with the most mechanical weight and highest chance of a real fixture to verify against, e.g. Toughness's flat +3 HP, since that's the exact gap QA's own verification already demonstrated) rather than all 185 records at once, following this swarm's established "prove one real case end-to-end before widening" discipline. **In progress (backend, 2026-07-24)** — dispatches resumed; backend landed item 7 first, now starting this one.

open.title: OPERATOR QUESTION (surfaced by backend's item-1 design pass, 2026-07-24) — should `Computed` ever accept an equipment loadout other than the one exact hardcoded posture?
open.body: Not an engineering call: `unmet_combat_posture_conditions`/`unmet_selected_skill_posture_conditions` gate on exact `item_id` matches (`"item:longsword"`, `"item:chain_shirt"`), completely independent of whether the compute engine could correctly handle other gear. This means bridging the headless/corpus-aware architecture wall (item 1's fix shapes a/b) buys **zero** currently-displayed value on its own — every build that reaches `Computed` today already uses only the one hardcoded posture, so widening what the math *could* compute changes nothing unless this gate is separately widened to accept other item ids. This is a claim-gating philosophy question (how much loadout variation is "supported enough" to honestly claim `Computed`, given the no-stub/never-persist-unproven-build discipline this whole swarm runs on) — distinct from and prerequisite to any value from shapes (a)/(b). Shape (c) (backend's recommendation, see item 1) sidesteps this entirely by surfacing corpus-derived AC/ACP as a non-claim-gated display section instead of trying to widen the gate. Not resolved here; genuinely the operator's call. **OPERATOR DECISION (Todd Hintzmann, 2026-07-24) — widen the gate to accept any equipment.** Explicit call, made after the swarm-wide closure-readiness checkpoint (item 31): `unmet_combat_posture_conditions`/`unmet_selected_skill_posture_conditions` should stop gating on exact hardcoded `item_id`s and instead validate whatever loadout is actually selected. This is real, substantial engineering scope — effectively item 1's original fix shapes (a)/(b) (thread corpus through the compute pipeline, or move the claim gate to the corpus-aware layer), not a quick flip, and every equipment/weapon combination that newly reaches `Computed` needs to be verified genuinely correct, not just unblocked. **Not dispatched as a single bounded task** — given the scale (backend's own item-1 design doc already sized shape (a) at ~347 call sites), backend should first produce a scoping/sequencing plan (same shape as `item-1-architecture-wall-design.md`) before implementation starts, so this doesn't turn into an unbounded, un-verifiable mega-change. This decision also directly informs item 1's multi-weapon question below (an equipment-attachment schema is needed either way). **SCOPE DISCOVERY, backend stopped before coding (2026-07-24) — the gate can't be swapped in isolation without regressing into fabricated values.** Before writing sub-task 4, backend traced `unmet_combat_posture_conditions`/`unmet_selected_skill_posture_conditions`'s own gated functions (`compute_combat_baseline`'s `baseline_armor_class`/`baseline_melee_attack_bonus`, `compute_selected_skill_modifiers`'s climb/intimidate/swim) and found they are hardcoded arithmetic on compile-time constants (`ARMOR_CLASS_BASE + CHAIN_SHIRT_ARMOR_BONUS + ... `), not real per-item corpus resolution — zero corpus access anywhere in either function, by construction (the headless layer has no corpus parameter). **Why this matters**: naively widening only the gate check while leaving the arithmetic untouched would let a character in, say, a Breastplate instead of the fixed Chain Shirt reach `Computed` and then get served the *exact same hardcoded* numbers regardless of what they actually have equipped — not a completeness gap but a fabricated-value regression, the exact failure mode the no-stub-mvp doctrine exists to catch. Backend correctly asked whether this now needs the operator's eyes since it reads as a correctness question, not just an engineering one. **Lead ruling: no operator escalation needed — this is a doctrine-mandated implementation detail of the already-made decision, not a new policy question.** The operator decided the *policy* (widen the gate, replace it outright); they never authorized shipping fabricated numbers to get there, and the no-stub-mvp doctrine (`scope: universal`, standing, not re-litigated per-decision) already forbids it regardless of who decides. There is only one correct way to implement the operator's decision without violating that doctrine: move the arithmetic to real corpus-resolved computation. **Approved sequencing** (backend's own proposal): (1) new corpus-aware `baseline_armor_class`/`baseline_melee_attack_bonus`, sourced from `compute_equipment_effects`'s already-real `armor_class_delta`/`armor_check_penalty_total`/`attack_bonus_delta`/`to_hit_bonus` (sub-tasks 1/2's own output) — verified byte-identical against today's hardcoded formula for the existing fixed posture, which doubles as both the compatibility check and the correctness proof the corpus-resolved path is right; (2) same treatment for the selected-skill pillar; (3) only then swap the command-layer gate to consult the new path. `base_attack_bonus`/`base_saves` are unaffected (already class/level-generic, not posture-gated). Sub-task 4 is now meaningfully bigger than originally scoped — flagged here plainly rather than quietly absorbed, per this doc's own recurring practice. **Further boundary drawn, first slice scoped to armor/shield only (backend, 2026-07-24, lead-approved).** A second hardcoded dependency surfaced: `fighter_weapon_training_attack_bonus` (Weapon Training's contribution to melee attack bonus) is gated on the "Heavy Blades" weapon-training group, hardcoded because the fixed posture's Longsword happens to be a Heavy Blade. Widening the *weapon* to any resolvable item would require mapping an arbitrary weapon to its real PF1 weapon-training group — a distinct, real data-mapping problem, not something already built. **This slice's boundary**: widen armor/shield only (any resolvable `arms_armor`-category item or genuine absence, real `armor_class_delta`/`max_dex_cap`/`armor_check_penalty_total`), leave the weapon requirement exactly as today (must still be the Longsword, keeping Weapon Training's group-matching valid) and feat requirements exactly as today (a separate, undecided question from the already-settled "never block on an unrecognized feat *effect*" policy). Still a real, meaningful widening — a Fighter could wear Breastplate/Full Plate or go shieldless and get genuinely correct AC. Weapon-loadout widening is a distinct, later increment. Same "prove the narrow case first" discipline as Toughness-before-widening and the single-weapon-before-per-weapon slice; lead agrees, no operator input needed. **Both pillars built and lead-verified, not yet committed (backend, 2026-07-24).** New `compute_combat_baseline_from_corpus`/`compute_selected_skill_modifiers_from_corpus` in `pilot_compute_corpus.rs`, real per-item resolution via `compute_equipment_effects`. Exposed ~29 previously-private `pilot_compute.rs` helpers/constants as `pub(crate)` to avoid duplicating the level-based Weapon/Armor Training math and posture constants — verified via `git diff` that each is a pure visibility-prefix addition, zero behavior change. **The correctness proof**: one test drives both the old hardcoded path and the new corpus-aware path through the identical fixed posture at every Fighter armor/weapon-training breakpoint (levels 1/3/5/7/9/11/15/20) plus Wizard and Rogue level 1, asserting byte-identical `melee_attack_bonus`/`armor_class`/`climb`/`intimidate`/`swim` — passes with no discrepancy. 7 more tests prove the real widening: a Breastplate computes its own correct AC; an equipped shield (previously required-absent) adds its real bonus; no armor computes a real unarmored AC; a real enhancement attached to the required Longsword (connecting sub-tasks 1/2/6 end to end) raises the attack bonus by its exact real value; a second weapon and an unresolvable item are both honestly `Blocked`, not guessed. **Lead independently ran** the new 8-test module (`corpus_aware_posture_widening_tests`): 8/8 pass, matches exactly. Not yet wired into any command (sub-task 5) or committed as of this check. **Landed (`6ef7f3ef`, 2026-07-24), lead independently re-confirmed with a fresh full-workspace run.** 4292/4292 root-crate tests (up from 4284 — 8 new), 211/211 desktop, both matching backend's own report exactly. Sub-task 4 fully closed; sub-task 5 (the actual command-layer gate swap) is next. **Sub-task 5 landed (`350e6566`, 2026-07-24) — the re-verification bar caught a real regression before it shipped, exactly as intended.** New chokepoint `resolve_unified_pilot_snapshot` (`pf1_adapter.rs`) replaces every command's own inline exact-posture-only check; `combat.baseline_unsupported`/`skill.selected_modifier.unsupported` are no longer independently claim-blocking (the sub-task 4 corpus-aware pillars decide those two now, for any resolvable armor/shield loadout), every other headless diagnostic still blocks exactly as before. Wired into all 7 real call sites sharing this pattern: `mutate_saved_character_at_root` (the shared chokepoint for level-up/add-equipment/add-spell/append), `create_character_at_root`, `clone_character`, `import_character`, both copies of `load_saved_character` (found a genuine pre-existing duplication between the `RuleSystemAdapter` trait impl and the direct Tauri command — not introduced by this sub-task, fixed while already there), and `recompute_character_at_root`. **The real discrepancy, caught and fixed, not shipped**: the first full desktop run came back with 9 failures. Root cause: sub-task 4's implementation required *every* `EquippedActive` selection to resolve against corpus with a known category — over-strict against the real desktop app, whose bundled demo corpus has only 2 records, and many existing tests equip a harmless second item (a Dagger, a Wand) the old exact-posture gate never cared about (it only checked its 3 hardcoded items). The new requirement turned a previously-harmless extra item into a hard block. **Fixed** by removing the requirement entirely — `compute_equipment_effects` already tolerates an unresolvable selection gracefully (skips it, contributes nothing), so the new pillars trust that same existing tolerance instead of re-blocking on top of it. The one real constraint that survives is genuine 2-real-weapon ambiguity, already naturally expressed via `attack_bonus_delta`'s existing `None` case. **Lead independently re-verified**: full workspace 4292/4292 (unchanged from sub-task 4, as expected — a wiring change, not new tests), desktop 211/211 (0 failures, confirming the fix), and specifically re-ran the 8-test `corpus_aware_posture_widening_tests` module directly — all 8 pass, including `matches_the_hardcoded_baseline_exactly_for_every_currently_computed_build` (the byte-identical proof) and a renamed test (`an_unresolvable_equipped_item_does_not_block_and_contributes_nothing`, updated from its sub-task-4 name to reflect the regression fix). **Sub-tasks 1 through 5 of the items-1+27 plan are now all fully closed.** Only sub-task 3 (operator-skipped) remains formally open on that plan, plus any further frontend attachment-UI polish. **Sub-task 6 landed both halves and lead-verified (backend `3a05539a` + frontend `a768ad85`, 2026-07-24).** Frontend wired the Gear tab: an "Attach Modifier" button per equipped item opens the existing `ItemPickerModal` scoped to Equipmods; new `attachEquipmentModifier.ts` mirrors `purchaseEquipment.ts`'s exact shape; `ResolvedEquipmentDto` gained `appliedModifiers` for nested display. Live-verified end to end against a real character: attached both an unknown-cost enhancement (free-attach path) and a known-$0-cost Masterwork modifier (a different code path) to two different items, both persisted correctly to disk targeting the right item, both survived a reload, both correctly surfaced via the unresolved-corpus indicator since the demo corpus has zero Equipmods records to resolve against. **Honest limitation noted by frontend**: the nested-nested-modifier-under-its-weapon display path is code-correct but not live-reachable today given the empty demo corpus — same "structurally correct but currently unreachable" shape as Barbarian DR and the Wizard-bootstrap branch noted elsewhere this session. **Lead independently verified**: full workspace 4284/4284 (unaffected — frontend's changes are TS-only), desktop 211/211, frontend suite 78/78 (up from 77), typecheck clean. Sub-task 6 fully closed. **Independently re-verified, two RED reproductions (QA, 2026-07-24).** Confirmed free-attach-on-unknown-cost against the real generated `EQUIPMODS_TABLE` directly, not just the doc comment's claim: `"Special Ability ~ +1 ~ Weapon"` genuinely resolves `cost_gp: None`, `"Special Quality ~ Masterwork ~ Weapon"` resolves `Some(0.0)` via first-match semantics — matching both the commit and frontend's live numbers. (Noted, not a defect: the generated table has pre-existing duplicate keys with differing `cost_gp`, resolved deterministically by first-match order — unrelated to this sub-task.) **RED #1**: disabled `local_store.rs`'s new `equipment_modifier=` line emission, reran the round-trip test — failed with `left: []` vs. two expected modifiers, exactly reproducing the silent-drop-on-save bug; restored, confirmed green. **RED #2**: changed the free-attach `None => 0` branch to `None => Blocked` — failed exactly as expected; restored, confirmed green. **RED #3**: swapped the modifier picker's routing in `buildItemPickerConfig.test.ts` for the plain equipment path — failed exactly as expected; restored, confirmed green. Confirmed frontend's `appliedModifiers` is a plain array guarded by `.length > 0`, not an `Option` — no risk of the earlier null-serialization bug class recurring here; `handleModifierPicked` refreshes from the real server response on success, zero state mutation on `Blocked`, same shape as other mutation handlers. Live-UI attempt hit the same recurring `libEGL`/DRI3 black-screen issue (risk item 29, third occurrence) — fell back to the static/RED rigor above per standing practice. Ran clean: 7/7 + 2/2 + 2/2 new tests, 275/275 lib, 211/211 desktop, 78/78 frontend, typecheck clean. Correctly left backend's new in-progress sub-task 5 diff untouched.

open.title: Alpha-bar distance — SHARPENED, then SCOPED.
open.body: Current state (`docs/architecture/status.md`, 2026-07-23): only single-class Fighter 1–3 reaches a `Computed` receipt; 7 of 10 CharacterSheet tabs stubbed; Feat picker and Money panel do not exist; level-up/skill/bio persistence are no-ops. The §1 bar (6-level multiclass, four books, PCGen parity, zero stubs) requires multiple task waves; the go/no-go checkpoints in §6 are the containment mechanism. **Update (backend, task 2 delivery):** the compute engine's `Computed` path is narrower than "Fighter 1–3" implied — it currently only computes for one exact hardcoded posture. Any other skill/equipment choice returns `Blocked` with diagnostics rather than a receipt — pre-existing engine narrowness, not something the swarm introduced, but it means most tester choices through the newly-wired UI will hit Blocked, not Computed, until this is widened. **Full scoping (backend proposal, 2026-07-23, greenlit in part):** the narrowness is actually 4 independent exactness gates in `pilot_compute.rs`, each class-agnostic except one sub-check, any deviation trips `Blocked` with no partial credit: 1. `unmet_combat_posture_conditions` — exact Longsword+Chain Shirt, no shield, Power Attack selected-inactive, Dodge+Weapon Focus feats (one Fighter-only sub-check). 2. `unmet_selected_skill_posture_conditions` — exactly Climb/Intimidate/Swim rank 1, chain shirt equipped, nothing else. 3. A Human-Wizard-only spellbook posture gate (level ≤3, canonical Evocation specialization, exact prepared spellbook) — newly found, wasn't previously documented, fires independently. 4. AC specifically: `baseline_armor_class` (the gate) never calls `equipment_effects.rs`'s `compute_equipment_effects`, which already computes *real, correct* per-item AC deltas for arbitrary gear and is already wired into the separate desktop-UI equipment tab. The correct math exists and is simply disconnected from the gate. **Sizing by pillar (backend's original proposal):** AC — small-medium, a real wiring job (initially greenlit, scoped to Fighter/Wizard/Rogue: splice the existing correct math into the gate). Attack bonus — large, needs genuinely new equipment-driven to-hit math that doesn't exist (feats/enhancement bonuses only today). Skills — medium-large: `allocate_skill_ranks` only maps 5 skills, class-skill recognition is Fighter-only, and has no armor-check-penalty term at all (explicitly deferred in its own doc comment) — not a drop-in fix even for the 5 skills it knows. Wizard spellbook gate — separate, untouched by the above. **AC SLICE DROPPED — the real finding is architectural, not per-pillar (backend, mid-implementation, 2026-07-23):** the original AC sizing assumed the correct per-item math could be spliced directly into the gate. It can't, cheaply. `compute_combat_baseline`/`baseline_armor_class` (the thing that gates `Computed`/`Blocked`) lives in the **headless** compute layer — `build_pilot_headless_receipt`/`compute_pilot_base_chassis` take a `CharacterInput` only, **no corpus parameter**, by design. Real per-item AC values only exist via `equipment_effects::arms_armor::compute_arms_armor_effect`, which needs a corpus-resolved `EquipmentRecord` — corpus access the headless layer structurally doesn't have. The static, corpus-free `equipment_tables()` carries no AC-bonus field at all. Bridging this means either (a) threading a corpus parameter through the entire headless chassis call chain — ~347 call-site grep hits, a blast radius comparable to or bigger than task 4's Rogue widening — or (b) moving the `Computed`/`Blocked` decision itself to the corpus-aware layer (`pilot_compute_corpus.rs`'s `compute_pilot_with_corpus`, which already has both), a real architecture decision about which layer owns claim-gating, not an implementation detail. Backend caught this *before* writing the change and stopped to ask rather than push forward on unscoped work or fabricate a corpus-free approximation — correct call, no code written. **Decision:** dropped for this swarm. Option 1 (leave the gate alone, since the corpus-aware desktop equipment tab already shows real AC for arbitrary gear today — that's existing behavior, not new work) is close to a no-op and not worth landing on its own. Option 2 (the corpus-threading/layer-ownership change) is a genuine future epic, not a wave-2 item — **flagging for the operator**: this likely isn't just an AC problem. If attack-bonus and general-skill widening (already sized large/medium-large above) hit the same headless/corpus-aware split, bridging that one architecture boundary might be the actual unlock for all three posture-narrowness pillars at once, rather than three independent slices. Worth a dedicated scoping pass before any future wave attempts AC, attack-bonus, or skill-posture widening again. Backend proceeding instead to items 2-4 (durability, money-conversion PCGen verification, comparator field-extraction), none of which share this problem. **Follow-up scoping pass, answered precisely, split by dimension (backend, 2026-07-24, read-only, no code).** Confirms the hypothesis for two of the three remaining pillars, refutes it for the third: - **Attack-bonus widening: YES, same wall, confirmed exactly.** Real to-hit for arbitrary weapons needs `equipment_effects/equipmods.rs`'s `compute_equipmods_effect`, which reads a weapon's magic enhancement bonus (`WeaponEnhancementBonus`, the corpus's `BONUS:WEAPON|TOHIT|...|TYPE=Enhancement` token) off a corpus-resolved `EquipmentRecord` — same structural requirement as AC's `compute_arms_armor_effect`. The static, corpus-free `equipment_tables()` table carries nothing enhancement-related. - **Skill-posture widening splits into two genuinely different sub-problems.** (1) Armor-check-penalty for arbitrary armor: **YES, same wall** — the real corpus record's `ACCHECK:` token exists (verified against `Leather Armor (Base)`, `ACCHECK:0`) but the static `equipment_tables()` doesn't carry it. (2) Class-skill-list recognition (which skills are class skills for Wizard/Rogue/Cleric/etc., beyond the already-fixed Fighter/Rogue case): **NO, this is NOT corpus-blocked** — it's a labor-volume problem, not an architecture wall. This data isn't in any static table today, but it doesn't need corpus access to get there: it can be hand-authored as literal per-class skill lists, exactly the existing `GROUNDED_FIGHTER_CLASS_SKILLS` precedent already used in `skill_allocation.rs`. - **Bottom line for the future-epic writeup:** bridging the headless/corpus-aware boundary would genuinely unlock both AC-shaped gaps (attack-bonus enhancement, skill ACP) at once — confirms the hypothesis for those two dimensions specifically. It would **not**, by itself, close the class-skill-list gap, which needs separate hand-authored per-class data regardless of which layer owns the gate. Both halves stated explicitly so a future scoping pass doesn't overstate what the architecture fix alone would buy. **NEW — Wizard spellbook gate is unreachable, not just narrow (frontend, 2026-07-23).** Gate 3 above turns out to be categorically worse than gates 1/2: it isn't merely one exact combination out of many, it's **structurally impossible to satisfy through any shipped UI path**. `compose_character_input` (the fixed-loadout composer every UI-created character goes through) never seeds the required `choice:wizard_school_specialization -> school:evocation` plus opposed-Necromancy/Transmutation choices for any class, and `CreateCharacterForm.tsx` has no arcane-school field at all. Verified live two independent ways — fresh Wizard creation, and multiclassing Wizard onto an existing character via level-up — both correctly `Blocked` with the real diagnostic, neither persisted (reject-don't-persist invariant held). This directly blocks bar item 3's "select spells at each spell-gaining level" for the entire class most associated with spellcasting, and is likely the deeper reason `status.md`'s "only Fighter reaches Computed" framing has held architecture-wide. **Decision:** seed the required choices as a hardcoded default in `compose_character_input`, mirroring the existing precedent — Fighter's loadout already hardcodes Power Attack/Dodge/Weapon Focus the same way, so this is consistent with the fixed-loadout composer's current maturity level, not a new kind of shortcut. Sufficient for the bar: item 3 requires spell *selection*, not arcane-school *choice* — hardcoding the school while leaving real spell selection intact satisfies the literal requirement. A real UI-facing arcane-school selector (frontend's Option A) is a separate, larger feature — **backlog, not blocking**. Backend pausing item 4 to take this first, since it unblocks a literal named bar requirement rather than test infrastructure. **SOBERING FOLLOW-UP — Wizard's fix is a lucky exception, not a pattern (frontend survey, 2026-07-23).** Checked the other four caster classes in `pilot_compute.rs` (Cleric, Druid, Bard, Sorcerer) for an equivalent single-seeded-choice gate. None exists. Each has its own `supported_X_level` gate with a doc comment listing genuinely unimplemented calculation subsystems, not missing UI inputs: **Cleric** — no channel energy resolution, no domain spell-list contents, no spellbook posture, no spells prepared, no spontaneous cure/inflict conversion, no spell slots per day, no save DCs, no Wisdom bonus spells. **Druid** — same shape, flat identity records for class features (Wild Empathy etc.) but zero spell math anywhere. **Bard** — flat numbers for non-spell features, explicitly "no spell math whatsoever," plus no bardic-performance execution engine at all (no action economy, no round tracking, no Fascinate resolution). **Sorcerer** — doc comment explicitly says "no bloodline arcana, or spell math," same shape as Bard. None of these are "one missing seeded choice away from Computed" the way Wizard was — they're missing entire arithmetic/mechanic subsystems, which seeding a default cannot fix. **Scoping implication:** the alpha bar's "any class... from the four primary books" (§1 item 2) is a substantially bigger lift than Wizard's fix suggests — backend's incoming fix makes Wizard the *second* class (alongside Fighter) a tester can reach `Computed` with, but the other four full/partial spellcasters remain genuine multi-epic engine work, consistent with `status.md`'s existing "only Fighter reaches Computed" framing. Worth the operator weighing this when judging how close v0.6 alpha actually is to its own bar. **PARTIALLY RESOLVED then CORRECTED, 2026-07-23: the compute-gate fix (3484b5d) landed, but frontend's live testing found it necessary, not sufficient — see the new item 10 below. Wizard does not yet reach `Computed` through any shipped UI path.** **Comparator wiring confirms the architecture split is real, not AC-specific — then finds a clean way around it for encumbrance (backend, 2026-07-23).** Wiring `SelectedParityDimensions::from_receipt` to expose the new encumbrance/durability/money PCGen-comparison dimensions turned out to be three genuinely different problems, not one small task — backend stopped before writing code and split them honestly: **(1) durability** — small, bounded, landed. **(2) encumbrance** — initially looked blocked by the exact same headless/corpus-aware wall that killed the AC slice (`compute_encumbrance` needs real corpus-resolved item weights; `from_receipt`'s headless receipt has no corpus access) — independent confirmation the boundary is real. **RESOLVED, not deferred after all**: backend found `contract::PilotReceipt` (produced by `contract::to_pilot_receipt`) is *already* corpus-aware and already carries both `chassis` (the same struct `from_receipt` reads) and a resolved `encumbrance: EncumbranceComputation` — so instead of forcing corpus access into the headless layer, backend added a new, additive `SelectedParityDimensions::from_pilot_receipt(receipt: &contract::PilotReceipt, ...)` that reads from this already-resolved data. `from_receipt` itself is provably untouched (zero blast radius on QA's 3 existing callers). This sidesteps the architecture wall for *parity-testing* purposes without touching the harder problem of moving the `Computed`/`Blocked` gate itself into corpus-awareness (that part of the finding, relevant to AC/attack-bonus/skill-posture widening, still stands as a future epic). **(3) money** — confirmed, not deferred: a different kind of gap entirely, `money.json`'s balance is persisted session state never derived from `CharacterInput`/`PilotReceipt` at all, so there's structurally nothing for any receipt-projection function to expose. **Backlog item stands**: money parity-testing, if ever wanted, needs its own comparison path reading `money.json` directly. **OPERATOR DIRECTIVE (Todd Hintzmann, 2026-07-24) — work out the math, add to backlog.** Un-deferred, alongside items 7 and 17. Scope: this is the harder of the three un-deferred items — it isn't a single build task like starting-wealth or a bounded first-slice like Toughness's HP, it's the design/derivation work `future-epic-scoping.md` (gap A) already flagged as needing "a dedicated scoping/design pass before committing to either fix shape." Two things need working out, not one: (1) **the architecture decision** — thread a corpus parameter through the headless chassis call chain (~347 call sites) vs. move the `Computed`/`Blocked` gate to the already-corpus-aware layer (`pilot_compute_corpus.rs`); (2) **the actual combat math that doesn't exist yet** — real equipment-driven attack-bonus (enhancement bonuses, currently only feats/base BAB are computed) and the armor-check-penalty term for arbitrary armor, both confirmed genuinely unwritten, not just disconnected (backend's item-1-adjacent scoping pass). AC itself is closer to a non-issue (the desktop equipment tab already shows correct AC via the corpus-aware path) — the real payoff here is attack-bonus and skill-ACP. **Queued, third in line** — dispatches resumed; backend working items 7 (done) → 17 → this one, expected to start with the architecture-decision half before any math-derivation work, since the fix shape determines where the new formulas need to live. **Design pass done (backend, `4dadad51`, `docs/release/v0.6/item-1-architecture-wall-design.md`) — the earlier sizing was too coarse, three real findings reshape the picture.** (1) **Most of the real math already exists**: `equipment_effects.rs`'s `compute_equipment_effects` is fully written, tested, and already running in production (the desktop equipment tab calls it directly for AC); `pilot_compute_corpus.rs` already carries a `DerivedEquipmentStats` struct on every resolved item, just never populated (`::default()` unconditionally). ACP turns out to be a few-line field addition to a function that already has the record in hand, not a corpus-access problem. (2) **Attack-bonus enhancement has a genuine data-model gap, separate from corpus access**: `EquipmentSelection` is flat (`{item_id, equipped_or_active, active_state}`) with no way to express that a "+1 Enhancement to Weapon" item attaches to a specific weapon — real PF1 composes a "+1 Longsword" as base+modifier; summing the enhancement bonus without resolving that attachment would silently misapply one weapon's bonus to another or double-count on a two-weapon build. Needs its own design decision (a schema change, or a narrower one-weapon-equipped convention), independent of whichever fix shape wins. (3) **The biggest correction — bridging the corpus wall alone would not unlock a single additional equipment loadout today**: `unmet_combat_posture_conditions`/`unmet_selected_skill_posture_conditions` gate on an *exact* hardcoded `item_id` (`"item:longsword"`, `"item:chain_shirt"`), completely independent of what the math could resolve for other gear — so even with full corpus access wired into the claim gate, zero currently-displayed numbers would change. The wall's payoff is entirely contingent on a separate, larger, unasked question: **would `Computed` ever accept an equipment loadout other than the one exact hardcoded posture?** That's a claim-gating philosophy call (how much variation is "supported enough" to claim correctness), not an engineering one — logged as item 27 below for the operator, distinct from the fix-shape question. **Three fix shapes compared, with real call-site counts**: (a) thread corpus through the headless chain — ~19+37+100ish call sites, large, and per finding (3) buys nothing today without the separate posture-gate decision; (b) move the `Computed`/`Blocked` decision to the corpus-aware layer — a real cross-cutting change to every command's save/mutate control flow, same ceiling as (a); (c) **NEW, recommended** — enrich the corpus-derived DTO section (where `compute_pilot_with_corpus` already has corpus in scope) by calling the already-existing `compute_equipment_effects`, surfaced as an additional, explicitly-not-claim-gated display section, same shape `corpus_derived.equipped_items` already uses today. Zero changes to `build_pilot_headless_receipt`'s signature or any of its call sites, zero changes to claim-gating semantics. Delivers real ACP and a second AC path now; does not close attack-bonus (needs the attachment decision first). Full comparison table in the design doc. **Shape (c) implemented (backend, `08a829a1`†).** `EquipmentStatEffect`/`EquipmentEffects` (`equipment_effects.rs`) gained a real `armor_check_penalty`/`armor_check_penalty_total` field, reading the `ACCHECK:` token `arms_armor.rs`'s own doc comment already cited as present — the few-line fix the design pass predicted. `pilot_compute_corpus.rs`'s `CorpusDerivedSection` gained a new `equipment_effects: EquipmentEffects` field, computed inside `compute_pilot_with_corpus` over the `EquippedActive`-filtered equipment (mirroring `contract::to_pilot_receipt`'s own filtering exactly) via the already-existing `compute_equipment_effects` — `build_pilot_headless_receipt`'s signature and every one of its call sites untouched, as scoped, and deliberately **not** wired into any claim-gated pillar. Surfaced through the desktop DTO layer as a new `CorpusDerivedDto.equipmentEffects` section (`armorClassDelta`, `armorCheckPenaltyTotal`, `maxDexCap`, `spellFailureChance`), explicitly separate from the claim-gated `PilotSnapshotDto` fields. Attack-bonus enhancement deliberately excluded (the attachment-relationship gap from the design pass still stands, unresolved). Genuine RED→GREEN at every layer: `arms_armor.rs`'s 3 existing tests extended with real ACCHECK assertions (Leather Armor `Some(0)`, Buckler `Some(-1)`, Longsword `None`); 3 new `pilot_compute_corpus.rs` tests (real penalty present, `SelectedInactive` correctly excluded, no-equipment correctly zero) with the wiring temporarily disabled to confirm the failure before restoring; 1 new end-to-end `character_hub.rs` test proving the real Fighter fixed loadout's Chain Shirt surfaces a real nonzero ACP through the actual `create_character` command, same disable-verify-restore discipline. 236/236 lib, 202/202 desktop, full workspace 4253/0 clean. †Landed via a shared-checkout index race (backend's staged work got swept into the lead's own docs commit while restaging mid-flight) — both sides independently confirmed the content is complete, correct, and unaffected by the race; attribution corrected here for the record, not re-done. Backend correctly declined to rewrite history over a cosmetic commit-message issue in a live shared checkout. **Attack-bonus, bounded single-weapon slice landed (backend, 2026-07-24), greenlit by the lead as a real engineering-scope call distinct from item 27's philosophy question.** `EquipmentEffects` gained `attack_bonus_delta: Option<i16>`: `Some(n)` only when exactly one real weapon (a record carrying a `DAMAGE:` token, the same signal `damage_total.rs`'s own `resolve_base_damage_dice` already uses to identify a weapon) is `EquippedActive`, summing every equipped `equipmods` item's TOHIT-affecting enhancement bonus (`"TOHIT"` or `"DAMAGE,TOHIT"`, explicitly excluding a `"DAMAGE"`-only bonus, which doesn't affect the attack roll). `None` for zero or two-or-more weapons equipped — the attachment ambiguity the design pass identified stays honestly unresolved rather than guessed at; `Some(0)` is a real, distinct value from `None` (unambiguous, just no enhancement present) so the frontend must not treat the two the same. No schema change to `EquipmentSelection` — the narrower, bounded alternative to the attachment-relationship redesign, matching this session's established "prove the narrow provably-correct case" discipline (Toughness-only, the durability multiclass-order deferral, etc.). Surfaced on `CorpusDerivedDto.equipmentEffects.attackBonusDelta`, same non-claim-gated section shape (c) already established. Genuine RED→GREEN: 6 new `equipment_effects.rs` tests (single weapon + real enhancement, Masterwork TOHIT-only, a DAMAGE-only bonus correctly excluded, single weapon with no enhancement yielding a real zero, zero weapons honestly absent, two weapons honestly ambiguous), disabled-then-restored to confirm the exact expected failures; 1 extended end-to-end `character_hub.rs` test proving the real Fighter fixed loadout (exactly one weapon, no equipmods) surfaces the real `Some(0)` through the actual `create_character` command. 242/242 lib, 202/202 desktop. **OPERATOR DECISION (Todd Hintzmann, 2026-07-24) — add an equipment-attachment schema field.** Explicit call, made after the swarm-wide closure-readiness checkpoint (item 31): resolve the multi-weapon ambiguity with a real data-model change rather than leaving it honestly absent long-term. `EquipmentSelection` needs a way to express that a modifier (e.g. a "+1 Enhancement") attaches to one specific weapon, not the whole loadout — the flat `{item_id, equipped_or_active, active_state}` shape has no slot for this today. Backend to design the schema addition (new field vs. a separate attachment table/map), migrate `EquipmentSelection` and its consumers, and widen `attack_bonus_delta` to resolve correctly for 2+ weapons once the attachment is explicit. This overlaps with item 27's decision (widening the posture gate to accept any equipment) — both need the same underlying attachment data, so backend should sequence/scope them together rather than solving the schema twice. **Scoping plan landed (backend, `1f8dd2fa`, `docs/release/v0.6/items-1-and-27-scoping.md`), design/scoping only, no code.** Verified PCGen's own `.pcg` convention for an enchanted weapon before designing: a single equipment entry carrying its own applied modifiers inline (`CUSTOMIZATION:...EQMOD=...`), not two entries needing a cross-reference — so the real schema shape is `applied_modifiers: Vec<String>` directly on `EquipmentSelection`, not a separate attachment/instance-id scheme (backend's first instinct, correctly discarded as heavier and non-PCGen-faithful). Real blast radius counted, not estimated: 67 `EquipmentSelection` construction sites (42 in `tests/**`); checked `ChosenCharacterState` as an alternative location too — 74 sites there, no cheaper. **Central finding**: items 1 and 27 are no longer separable — the original item-1 design pass's "bridging the wall buys nothing" conclusion assumed the posture gate stays exact-match; now that item 27 widens it, corpus-awareness becomes a genuine prerequisite. Three gate-widening approaches compared (extend the static bootstrap table; move `Computed`/`Blocked` to the corpus-aware layer; thread corpus through the full headless chain), with a 6-step bounded sub-task sequence at the end (schema field → per-weapon attack-bonus → static category data → corpus-aware verdict → command-layer wiring → frontend attachment UI), each independently testable per this session's established incremental-widening discipline. **OPERATOR DECISIONS (Todd Hintzmann, 2026-07-24) — all three open questions from the scoping plan resolved.** (1) Feat-completeness policy: **never block `Computed` on an unrecognized feat effect** — extends the existing precedent (items 14/17/18/20/21), an unknown feat effect stays a completeness gap, not a correctness bug. (2) Gate-widening mechanism: **replace the existing exact-posture gate outright**, not the additive/keep-both approach backend recommended as lower-risk — this means the Fighter/Wizard/Rogue posture must be re-verified against the new unified corpus-aware path too, not left as an untouched fast path; backend needs the fullest test coverage on sub-task 5 (command-layer wiring) as a result, every currently-`Computed` build must still compute identically through the new single path. (3) Sub-task 3 (static category pre-filter data-authoring pass): **skip it** — go straight to the corpus-aware layer (sub-task 4), which already resolves the same question at runtime; no separate static pass needed. Dispatched to backend: proceed with sub-task 1 (schema field), coordinate the ~67-site mechanical update with QA (42 of the sites are theirs), skip sub-task 3, and build the gate widening as a full replacement per decision (2). **Sub-task 1 landed (backend, `797bd436`).** `EquipmentSelection` gained `applied_modifiers: Vec<String>`, exactly the schema shape the scoping plan verified against PCGen's own `CUSTOMIZATION:EQMOD=` convention. All 25 non-QA `EquipmentSelection` construction sites fixed (14 `src/rules_core`, 11 `apps/desktop/src-tauri`); the fixture-text grammar gained a new `equipment_modifier=<item_id>:<modifier_item_id>` line (`apply_equipment_modifier`), attaching onto an already-parsed `equipment=` selection by `item_id` using the same last-colon convention `apply_equipment_selection` already relies on (item_id may itself contain a colon) — errors with a diagnostic if the `equipment_modifier=` line has no matching prior `equipment=` line. 4 new tests (default-empty, single/multiple attach, unmatched-id diagnostic); 262/262 lib (258 baseline + 4 new), 204/204 desktop, both crates build clean. The remaining 42 `tests/**` sites are QA-owned — exact file:line list and the one-line fix sent to QA directly, coordinated per the operator's dispatch rather than touched unilaterally. **Process note, no code impact**: `cargo fmt -p codex` (no path scoping) turned out to reformat all 516 tracked files in this crate, not just the ones touched this cycle — the crate had drifted from the currently-installed rustfmt's formatting. Caught before staging (verified every non-mine file's diff was pure reformatting, no semantic change, via `git status`/`git diff`), reverted everything except the 10 intentionally-edited files, redid those by hand. Flagging so nobody else runs an unscoped `cargo fmt` in this shared checkout; a per-file `rustfmt <path>` is safe. **Sub-task 2 design fork, resolved by the lead as a bounded engineering call (not escalated — distinct from items 1/18/27's philosophy questions).** Backend correctly flagged before writing code: `EquipmentEffects.attack_bonus_delta` is a single scalar for the whole loadout; with 2+ weapons each carrying their own `applied_modifiers`, summing their to-hit bonuses into one number has no real combat meaning (which weapon are you rolling to hit with?). **Resolved**: add `to_hit_bonus: Option<i16>` to `ResolvedEquipmentEffect` (one entry per equipped selection already), computed per-selection from that weapon's own `applied_modifiers`; keep `attack_bonus_delta` exactly as it means today (`Some` only for exactly one weapon equipped, `None` for 0 or 2+), now backed by real per-weapon data instead of the old heuristic, wire contract stays additive — nothing downstream breaks, sub-task 6's UI reads the new per-item field for the real multi-weapon case whenever it's built. Same "prove the narrow case, extend additively" discipline as shape (c) and the feat-effects widening. **Landed and lead-verified (backend, `5b0c7243`, 2026-07-24).** `compute_equipment_effects` now resolves each weapon's own `applied_modifiers` directly instead of the old "sum every flat equipmods item, gate on exactly-one-weapon-total" heuristic; `ResolvedEquipmentEffect` gained the agreed `to_hit_bonus: Option<i16>`; `attack_bonus_delta` kept its exact existing semantics, no wire/DTO change (`per_item` isn't exposed on the wire yet). **Real, deliberate behavior change**: an equipmods item equipped but not listed in any weapon's `applied_modifiers` no longer auto-attaches to "the only weapon present" — explicit attachment is now required, matching the PCGen-verified shape. Checked this against the one existing e2e regression risk: the Fighter fixed-loadout test in `character_hub.rs` asserts `attack_bonus_delta == Some(0)` — safe, because that fixture has zero equipmods equipped at all, so the auto-attach-vs-explicit-attach distinction never applies to it. 6 existing tests rewritten to use `applied_modifiers`, 2 new (unattached modifier doesn't count; two weapons resolve independently). **Lead independently re-ran**: `cargo test --lib` (263/263, matches exactly) and the desktop suite (204/204). **QA's fixture fix landed (`eeaa876d`, 2026-07-24) — real count correction, and a real bug self-caught mid-flight.** QA's first automated pass over-matched: a naive text search for `EquipmentSelection {` also caught `-> EquipmentSelection {` function-signature return types, not just struct literals, corrupting a few files with misplaced braces. Caught before landing, reverted everything, rewrote more carefully. **Corrected the real count**: backend's message said 42 sites; QA independently grepped and found 32 real struct-literal construction sites plus 10 separate function-signature matches that correctly should NOT get the field — the "42" didn't match backend's own enumerated list. Diff is exactly 20 files, 32 one-line insertions, matching the corrected count precisely. **Handled a live collision correctly**: backend's sub-task 2 was mid-edit (uncommitted) on `src/rules_core/equipment_effects.rs` while QA worked, breaking QA's first build attempt with an unrelated `E0063`. QA `git stash`ed just that one file, verified their own fixture changes in isolation, then popped the stash back untouched — did not attempt to fix or work around backend's in-progress file. **Lead independently re-ran**: `cargo build --tests` clean, full `cargo test --workspace` — 4280 total passed, 0 failed across all 478 test-result blocks, matches QA's report exactly. Both sub-tasks 1 and 2 fully closed. Backend cleared to proceed to sub-task 4 (the highest-risk step, replacing the exact-posture gate per the operator's decision); frontend cleared to start sub-task 6 (equipment-modifier-attachment UI). **Sub-task 6 design done (frontend, 2026-07-24), no code yet.** Confirmed there's genuinely no existing command surface for `applied_modifiers` before asking (only reference in `character_hub.rs` is a hardcoded `Vec::new()`). Design: an "Attach Modifier" button on each equipped item's Gear-tab row, reusing the existing generic `ItemPickerModal` scoped to the Equipmods category — no new catalog query needed. Sent backend a concrete proposal directly: a new `attach_equipment_modifier` command modeled on `purchase_equipment`'s atomic-purchase shape (charges the modifier's real `cost_gp`, matching every other cost-bearing pick in the app rather than a free-grant exception), reusing `PurchaseEquipmentResponse`'s Purchased/Blocked outcome shape; plus a small DTO addition so the Gear tab can show what's already attached (not just raw ids). Deliberately bounded and flagged as such: no detach/remove affordance, flat catalog cost rather than modeling real PF1 enchantment-cost stacking. Correctly holding off on writing UI code until backend's command lands, per the no-stub discipline — a button wired to a nonexistent command would be exactly the kind of stub this doctrine forbids. **Two real gaps found before building, resolved peer-to-peer without escalating (backend+frontend, 2026-07-24).** Backend checked the proposal against real data before implementing: (1) real CRB weapon-enhancement records (+1 through +10) have no known flat `cost_gp` in the static table — real PF1 enhancement pricing is a formula (bonus² × 2000gp), not a flat catalog price, so mirroring `purchase_equipment`'s block-on-unknown-cost exactly would leave the headline use case (attaching an actual enhancement) permanently `Blocked`; (2) the bundled desktop demo corpus has zero Equipmods records at all, so an attached modifier would silently not affect the computed attack bonus unless the existing `unresolved_equipment_item_ids` tracking (item 1's shape-B fix) extends to cover `applied_modifiers` too. **Resolved between backend and frontend directly**: treat unknown cost as free-to-attach (an explicit, flagged deviation, not silent), and extend the unresolved-ids tracking — which the frontend's existing `UnresolvedNotice` component picks up with zero new frontend work. Both correctly judged this doesn't need lead/operator escalation — same shape as other bounded first-pass simplifications already made this session (explicitly flagged, not a claim-gating philosophy question), flagged to the lead for visibility rather than for a decision. Lead agrees with that read; logging for the record, not overriding. **Sub-task 6 backend half landed and lead-verified (`3a05539a`, 2026-07-24).** New `attach_equipment_modifier` Tauri command, mirroring `purchase_equipment_at_root`'s atomic resolve-cost → check-affordability → mutate → charge shape: validates `modifier_item_id` against the real catalog first (same check `append_to_character` already runs, rejecting a fabricated id before any cost/target check), treats an unknown `cost_gp` as free-to-attach per the agreed deviation. `ResolvedEquipment`/`ResolvedEquipmentDto` gained `applied_modifiers` (nested resolved records, reusing the existing DTO shape); `compute_pilot_with_corpus` resolves each selection's own modifiers the same way it resolves the selection itself, folding any unresolvable modifier into the existing `unresolved_equipment_item_ids` list. `rule_system_adapter.rs`'s `TestPf1Delegate` now reuses the shared mapper instead of hand-rolling a second mirror. **Real production bug found and fixed along the way, not introduced by this sub-task**: `SavedCharacterStore`'s save/load round-trip never had a writer for `applied_modifiers` — sub-task 1 only built the fixture-text *parser* side (for tests), never the production *writer* `character_hub.rs`'s real save path uses, so every attached modifier was silently dropped on save. Fixed in `local_store.rs` (validate + render), 2 new round-trip tests. 7 new desktop tests, 4 new lib tests, all genuine RED→GREEN. **Lead independently re-ran**: full workspace (4284/4284, matches exactly) and desktop suite (211/211, matches exactly). Frontend cleared to wire the Gear tab against the real command/DTO shape. **QA finding, landed (backend, 2026-07-24) — silent corpus-resolution drops now traceable, shape B of QA's two proposed fixes.** QA root-caused the Spells tab inconsistency to something bigger than the Spells tab: the desktop app's only bundled `corpus` (`corpus_fixtures.rs`) is a deliberately tiny ~4-record demo fixture (its own doc comment: "not a general corpus provider, exhaustive corpus coverage is out of scope") — any real, disk-persisted `spells_selected`/`equipment_selections` entry outside those exact records silently vanished from every corpus-derived output (`school_coverage`, `equipped_items`, and now shape (c)'s `equipment_effects`) with zero diagnostic, indistinguishable from "nothing selected." This also capped shape (c)'s real-world value: its ACP/AC looked complete only because the Fighter fixed loadout happens to use exactly the 2 bundled equipment records. **Decision (backend, greenlit as an engineering-scope call, "your read" per the lead):** shape B (an honest "unresolved" signal) over shape A (bundle more records) — bundling more records doesn't fix the bug, it just moves the boundary; the app structurally cannot ship the full ~652-spell/hundreds-of-equipment-record corpus, so any fixed bundle size is permanently, arbitrarily incomplete. `CorpusDerivedSection` gained `unresolved_spell_ids`/`unresolved_equipment_item_ids: Vec<String>` (`pilot_compute_corpus.rs`), populated wherever `spell_id_resolve`/`equipment_id_resolve` returns `None` instead of the previous silent `continue`, surfaced on `CorpusDerivedDto` for the frontend to render as an honest "not shown — outside demo corpus" indicator (UI treatment is frontend's call, not built here). Genuine RED→GREEN: 3 new `pilot_compute_corpus.rs` tests (an unresolvable equipment selection tracked, an unresolvable spell tracked, everything-resolves leaves both lists genuinely empty), both push calls disabled to confirm the exact expected failures before restoring; 1 new end-to-end `character_hub.rs` test against the real bundled corpus (not a hand-built fixture) confirming a real `add_equipment_selection` for an item outside the demo bundle surfaces correctly — which also surfaced a real, pre-existing, unrelated fact worth noting: the fixed Fighter loadout's own `item:shield`/`power_attack` placeholder entries were already silently unresolvable before this fix (not new, not a bug this introduces, just now visible instead of invisible). 245/245 lib, 203/203 desktop. **Follow-on bug found and fixed (QA finding + backend fix, 2026-07-24) — `EquipmentEffectsDto`'s three `Option` fields never actually hid on absence.** `maxDexCap`/`spellFailureChance`/`attackBonusDelta` lacked `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` (unlike the precedented `damage_reduction` field in the same file), so a Rust `None` serialized as `"maxDexCap":null` — key present, literal `null`, not an omitted key — defeating the frontend's `!== undefined` hide-checks (`null !== undefined` is `true`) and rendering garbled `"+null"`/`"null%"` strings. QA confirmed three independent ways (a throwaway serialization test, tracing the zero-transform `invoke()` call, running the actual JS template logic in Node) before flagging; the one character live-tested earlier (Chain Shirt + exactly one weapon) happened to resolve `Some(...)` for all three fields, so the `None`/hide path was never exercised until now. **Fixed (backend)**: added the same `skip_serializing_if` attribute to all three fields. Genuine RED→GREEN: a new permanent wire-serialization test (`equipment_effects_dto_omits_its_optional_fields_when_none_and_includes_them_when_some`) reproduced the exact bug (`"maxDexCap":null` etc.) with the attribute temporarily removed, then confirmed fixed after restoring. Frontend's TS type already declared these fields as optional (`maxDexCap?: number`, not `| null`), so no frontend change was needed — the wire shape now matches what frontend was always coded to expect. 204/204 desktop, frontend typecheck clean. **Independently verified, both structural claims confirmed, not trusted (QA, 2026-07-24).** Confirmed the `EquippedActive`-only filter is genuinely load-bearing, not vacuous — reproduced RED by replacing the filter with a pass-through, watched a `SelectedInactive` item's real `-2` ACCHECK leak through the test, restored. Confirmed the new field is genuinely inert with respect to claim-gating from three independent angles: structurally (`base` is computed via the unmodified `compute_pilot_base_chassis` first, with zero lines of that function touched in the diff), by call-order (`create_character_at_root`'s `Blocked` early-return happens before `compute_pilot_with_corpus` is ever called, same shape as item 7's wealth gate), and empirically (the new desktop test asserts `Saved`, not `Blocked`, on a build that also carries a real nonzero ACP). Also confirmed `arms_armor.rs`'s `None`-vs-`Some(0)` semantic distinction is preserved correctly (no token vs. a real zero-value token). Ran clean throughout, RED/GREEN reproductions restored byte-identical each time.

open.title: Three writers, one checkout.
open.body: No worktrees by design; commit serialization (§2) mitigates git-index and cargo target-dir races but depends on teammate discipline. First symptom to watch: a "committed" change absent from `git log` on `tranche/6`. **New hazard found and self-caught (backend, 2026-07-24) — unscoped `cargo fmt -p codex` silently reformats all 516 tracked files.** Full account under item 1's sub-task-1 landing note above. Standing lesson for this checkout: `cargo fmt -p codex` (no path scoping) is unsafe right now — it would silently rewrite every teammate's files, including in-progress uncommitted work, since the crate has drifted from the currently-installed `rustfmt`'s formatting. A per-file `rustfmt <path>` is safe.

open.title: Latent data-quality defect — `Combat Expertise` is a duplicate key in the generated feat catalog (featmate, 2026-07-26, lead-verified).
open.body: A `uniq -d` sweep over the `key:` field of all 185 CRB feat records across `feat_data/{general,combat,metamagic,item_creation}.rs` returns exactly one duplicate: **"Combat Expertise" appears twice** in `feat_data/combat.rs` (lines 25 and 26), with different effect payloads. Root cause verified in the raw PCGen corpus, not inferred: `grep -c '^Combat Expertise\t' cr_feats.lst` returns **2** — a base record and a `TYPE=Base` Monk-flurry-aware variant — and the generator emitted each as its own `FeatTableEntry` under the same `key`. **Consequence:** any exact-match `key` lookup silently takes the first record and ignores the second; any "sum every effect for this key" logic would double-count. **Harmless today** — nothing in this codebase reads Combat Expertise — but it sits directly under the deferred activation-gated feat work (Combat Expertise / Deadly Aim / Arcane Strike), which would be the first consumer to trip it. **Deliberately not hand-patched:** `feat_data/*.rs` carries its own "Not hand-authored — do not hand-edit; regenerate if the corpus changes" discipline, so this is a generator-level fix belonging to whoever next touches the feat-data generator, not an inline edit. Recorded here rather than left in a scoping doc so it survives as a durable finding.

open.title: Named deferral — Leadership stays ungrounded despite carrying a computable formula (featmate, 2026-07-26, lead-ratified).
open.body: Leadership's corpus record does carry a genuinely computable magnitude: `BONUS:VAR|LeadershipScore|(TL+LeadershipAbilityScoreMod)` with `LeadershipAbilityScoreMod|CHA`, i.e. a Leadership score of total level + Charisma modifier, plus a cohort-level cap formula. Under the corrected standalone-grounding bar this would technically qualify as a real, verified, self-derived number. **Decision: defer the whole feat anyway.** The feat's actual substance is a cohort/follower subsystem this engine models nowhere; grounding the score alone would surface one number from an almost entirely unmodeled mechanic, which reads closer to overstating coverage than to the Poison Resistance / Bardic Knowledge precedent (where the grounded magnitude *is* the feature's whole mechanical content). Correctly belongs in the same category as the Familiar, Eidolon, and opponent-tracking subsystem questions, not in the cheap-standalone-fact vein. Logged as an explicit, named deferral rather than silently dropped, so a future pass does not re-derive it and reach a different conclusion by accident.

open.title: OPEN — Summoner (APG) is the one remaining class on the whole 27-class roster with no closure and no cheap path to one; held deliberately, not forgotten.
open.body: With Shaman's closure (item 37) landing, Summoner is now the ONLY class across CRB+APG+ACG with zero class-specific engine work beyond BAB/save/HP chassis dispatch. Scout's own sizing research (`docs/release/v0.6/summoner-eidolon-subsystem-sizing.md`) found the real blocker: nearly every Summoner feature of value (Life Link, Bond Senses, Shield Ally, Aspect, Maker's Call, Transposition, Merge Forms, Twin Eidolon, Gate) requires the unbuilt Eidolon — a full companion-creature subsystem (a leveled monster class, a base-form choice, and a 104-record evolution point-buy economy), not a flat self-scoped power the way Oracle's Mystery/Warpriest's Blessing/Shaman's Spirit were. The only Eidolon-independent fact is Summon Monster's own uses-per-day pool (`CHA+3`), which is thinner than any closure landed this segment (no self-scoped always-on power to pair it with). **Two real paths exist, sized but not chosen**: (a) a bounded single-base-form Eidolon MVP (fixed `AUTOMATIC` free evolutions, pool-size as a flat fact, chosen evolutions deferred) — estimated comparable in size to a single landed closure, at the larger end (Warpriest-ish); or (b) leave Summoner untouched until/unless the operator wants the full evolution point-buy economy funded as its own deliberate subsystem investment (meaningfully bigger than any closure landed this segment). **Operator input needed**: is the bounded Eidolon MVP (path a) worth building as Summoner's first real content, or does Summoner stay untouched for now? open.title: OPEN — the #23/#24 undercount bug is repo-wide, not Alchemist-only, and the true scale is far larger than task #24 or #25 as filed describe. Operator input needed before dispatching a fix.
open.body: Backend's #24 close flagged `alchemist_spell_list` as short 26 ACG-book records (121→147) and filed #25 as a single yes/no book-scope question ("should Alchemist also pull from ACG"). The lead independently re-derived every currently-shipped spell list against the real ingested corpus (`core_rulebook/cr_spells.lst` + `advanced_players_guide/apg_spells.lst` + `advanced_class_guide/acg_spells.lst`, correct token parse: split on `|`, then each group on `,`, membership-test) and found **all six CRB caster lists are short, several by more than half**: | Class | Shipped (home-book only) | True (CRB+APG+ACG union) | Missing | |---|---|---|---| | Cleric | 236 | 298 | 62 (26%) | | Sorcerer | 394 | 576 | 182 (46%) | | Bard | 164 | 264 | 100 (61%) | | Druid | 169 | 271 | 102 (60%) | | Paladin | 45 | 95 | 50 (111%) | | Ranger | 51 | 114 | 63 (124%) | | Alchemist | 121 (post-#24) | 147 | 26 (21%, this is exactly #25) | Witch (324) and Bloodrager (200) are already correct because #23/#24's fix already unions APG+ACG for those two. **The underlying rule is unambiguous, not a preference**: PF1 RAW defines a class's spell list as every spell whose own `CLASSES:` entry names that class, regardless of which sourcebook printed the spell — a Cleric can prepare an APG- or ACG-published cleric spell exactly as freely as a CRB one. The CRB-list modules' own doc comments explicitly scope to `cr_spells.lst` alone ("this table re-parses ... `core_rulebook/cr_spells.lst`"), which was a **methodology gap inherited from before this session's `CLASSES:` bug was even found**, not a deliberate design choice — nothing in the codebase argues for single-book scoping on purpose. **Ruling: #25's technical answer is "all ingested books," full stop; that part is not in question.** What IS an open, operator-level decision: whether to dispatch a corrective wave across all 6 CRB lists (plus Alchemist's remaining 26) now, mid-swarm, given (a) it reopens six already-"closed" spell tables with no report of defect until now, (b) two of the six lists are undercounting by more than 100%, meaning "already correct" claims made earlier this segment about CRB casters were wrong by a wide margin, and (c) the standing 2026-07-26 directive already pauses new class work pending a full reconciliation review — this discovery surfaced *during* that pause, and the question is whether a same-day corrective wave counts as reconciliation (in scope now) or as new work (waits for the review). Not dispatched to backend pending this call.

open.title: OPEN — Witch's real spellcasting shape is a third caster posture this codebase hasn't built yet, and building it as a Shaman-shaped prepared-from-list caster would be quietly wrong. Needs a scoping pass (dispatched to scout) before #11's remaining piece is built.
open.body: Backend stopped before building rather than mirror Shaman's own stage 2, and the lead independently re-verified the finding directly against the corpus before dispatching. `CLASS:Witch`'s own posture token is `SPELLSTAT:INT KNOWNSPELLS:LEVEL=0` — automatic knowledge of cantrips only, with no full `KNOWNSPELLS:LEVEL=0|1|...|9` ladder the way Cleric/Druid/Shaman all carry, and no `SPELLBOOK:YES` the way Wizard carries. This matches RAW exactly: a witch's spells above cantrip level are stored in and prepared from her familiar, not innately known and not spellbook-gated — a genuinely third shape, not a variant of either shape this codebase already builds. **A real factual error already sitting in shipped code, found in the process**: `src/pcgen_import/lst_parser/spellcasting_class.rs:22-26`'s own comment claims Witch carries "the same absent-signals prepared-casting shape as Cleric/Druid" — the lead independently confirmed this is wrong (the absent-signals half is right, the "same as" half isn't; Cleric/Druid's own KNOWNSPELLS ladder is present and full, Witch's is present but cantrip-only). Dispatched to backend as a one-line factual correction, not a design call. **Why this needed stopping rather than building**: mirroring Shaman's own stage 2 would ship a Witch who prepares any of her 326 spells directly with zero familiar involvement — mechanically a Cleric with an INT stat, would pass every test written against it, and would be wrong about the class's own defining mechanic. Exactly the no-stub-doctrine failure mode this segment has been naming plainly rather than shipping quietly. **What's already usable, independently confirmed by the lead**: the 326-spell list (task #33) is built and verified; Witch's `CAST:` table is byte-identical to Cleric's through all 20 levels including L11 (found by backend while investigating Shaman's own L11 divergence, a different question landing on the same table). **The open design question**: how to model "prepares from the familiar" when the familiar's own stat block doesn't exist yet (the Familiar subsystem's deferred Tier 2, task #11's original scoping). Two honest paths named, not yet chosen between: a familiar-as-spell-store mechanism (retargeting Wizard's own spellbook shape at the familiar instead of the character), or an explicitly-bounded MVP that grounds slots/DCs and leaves preparation itself blocked on the missing store. Worth noting this may be the first real product reason to build Familiar Tier 2 at all, which should factor into how that deferral gets sized going forward rather than treated as indefinitely low-priority. **RULED (lead, 2026-07-27) — scout's `witch-spellcasting-shape-design.md` landed same day, correcting item 57's own open question: no Familiar Tier 2 is needed after all.** Scout's central finding, independently re-verified by the lead directly against the corpus before ruling: `KEY:Witch ~ Familiar`'s own DESC states plainly "The familiar stores all the spells that you know" — but this repo's Wizard spellbook mechanism (`unmet_wizard_spellbook_conditions`/`ground_wizard_prepared_spellbook`, lead-confirmed directly in the code) was never a modeled container object in the first place — it's a semantic read of `input.chosen.spells_selected` filtered by `AcquisitionMode`, nothing more. A spell store is a set of spell identities; the familiar's own stat block (HD, saves, INT, skills) is irrelevant to storing them, the same "creature is not an input to the mechanic" shape the Studied-Target and Familiar-master-benefit passes already established. Witch is genuinely **Cleric-shaped at level 0, Wizard-shaped at levels 1-9** — a hybrid of two already-built shapes, not a third mechanism needing new architecture. **Three rulings, all confirming scout's own recommendation after independent verification**:
