open.title: OPERATOR RULING (Todd Hintzmann, 2026-07-29) — the Monk's hit die is
open.body: d8**, deliberately overriding the PCGen corpus's `HD:10`. The engine's `CLASS_META` corrected 10 -> 8; the corpus itself intentionally left unedited.** The shipped product was **contradicting itself**: the UI class picker (`apps/desktop/src/characterHub/characterHubModel.ts:444`) offered Monk as `hitDie: 8` while the Rust engine computed HP from a d10, so a Monk 20 at CON +2 *displayed* a d8 chassis but *computed* 164 HP where d8 gives 143. The disagreement had been found and honestly reported earlier (three separate "left as found and reported rather than silently changed" comments in the desktop model and its test) but never adjudicated, so both halves shipped disagreeing. **The corpus token contradicts its own cited source.** `cr_classes.lst:147` reads `CLASS:Monk  HD:10  ... SOURCEPAGE:p.56`, and published PF1 Core Rulebook p.56 — the exact page that record itself cites — gives the Monk a d8. That is an internal contradiction of the same kind item 50 (Swashbuckler's `SwashbucklerDeedQualifyLVL` set from `MagusLVL` while its correctly-authored sibling `SwashbucklerDeedsLVL` was set from `SwashbucklerLVL`) and item 69 (Skald's Raging Song, where Bard's structurally identical sibling token revealed the missing `-2` offset) established as the bar for deviating from a literal corpus token — and expressly NOT the item 56 Shaman shape, where a class merely differed from its peers on one cell with nothing contradicting it internally. Here the record disagrees with the page it points at. The operator ruled directly on the merits regardless. **The corpus was NOT edited, on purpose, and this is the load-bearing part of the ruling.** `/home/ubuntu/workspace/repos/pcgen` is a clean clone of upstream and is this project's **independent parity oracle** (`src/oracle_validation/pcgen_runner.rs`, `comparator.rs`). Editing it to agree with us would (a) be lost on the next upstream pull and (b) destroy the independence that makes parity testing worth anything — making oracle and engine agree by construction. That is precisely the failure mode item 89 documented, where PCGen's own export omitted the same -4 nonproficiency penalty our engine omitted, so both agreed while both were wrong and a 4-point melee error survived a week. The fix therefore lives in our engine as a **documented corpus-defect override**, exactly the shape item 50 mandated ("the deviation must carry an explicit code comment recording the corpus defect and this ruling, so it reads as a deliberate, documented fix rather than an unexplained departure"). **Sites changed** (the value propagates from exactly one place, but three surfaces asserted it): `src/rules_core/rules_tables/crb/class_tables.rs` — the Monk `CLASS_META` row, now `hit_die: 8` behind a comment block naming the corpus token, the contradicted SOURCEPAGE, the operator and date, this item, and an explicit "DO NOT correct this back to 10"; the `hit_die` field's own doc comment, which previously claimed every row transcribes its `HD:` token, now names the one row that deliberately does not. `src/rules_core/durability.rs`'s inline `compute_max_hp_now_resolves_monk_the_last_class_to_join_table_class_id` (12 -> 10) and `tests/v06_durability.rs`'s `compute_max_hp_now_resolves_monk_since_table_class_id_recognizes_it` (13 -> 11), both with their doc comments rewritten to cite the ruling rather than the corpus. **No test was weakened** — expectations were corrected to the newly-correct values and two new tests were added pinning Monk HP at levels 1/10/20 (10 / 73 / 143 at CON +2) plus a companion asserting the d10 values (12 / 84 / 164) are specifically NOT produced, the same both-sides pinning shape item 56's `shaman_level_11_follows_the_corpus_not_the_peer_row` uses, so a regression that changed the die and the formula in compensating directions still fails. **No TypeScript value changed** — the desktop table was already `8` and was already right; the engine moved to meet it. The three stale "we deliberately left this disagreeing" comments were rewritten to record the resolution instead. **Parity harness: no Monk case exists, so nothing was adjusted and nothing is hidden.** The full set of oracle case ids is Human Fighter 1/2/8/10, Human Wizard 1, Human Paladin 1; the golden fixture is Human Fighter 1 only; `src/oracle_validation/` contains zero occurrences of "monk". `durability.max_hp` **is** a real compared parity dimension (`selected_parity_dimensions.rs:184-185`, asserted at 12 for Fighter 1 and 8 for Wizard 1), so if a Monk case is ever added it **will legitimately disagree with the oracle by the full d10-vs-d8 delta** — 2 HP at level 1, 21 at level 20. That expected mismatch must be declared explicitly in the case, naming this corpus defect, the way item 89's nonproficiency fix named the export defect rather than quietly tuning an expected value to match. Recorded here so whoever adds that case does not read the disagreement as a regression.
open.call_text: The operator ruled directly on the merits regardless.

resolved.title: RESOLVED — "durability" definition (§1 item 4).
resolved.body: QA flagged that the alpha bar's calculation list ("... AC, durability, carry capacity ...") is ambiguous between character survivability and item hardness/breakage; the codebase has no item-hardness/breakage mechanic anywhere. Ruling (lead, 2026-07-23): **durability = the character's displayed survivability stat — max/current HP, temporary HP, nonlethal damage tracking, and unconscious/dying/death thresholds** — distinct from "level-up hit points" (§1 item 4's separate entry), which is specifically the hit-die + Con-mod increment calculated during the level-up flow. This keeps the bar scoped to character-sheet mechanics already in the codebase's model and introduces no new game system. QA may proceed writing red-green tests against this definition. Follow-up (QA, same day): durability has almost no production surface either — only an isolated level-1 fighter HP value, no aggregate max/current/temp HP or dying-death fields anywhere — so this is a real wave-2 build item, not just a naming clarification. **Backend build landed, frontend never followed (backend's DTO-consumption sweep, 2026-07-24): full command/DTO shapes for whoever wires the UI, so this can be picked up cold.** - **`load_character_durability`** — request `{ characterId: string }` → `Result<CharacterDurabilityDto, string>`. Errs (not a `Blocked`-style payload, a rejected IPC call) when the saved build isn't single-class Fighter/Wizard/Rogue at a level `durability::compute_max_hp` recognizes — same scoping restriction the compute layer already has elsewhere, not new. A Durability tab needs to handle this the same way other tabs handle an unsupported-class build (a "not available for this build" fallback), not treat it as an unexpected failure. - **`adjust_character_hp`** — request `{ characterId: string, deltaHp?: number, deltaNonlethal?: number }` (both default 0) → same `CharacterDurabilityDto`, recomputed. **This is already atomic and delta-based, not two calls needing client-side coordination** — unlike the money/equipment-purchase coupling this doc flagged earlier, there's no read-then-compute-then-write race to design around: send `deltaHp: -8` to deal 8 lethal damage, `deltaNonlethal: +5` to add 5 nonlethal, and the server clamps (`current_hp` capped at `max_hp` on healing, `nonlethal_damage` floored at 0 on recovery) and reclassifies `status` in the same call. A "type an absolute new HP value" input just needs `deltaHp = newValue - currentHp` computed client-side before the one call — still one round trip, not two. - **`CharacterDurabilityDto`'s 4 fields, in PF1 terms**: `maxHp` — the character's ceiling, computed fresh from class hit die + Con modifier each load, never stored. `currentHp` — the live tracked value, persisted in a `hp.json` sidecar, defaults to `maxHp` the first time a character is loaded (no special "initialize" call needed). `nonlethalDamage` — PF1's separate nonlethal pool, persisted alongside `currentHp`; `currentHp` itself is never reduced by nonlethal damage. `status` — a pre-computed label, one of `Normal` / `Staggered` (`nonlethalDamage == currentHp`) / `Disabled` (`currentHp == 0`) / `Unconscious` (`nonlethalDamage > currentHp`) / `Dying` (`currentHp < 0`) / `Dead` (`currentHp <= -constitutionScore`) — a minimal UI can render this string directly (e.g. as a badge/color) rather than re-deriving thresholds client-side. - **What doesn't exist yet, flagged so it isn't assumed**: no temporary HP field (already noted above as explicitly out of scope for this wave); no dedicated "heal to full"/"stabilize" convenience call (achievable client-side as `deltaHp: maxHp - currentHp`, just not a named single-purpose command); no death-save/stabilization mechanic beyond the `Dying`/`Dead` labels themselves (labels only, no dice-roll flow) — consistent with the alpha bar not naming that affordance. - **Net for whoever builds this**: the backend side is a clean, already-atomic read/write pair with no coupling hazard to design around — the missing piece is purely a new HP display + a damage/heal input calling `adjust_character_hp`, no new backend work anticipated for a minimal version. **Status thresholds verified against real PF1 rules, not just internal consistency (backend, 2026-07-24).** `classify_durability`'s exact formula (`durability.rs:99-113`) checked against the real d20/PF1 "Injury and Death" and "Nonlethal Damage" rules: Dead (`current_hp <= -constitution_score`, correctly the Constitution *score* not modifier), Dying (`current_hp < 0`), Disabled (`current_hp == 0`), Unconscious (`nonlethal_damage > current_hp`), Staggered (`nonlethal_damage == current_hp`), Normal (fallthrough) — all 6 match. One precedence question confirmed deliberate: at `current_hp == 0` with `nonlethal_damage == 0`, Disabled and Staggered are both literally true, but the `if/else if` order checks Disabled first — correct, matches the real ruling that 0-hp-Disabled is the more specific controlling rule. **Sourcing caveat stated plainly**: no local PCGen corpus source contains this rule text (checked; PCGen's data only references these conditions as effects *caused by* specific abilities, not the core rules defining the thresholds) — verified against the well-established, unchanged-since-3.5e d20 SRD Open Game Content text instead, same sourcing category as `money.rs`'s already-flagged pp/gp/sp/cp ratio. Clean result, no mismatch — safe for frontend to render these labels as ground truth. **Backend half landed, frontend half never started (backend, 2026-07-24, DTO-consumption sweep).** `CharacterDurabilityDto` (`maxHp`/`currentHp`/`nonlethalDamage`/`status`) and its two Tauri commands (`load_character_durability`, `adjust_character_hp`) are real, registered, computed, and fully tested backend-side — but frontend has zero `invoke()` calls for either command and zero components/tabs mentioning "durability" anywhere (case-insensitive grep, zero hits). `CreateCharacterForm.tsx`'s own `maxHp` is a separately-computed client-side local value, not a read of the backend DTO. Matches the untracked/unattributed `SWARM_TASKS.md`'s durability row still showing "queued" (that file's overall claims are not trusted, per the earlier flag, but this one line happens to be independently confirmed true). This is real remaining bar-item-4 distance: not an architecture gap, a genuine missing UI surface (HP/dying-death display, damage tracking) — bounded, frontend-shaped work whenever dispatched. **RESOLVED — frontend built the Durability/HP tab (`75b083bd`).** New `characterDurability.ts` boundary wraps both commands exactly per the scoping above; `CharacterSheet.tsx` gained durability state, a loader effect (mirrors the money pattern), `handleAdjustHp`, and a new `DurabilityPanel` inside the Defense tab — current/max HP, nonlethal damage, an emphasized status badge when not `Normal`, and Damage/Heal buttons styled like `MoneyPanel`'s Add/Spend. Falls back to an honest "not available for this build" line when durability is `null` (covers both in-flight loading and a genuinely unsupported build, same treatment as other unreachable-build cases). **Live-verified against the real dev build, both directions**: a supported Dwarf Rogue 2 went 19/19 → damaged to 12/19 (disk-confirmed) → healed to 15/19 → damaged into negative HP, status correctly flipped to "Dying" and rendered emphasized, then healed back to exactly 19 (clamped at max, no overshoot). An unsupported Wizard/Rogue multiclass correctly showed the fallback line, no crash, and confirmed no stray `hp.json` was written for it. No new test file (UI-only, no new pure logic beyond what the live drive already covered); 63/63 existing suite still green, typecheck clean.

resolved.title: RESOLVED — damage reduction exposed through the DTO, and now actually rendered.
resolved.body: Landed (`f7ce289d`): `pilot_compute.rs`'s existing per-class DR explanations are now exposed through the DTO layer. **Frontend follow-through landed (`26ac0704`)**: the Defense tab (previously the literal "coming soon" stub) now renders "Damage Reduction: X/—" when present, added `damageReduction` to the shared `PilotSnapshotDto` TS type (was entirely missing there too — the DTO-consumption sweep that found this gap was right). Absent case live-verified honestly across all 3 chassis-supported classes (Fighter/Wizard/Rogue, including a multiclass) — `undefined`, not a fabricated zero, correct stub text still shown. Populated case **cannot** currently be live-verified: Barbarian is the only DR-granting class and it's `human-diagnostics-only` (always `Blocked`), so no live UI path today ever produces a saved character with a real non-zero value — a structural fact, not a testing gap, noted in the code rather than glossed over. One honest note left in-code at the time, initially unfixed: the "Recompute" action's own DTO didn't carry `damageReduction`, so it wouldn't have refreshed if a real value ever became reachable later — **closed the same day, see the `af2d8b9f` entry immediately below**, not left standing. Not part of the alpha bar's explicit calc list (item 4 doesn't name DR), but a real completeness improvement landed opportunistically, now genuinely end-to-end. **Recompute-DTO parity gap closed (backend, `af2d8b9f`).** Found the DTO under its real Rust name (`CharacterSnapshotDto` in `recomputeCharacter.rs`, backing `recompute_character`) and added `damage_reduction: Option<i16>` with the identical serde shape `PilotSnapshotDto` already uses, populated from the same source field (`PilotDefenseViewModel::damage_reduction`) at the one construction site. Since no live pipeline can exercise a real non-`None` value (Barbarian never reaches `Computed`, same structural fact as above), added the meaningful test that *is* available instead: a direct serialization test proving `Some(3)` emits the camelCase `"damageReduction"` key and `None` omits it entirely (not `null`), plus a golden-path assertion that the existing Fighter fixture correctly stays `None` — same wire-shape rigor as the earlier `corpusDerived` regression tests, without needing a real compute pass to get it. 2 new tests, full suite green, zero blast radius. **Independently re-verified, not just self-reported (QA, 2026-07-24).** Read the actual diff and code rather than trusting the commit message: (1) confirmed `damageReduction?: number` is genuinely on the shared `PilotSnapshotDto` interface every consumer imports, not used ad-hoc; (2) read `DefenseTab`'s JSX directly — `!== undefined` guards the rendered line, falling through to the stub text on absence, with `snapshot?.damageReduction` correctly propagating `undefined` all the way from a `Blocked`/`None` snapshot; (3) traced Barbarian's unreachability in the compute layer itself rather than trusting the claim — `table_class_id` (used by both the single-class dispatch and `is_supported_multiclass_mix`'s per-class check) has no Barbarian entry, so no single-class or multiclass Barbarian-containing build can produce anything but `class_chassis.unsupported` → `Blocked` → `snapshot: None`. All three claims hold completely. Clean, independently confirmed record.

resolved.title: RESOLVED (2026-07-24) — starting wealth by class, operator-provided with citation.
resolved.body: Was: exhaustively searched and correctly left unresolved (QA/backend found no citable value in any local corpus source, correctly declined the file-shape-stub trap in `docs/release/SD-22/artifacts/corpus/{acg,apg}/class_*.lst.md`, correctly declined to implement from unverified memory) — a genuine content-provenance/licensing question, not an engineering call, deliberately kept out of the autonomous-operation decision set. **Operator (Todd Hintzmann) provided the full table directly, sourced from d20pfsrd.com's "Character Creation" page** (`https://www.d20pfsrd.com/basics-ability-scores/character-creation/`, Pathfinder SRD / OGL content): | Class | Starting Wealth | Average | |---|---|---| | Alchemist | 3d6 × 10 gp | 105 gp | | Barbarian | 3d6 × 10 gp | 105 gp | | Bard | 3d6 × 10 gp | 105 gp | | Cavalier | 5d6 × 10 gp | 175 gp | | Cleric | 4d6 × 10 gp | 140 gp | | Druid | 2d6 × 10 gp | 70 gp | | Fighter | 5d6 × 10 gp | 175 gp | | Gunslinger | 5d6 × 10 gp | 175 gp | | Inquisitor | 4d6 × 10 gp | 140 gp | | Magus | 4d6 × 10 gp | 140 gp | | Monk | 1d6 × 10 gp | 35 gp | | Ninja | 4d6 × 10 gp | 140 gp | | Oracle | 3d6 × 10 gp | 105 gp | | Paladin | 5d6 × 10 gp | 175 gp | | Ranger | 5d6 × 10 gp | 175 gp | | Rogue | 4d6 × 10 gp | 140 gp | | Samurai | 3d6 × 10 gp | 105 gp | | Sorcerer | 2d6 × 10 gp | 70 gp | | Summoner | 2d6 × 10 gp | 70 gp | | Witch | 3d6 × 10 gp | 105 gp | | Wizard | 2d6 × 10 gp | 70 gp | Plus the companion **Character Wealth by Level** table (for characters created above 1st level — PC level 2 through 20, 1,000 gp through 880,000 gp), same source. Worth noting: the Alchemist value (3d6×10) exactly matches what the earlier file-shape stub in `docs/release/SD-22/artifacts/corpus/apg/class_alchemist.lst.md` showed — that stub's *value* was apparently correct, it was the *provenance* (an unlicensed placeholder file, not a real source) that made it unusable at the time; this operator-cited value is independently sourced and now usable. **Implemented (backend, 2026-07-24).** `money::starting_wealth_gp` (`src/rules_core/money.rs`) returns the operator-cited average gp value for any of the 11 PF1 Core Rulebook classes `ClassId` models (all 11 rows populated, not just Fighter/Wizard/Rogue — mirrors `class_tables()`'s own "complete table, narrower dispatch" precedent, since a class outside the 3 that currently reach `Computed` never reaches the wealth-granting code path anyway). The 12 non-CRB classes in the operator's table (Alchemist, Cavalier, Gunslinger, Inquisitor, Magus, Ninja, Oracle, Samurai, Summoner, Witch) are deliberately omitted — no `class:<name>` id for any of them is recognized anywhere in this crate yet, so their rows would be inert data with nothing to key against. **Deterministic by design, not a rolled value**: PF1's own rule is to roll the die (e.g. Fighter 5d6×10), but this crate has no random-number generator anywhere and is deterministic throughout (every computed value is exactly reproducible from its inputs) — rolling would be a genuine architecture departure, not a drop-in fix. Uses the operator's own printed "Average" column directly (a citation, not a re-derived computation); a future "reroll" UI affordance, if ever wanted, is a separate frontend feature layered on top of this default. `create_character` (refactored into a testable `create_character_at_root` split, mirroring every other mutation command's own `_at_root` precedent) now initializes the new character's `money.json` balance via the existing `adjust_character_money_at_root` sidecar mechanism (item 9's own infrastructure, reused rather than duplicated) immediately after the build reaches `Computed` and saves — atomic with creation, no separate call for the caller to remember. A `Blocked` build is granted no wealth, fabricated or otherwise (verified by test). 3 new desktop-crate tests (Fighter/Wizard/Rogue's distinct correct balances, and a Blocked-build zero-grant proof) plus 5 new lib-crate tests on `starting_wealth_gp` itself (the 3 reachable classes, the other 8 CRB classes, an independent dice-count×35 arithmetic cross-check, and unrecognized-class `None` handling). Genuine RED→GREEN: the wealth-granting call was temporarily disabled, the two positive tests failed with the exact expected 0-vs-17500/7000 mismatch, then restored and confirmed green. 228/228 lib, 200/200 desktop. **OPERATOR DECISION (Todd Hintzmann, 2026-07-24) — go ahead on the 12 (currently: 10 named) non-CRB classes, d20pfsrd.com re-confirmed as an approved reference source.** Explicit go-ahead given directly, in response to a dashboard status question about blocked items. **Count discrepancy to reconcile before implementing**: this doc's own transcription above names exactly 10 non-CRB classes (Alchemist, Cavalier, Gunslinger, Inquisitor, Magus, Ninja, Oracle, Samurai, Summoner, Witch), but both this entry's own prose and `SWARM_TASKS.md` say "12" — backend should re-check the original d20pfsrd table (`https://www.d20pfsrd.com/basics-ability-scores/character-creation/`) directly to confirm the real count and catch any missed row before building, not assume either number is right. **Scope, once reconciled**: unlike the class-breadth item below, this does NOT require a full rules-engine chassis (BAB/saves/HP/skills/spells) per class — starting wealth is level-independent, flat data. Needs: (1) a recognized `class:<name>` id for each new class (extending whatever id space `ClassId`/`class_tables()` uses, even if the class has no other engine support yet — same "recognized but narrow" shape `class_tables()` already established), (2) a `starting_wealth_gp` table entry per class using the already-transcribed Average column, (3) confirm the wealth-granting path handles a recognized-but-otherwise-`Blocked` class correctly (a class with no working chassis will never reach `Computed` regardless, so no wealth grant risk — verify this explicitly rather than assume it). Bounded, real work; queued for backend after sub-task 5. **Count reconciled (backend, 2026-07-24) — the real count is 10, not 12; "12" was a prose typo, not a sign of missing rows.** Fetched the live d20pfsrd "Character Creation" page directly rather than trusting either number: its "Starting Character Wealth" table lists exactly 21 classes total. Cross-checked every single row (id + average gp) against this doc's own already-transcribed table programmatically — zero mismatches, zero missing classes. 21 = the 11 CRB classes already implemented + the 10 non-CRB classes already named here (Alchemist, Cavalier, Gunslinger, Inquisitor, Magus, Ninja, Oracle, Samurai, Summoner, Witch). No twelfth or thirteenth class exists on the real source. **Implemented (backend, 2026-07-24).** `money::starting_wealth_gp` now also recognizes the 10 non-CRB class ids (e.g. `"class:alchemist"`), each mapped to its real d20pfsrd average. None of the 10 has a `class_tables()` row or a `compute_class_chassis` dispatch arm — recognized only by this one function, the "recognized but narrow" shape, same as `class_tables()`'s own precedent of carrying rows a `Computed` build might never reach. **Verified explicitly, not assumed**: a new desktop-crate test creates a Human Alchemist level 1 and confirms it still reaches `Blocked` (no chassis dispatch exists for that class id) with zero wealth granted — proving the new recognition carries no risk of ever granting wealth to an unproven build. 2 new lib tests (all 10 real averages, including an independent dice-count arithmetic cross-check folded into the existing check) + 1 new desktop test. 276/276 lib, 212/212 desktop.

Closes the gap flagged against frontend's `59d5bc0` money panel — buying a weapon/armor now actually spends money. **Independently verified, static leg clean, live-UI leg inconclusive on an environment quirk (QA, 2026-07-24).** Confirmed `characterMoney.ts`'s `gpToCopper` (`Math.round(valueInGp * 100)`) mirrors `money.rs`'s `gp_to_copper` exactly (same `COPPER_PER_GOLD = 100` ratio, same rounding), and the boundary wiring (`loadCharacterMoney`/`adjustCharacterMoney`) correctly calls the matching Rust commands. Called clean on the strength of the static verification (exact formula match, direct source read of the wiring) rather than blocked; live-UI leg left inconclusive, not failed. 9a. **RESOLVED.** Backend field landed (`034d1b84`); frontend consumption landed separately (`d5db4321`, `perf(spells): use the cheaper addSpellSelection once a Wizard has 1+ spells`) — found stale during a routine idle-teammate check (2026-07-25), lead confirmed directly in `CharacterSheet.tsx`'s `handleAddSpell`: `existingSpells` is read from `props.detail?.spellsSelected`, fed through `resolveSpellRouting`, which picks the cheap `addSpellSelection` path once the character already has ≥1 spell and only uses the atomic bootstrap command for the genuine first-spell case. resolved.title: RESOLVED, LIVE-VERIFIED (2026-07-23) — Wizard is a genuinely playable second class now.
resolved.body: Frontend live-tested backend's Wizard fix (3484b5d) and found two further, independent gaps underneath it: - **RESOLVED — level-up path gap.** `apply_level_up` seeded zero choices for any class — only `compose_character_input` (character creation) was touched by 3484b5d, so multiclassing Wizard onto an existing character still hit the OLD diagnostic. Fixed in `1aabdf8`: seeds the same canonical choices in the new-class-entry branch only, guaranteed to fire exactly once per character (verified with a dedicated test — `wizard_has_canonical_specialization_selections` requires exactly 2 opposed-school entries, so a re-seed on a later level-up would break it, and doesn't). - **RESOLVED — bootstrap deadlock (the real bottleneck).** `create_character` only ever persists a proven-`Computed` build, so a fresh Wizard (empty spellbook) could never be saved in the first place. The Add Spell picker couldn't bootstrap around this either: `unmet_wizard_spellbook_conditions` requires one spell recorded as **both** `AcquisitionMode::Known` and `AcquisitionMode::Prepared`, but `add_spell_selection` only sets one mode per call, and `mutate_saved_character_at_root` discards (never persists) any call that doesn't independently reach `Computed` — so a Known-only call was discarded, a Prepared-only call was discarded, neither built toward the other. Backend's own earlier passing test only reached `Computed` by constructing `CharacterInput` directly in Rust, bypassing the command layer — real proof the compute logic was correct, not proof the UI could produce this state. **Root cause confirmed + fix landed for the second-call problem (backend, 2026-07-23).** Backend independently re-derived the same root cause before reading the framing above (verification, not agreement-seeking) and confirmed the scope precisely: purely a bootstrap/chicken-and-egg problem for the *first* spell — once a character has ≥1 Known and ≥1 Prepared entry, subsequent single-mode `add_spell_selection` calls already work fine, so `add_spell_selection` itself needed no redesign. Landed as `record_and_prepare_spell_selection` (`6e12437`) — a new Tauri command whose mutation closure pushes both a Known and a Prepared `SpellSelection` entry (same spell) in one `mutate_saved_character_at_root` call, atomically satisfying both conditions on the first call, same additive-command shape as every other `add_*_selection` command, no changes to `add_spell_selection` or the never-persist-unproven invariant. Scoped Wizard-only, shape generalizes without rework if another prepared caster gets a similar gate later. **This command is real and correct** — it just turned out not to be sufficient on its own; see the next sub-item. - **STILL OPEN, discovered after the above landed — a character holding a Wizard class level can never get saved in the first place.** Frontend live-tested `record_and_prepare_spell_selection` against a real build and found it still `Blocked`, on the new-and-correct "no wizard spells recorded/prepared" diagnostic (confirming 3484b5d's school-choice fix genuinely works) — never persisted, both via fresh creation and via leveling an existing character into Wizard as a third class. Read `record_and_prepare_spell_selection_at_root` directly: like every mutation command, it operates via load-existing-saved-character → mutate → recompute → save-if-`Computed`. It **requires a character that is already saved while holding a Wizard class level**. But `create_character` and `apply_level_up` both discard (never persist) a build that isn't independently `Computed`, and "Wizard class level + zero spells" is never `Computed` — so nothing in the current command surface can ever produce that starting state. This is a distinct, one-level-deeper chicken-and-egg from the one already fixed: class-acquisition and first-spell-acquisition are each independently gated, and neither can happen before the other. Backend's own earlier passing test proves the compute layer can represent this state (it saves a `SavedCharacterEnvelope` directly via `SavedCharacterStore::save`, bypassing the `Computed` gate — a test-only shortcut, not something the UI can do) — same "compute-correct vs. UI-reachable" distinction that's recurred at every layer of this investigation. Plausible direction floated to backend (not mandated): have class-acquisition itself (`compose_character_input` for creation, and `apply_level_up`'s new-class-entry branch) atomically seed one canonical starter spell as both Known and Prepared in the same mutation that adds the class level and school choices — mirrors the exact pattern already used for the school-specialization seeding. Backend investigating and proposing before any code, same diligence as every prior layer. **Net effect, unchanged from before this whole sub-thread**: bar item 3's "select spells at each spell-gaining level" remains untestable for Wizard. Frontend's UI routing change (Wizard spell picks always via `record_and_prepare_spell_selection`) is still correct, necessary work and was committed regardless — it's just not sufficient by itself. - **Minor, not urgent** — `apply_record_and_prepare_spell_selection` doesn't validate `source_class_id` against classes the character actually holds. Not a real discoverable tester workflow either way (flagged by frontend as a test-fixture curiosity only, explicitly not recommended as something to build UI around). Backend's call whether to fold into whatever it builds next or leave as backlog. - **RESOLVED, live-verified (backend `b2a5eb6`, frontend verification 2026-07-23).** `compose_character_input` and `apply_level_up`'s new-class-entry branch now both seed one canonical starter spell (`evocation.0.light`, Known+Prepared, reusing an already-proven-safe spell_id rather than a new literal) alongside the school-specialization choices — verified against `unmet_wizard_spellbook_conditions`'s own budget math (1 consumed vs. 3 available cantrips, comfortably under budget at every supported level 1–3) and confirmed not to touch the separate `WIZARD_SPELLBOOK_SUPPORTED_MAX_LEVEL=3` ceiling. Both existing deadlock-reproduction tests rewritten (not deleted) to explicitly clear `spells_selected` first, turned into standing regression guards for the mechanism; 3 new tests prove the actual fix. 187/187 desktop suite. **Live verification (frontend, full walkthrough with `b2a5eb6` pulled):** created "Elara Spellweaver" (Human Wizard) — creation form reported "computed and saved" for the first time in this investigation. Loaded the real sheet: Wizard 1, HP 8/8, a real Progression rail (Arcane bond/school/Cantrips/Scribe Scroll/Spells-per-day/Spellbook). Used the real Add Spell picker twice — Magic Missile (Evocation, rev.1→rev.2), then Alarm (Abjuration, rev.2→rev.3), both genuinely persisted. This closes the entire three-layer bootstrap investigation: class acquisition (`3484b5d`/`1aabdf8`), then first-spell bootstrap (`b2a5eb6`), all confirmed with real UI-driven persistence, not just compute-layer proof. **This is the first point in the swarm where a second class (Wizard, alongside Fighter) is genuinely creatable/loadable/level-up-able end-to-end through the shipped UI** — the "second class reaches Computed" claim struck twice earlier in this doc is now actually true for class acquisition and the first spell. **CORRECTION (see item 13): the "slot math summed to exactly 2/2, honestly enforced" claim originally recorded here was wrong** — it was a coincidence of the UI's own client-side arithmetic, not server-side enforcement; the actual budget check never runs against real spells at all, see below. **RESOLVED (2026-07-24) — render-staleness bug.** Right after a spell-add mutation, the Spells tab's corpus-derived reachability list briefly still showed "No corpus-reachable spells selected yet" even though the mutation succeeded — closing and reopening the character showed it correctly. Not Wizard-specific: same shared mutation pipeline every Add Weapon/Add Armor/Add Spell action uses. Root cause: `character_hub.rs`'s `CreateCharacterResponse::Saved` variant has `#[serde(tag = "kind")]` with no `rename_all`, so `corpus_derived` serialized literally as `"corpus_derived"` on the wire while the TS boundary's asserted-not-validated type declared `corpusDerived` — silently `undefined` at runtime. `summary`/`snapshot`/`diagnostics` all happen to have no underscores, which is exactly why every other post-mutation update looked correct and only corpus-derived data looked stale. **Fixed (backend, `498679d1`) with the correct targeted approach, avoiding the tag-renaming trap**: a per-field `#[serde(rename = "corpusDerived")]` on just the one field with an underscore, not an enum-wide attribute. Backend also caught and fixed an identical latent bug it had introduced earlier the same session in `PurchaseEquipmentResponse` (same pattern, before this bug class was known) before it became a second incident, and proactively swept the rest of the desktop crate's `#[serde(tag = ...)]` enums — none of the others needed a change (already `kebab-case` by deliberate design, or no underscored fields). **Genuine RED→GREEN**: 2 new tests serialize a real response with `serde_json` and assert on the actual JSON keys directly — the only test shape that can catch this bug class, since a test on Rust struct field values alone is blind to it. Backend reverted the fix, watched both tests fail with the exact snake_case symptom, then restored and confirmed green. 196/196 desktop suite. **Independently re-verified end to end, not just the diff (QA, completeness sweep, 2026-07-24).** Ran the 2 tests directly (pass). Reproduced RED themselves — removed the `#[serde(rename = "corpusDerived")]` attribute, reran, watched the exact reported symptom (literal snake_case `corpus_derived` while every other field stayed correctly camelCase, the `"Saved"` tag untouched) — restored, confirmed GREEN again. Confirmed the TS side genuinely expects `corpusDerived` (`loadCreateCharacter.ts:102`), closing the loop end to end. Independently checked the "swept the rest of the crate" claim rather than trusting it: grepped for every `#[serde(tag = ...)]` enum in the crate — exactly 4 exist, the 2 already fixed plus `Ge08BaselineArmorClass` (no underscored fields, genuinely unaffected) and `IssueUrlError` (uniform `kebab-case`, its own doc comment confirms the React consumer matches kebab-case throughout, not a camelCase boundary — also genuinely unaffected). Clean, fully independently confirmed.

resolved.title: RESOLVED, LIVE-VERIFIED (2026-07-23) — Wizard spell-slot budget enforcement never applied to any real spell.
resolved.body: Found by frontend while investigating item 10's cosmetic render-staleness finding, then verified live rather than left as a code-reading suspicion. Root cause in `pilot_compute.rs`'s `parse_wizard_spellbook_spell_id`: it expects the bespoke `<school>.<level>.<name>` format (matching the one seeded starter spell, `evocation.0.light`), but real corpus spell keys ("Magic Missile", "Alarm", "Grease") contain no dots at all — `spell_id.splitn(3, '.')` yields one segment, `level_token = parts.next()?` returns `None`, and the function returns `None` for every real spell. `unmet_wizard_spellbook_conditions`'s slot-consumption loop uses `.filter_map(parse_wizard_spellbook_spell_id)` to build the `consumed` sum, so every real-catalog spell is silently dropped before the over-budget check ever runs — the check can mathematically never fire against real spells, only the one bespoke-format seed spell is ever counted. **This means item 10's earlier "slot math summed to exactly 2/2, honestly enforced" observation was a coincidence of the UI's own client-side arithmetic (the picker showing "N of 2" locally), not a server-verified budget — corrected above.** Verified live: a Wizard at a 2-slot budget added two real spells (looked correct at "2/2" in the UI), then a third 1st-level spell (Grease) — expected `Blocked`, got silent acceptance and persistence (`rev.3`→`rev.4`, confirmed on disk). A Wizard can add unlimited real spells today with zero slot enforcement. Directly relevant to alpha bar item 4 ("spell slot allocation... matches PCGen") — this is a real gap, not cosmetic, and more significant than the render-staleness issue that led to finding it. Frontend correctly did not propose a fix (real ambiguity in the right repair shape — resolve real `spell_id`s against actual school/level data via the corpus, widen the parser, or something else backend would judge better — and it's backend's file). **Fix landed (backend, `365b3a1a`).** Confirmed this was NOT the same headless/corpus-aware architecture wall as AC/encumbrance — the real spell catalog (`SPELL_LIST`, 652 CRB records) is a plain `pub const` compiled directly into the binary, already headless-accessible with zero corpus threading, unlike equipment. `parse_wizard_spellbook_spell_id` now resolves real `SPELL_LIST` keys directly first, falling back to the old synthetic convention for zero blast radius on QA's 3 existing fixture files. `WIZARD_STARTER_SPELL_ID` upgraded from the synthetic placeholder to the real key `"Light"`, since real resolution now exists. **Genuine RED→GREEN verification, not just claimed**: backend temporarily disabled the fix, reran the new regression test, watched it fail with Grease silently accepted exactly as frontend reported, then restored the fix and confirmed it passes. New test reproduces frontend's exact scenario through the real command surface (not a parser-only unit test): Magic Missile + Alarm accepted at 2/2, Grease as a third prepared spell correctly `Blocked`, not persisted. 188/188 desktop, 197/197 lib. **Live re-verification (frontend, 2026-07-23).** Built a fresh Wizard ("Verify Slotbudget") rather than reuse the earlier "Elara Spellweaver" save, whose disk state still carries the pre-fix Grease artifact as stale data, not a live bug. Through the real Add Spell UI (full 652-spell catalog): Magic Missile accepted (rev.2, disk-confirmed) → Alarm accepted (rev.3, disk-confirmed, 2/2 real slots) → Grease as a third spell honestly `Blocked` with a real diagnostic ("spell level 1 over-prepared: 3 slots consumed... but only 2 available"), revision stayed at rev.3, no Grease entry on disk — mutation discarded, not silently persisted. Frontend verified both outcomes against disk rather than the screen, since the still-open render-staleness bug (below) makes accepted-vs-blocked look identical at a glance in the UI. Reproduces the exact original repro end-to-end, both sides disk-confirmed. This closes the entire Wizard investigation: class acquisition, first-spell bootstrap, and now slot-budget enforcement, all live-verified.

resolved.title: RESOLVED (2026-07-24) — `compute_selected_skill_modifiers` applied the Climb/Intimidate/Swim class-skill bonus regardless of actual class.
resolved.body: Found by QA's systematic Fighter/Wizard/Rogue gap sweep (autonomous mode), verified concretely rather than reasoned abstractly. `CLASS_SKILL_BONUS` (+3) was written when this function only served Fighter (whose real PF1 class-skill list genuinely includes all three skills); the `Computed`/`Blocked` gate (`unmet_selected_skill_posture_conditions`) was later widened to any dispatch-supported class, but the +3 itself was never made class-aware. Rogue is coincidentally correct (its real class-skill list also includes all three). Wizard's real class-skill list includes none of them (Wizard: Appraise/Craft/Fly/Knowledge-all/Linguistics/Profession/Spellcraft) — a Wizard built with the deterministic Climb/Intimidate/Swim posture currently gets `climb = 5` (rank 1 + STR 3 + class-skill 3 − ACP 2); the real value should be `2` (no class-skill bonus). No claim-blocking diagnostic fires — this is a silently wrong number in the explanations list, not a caught/Blocked case, live right now for any Wizard (or Wizard-containing multiclass) that reaches this path. **Distinct from and more urgent than** the already-known, correctly-deferred "class-skill recognition is Fighter-only" finding in `skill_allocation.rs` (item 1's sizing discussion) — that one is medium-large and doesn't gate anything reaching `Computed` today; this one does, and is wrong today, not theoretical. QA correctly filed rather than fixed (production code, not their lane). Backend redirected here as top priority, ahead of the render-staleness investigation (item 10's render-staleness sub-item — reopened, see there, not actually eliminated). **Fix landed (backend, `93a0636d`), verified against the real PCGen corpus before writing code**, not memory: checked `cr_abilities_class.lst` directly and confirmed Fighter (`:2835`) and Rogue (`:2838`) both have Climb/Intimidate/Swim as real class skills, Wizard (`:2565`) has none of the three — resolvable entirely with data already available headlessly, no corpus wall this time. `compute_selected_skill_modifiers` now only applies the +3 when the character has at least one class (of the two, Fighter or Rogue, that actually grants it) that includes the skill; multiclass gets it correctly via PF1's real union rule (a Fighter/Wizard multiclass still gets the bonus via the Fighter side — explicitly tested, not assumed). 4 new inline tests. One real test break found and coordinated with QA before pushing: `tests/sd21_wizard_chassis_computes.rs`'s `wizard_level3_with_ge06_combat_posture_clears_the_selected_skill_diagnostic` asserted the old buggy `climb = 1`; correct value for that fixture's ability scores is `-2`. **Two smaller findings from the same sweep, logged, not actioned:** level-up hit points has an inconsistent exposure pattern (Fighter has a dedicated `class_chassis.fighter.level_1_hit_points` explanation + catalogue test; Wizard/Rogue don't have an equivalent per-class explanation, even though `durability.rs`'s `compute_max_hp` already computes the mathematically-identical, PCGen-cross-verified value for all three) — not a missing calculation, likely not worth dedicated work. Bonus spells from high ability score, including the Wizard Intelligence-based bonus-spells record, confirmed present and correctly wired — no gap. **Follow-up sweep (QA, same day): the adjacent narrow-posture-gate functions came back clean.** Checked `unmet_combat_posture_conditions`'s Fighter bonus-feat sub-check (correctly guarded by `supported_fighter_level(input).is_some()`, genuinely skipped for non-Fighter) and `compute_combat_baseline`'s Weapon/Armor Training bonuses (default to level=1 for non-Fighter via `.unwrap_or(1)`, correctly producing a 0 bonus — semantically right, not a bug despite the implicit fallback). Closes out the "does this bug pattern recur nearby" question with certainty rather than leaving it assumed.
resolved.call_text: `CLASS_SKILL_BONUS` (+3) was written when this function only served Fighter (whose real PF1 class-skill list genuinely includes all three skills); the `Computed`/`Blocked` gate (`unmet_selected_skill_posture_conditions`) was later widened to any dispatch-supported class, but the +3 itself was never made class-aware.

resolved.title: RESOLVED — class-dropdown honesty fix, plus a real positive surprise: Wizard and Rogue actually support any race, not just Human.
resolved.body: Frontend's class-dropdown audit (autonomous mode) found the create-character dropdown's "(Human only, partial)" label was actively false for 8 of 11 CRB classes (Paladin/Ranger/Sorcerer/Bard/Barbarian/Monk/Cleric/Druid): each has its own "does not compute a supported chassis" doc comment in `pilot_compute.rs`, and live-testing (fresh Human Barbarian) confirmed a real named `Blocked` diagnostic, never `Saved`, for **any** race including Human — the non-Human fallback text ("Pick Human to see what's computed") was false for these 8; Human only gets nicer-named diagnostics instead of 4 generic ones, never an actual computed build. Fixed with a new `ClassSupportLevel` variant (`human-diagnostics-only`, distinct from the genuinely-working `partial-human-only`) and honest dropdown/description/fallback text. Not a stub or silent failure — the `Blocked` path itself was always correctly detailed, only the labeling overclaimed. Pushed `34635157`, 62/62 suite green. **Bonus finding, opposite direction — real, free alpha-bar progress.** Wizard and Rogue, both labeled `partial-human-only`, turn out to be mislabeled too: confirmed via git archaeology (`3484b5d`, the Wizard fix's original commit, never had a Human condition) and live-verified (fresh Elf Wizard 1 and fresh Elf Rogue 1 both reached `Computed`/`Saved` through the real creation UI, disk-confirmed with `race_id=race:elf` and correct distinct stat blocks) that neither ever had a race restriction — `supported_wizard_level`/`supported_rogue_level` and every downstream gate check class_id and level only, never race. Reclassified both to `full`, same as Fighter. This means bar item 2 ("any class or race from the four primary books") is materially closer than believed for the three working classes — the "Human only" framing had been a stale, never-verified assumption carried forward since the original investigations, not a real constraint. **Confirmed through level-up too, not just creation (frontend, follow-up).** Leveled both the Elf Rogue and Elf Wizard from creation up one level via the real `LevelUpDialog`: Elf Rogue 1→2 (HP 10→17, BAB +0→+1, Reflex +4→+5) and Elf Wizard 1→2 (HP 8→14, BAB +0→+1, Will +3→+4), both disk-confirmed with correct progression and `race_id=race:elf` retained. The `full` race-support claim holds through the level-up path, not just a creation-time fluke. **Independently re-derived, all 11 rows, not just the two already touched (QA, 2026-07-24, completeness sweep).** Read every classification directly against `pilot_compute.rs` rather than trusting the commit: Fighter/Wizard/Rogue's `supported_X_level` functions check only `class_id` and level, confirmed no `race_id` reference in either — genuinely `full`. All 8 `human-diagnostics-only` classes (Paladin, Ranger, Sorcerer, Bard, Barbarian, Cleric, Druid, Monk) individually checked, not spot-checked — every one has the identical `supported_X_level` gate plus a `race_id != HUMAN_RACE_ID` early return, and none appear in `table_class_id`'s exact 3-class allowlist, which is what guarantees `Blocked` regardless of race for all 8, Human included. `describeClassSupportLevel`'s description strings don't overclaim anywhere. `characterHubModel.test.ts` re-ran clean. Clean, independently confirmed record for all 11 classes, not just the ones this doc had already touched.
resolved.call_text: Fixed with a new `ClassSupportLevel` variant (`human-diagnostics-only`, distinct from the genuinely-working `partial-human-only`) and honest dropdown/description/fallback text.

resolved.title: RESOLVED (2026-07-24) — 4 of 7 grounded races were missing their real third ability-score adjustment.
resolved.body: Elf fixed first (`9ec0e036`), then Dwarf/Gnome/Halfling + the size-explanation text fix landed together (`2f05dee4`) — backend independently re-verified all 3 remaining races against the real PCGen corpus rather than trusting QA's citations (confirmed Dwarf +2 Wis, Gnome +2 Cha, Halfling +2 Cha, all matching exactly), correctly declined to wire size into AC/attack (real future scope, not folded in), and applied the shared-checkout commit-serialization mitigation (checked `git diff --cached --stat` before committing) so no attribution race recurred. All 4 races now have accurate racial ability-adjustment recognition records; QA independently confirmed zero blast radius held (full integration suite clean) rather than trusting the claim. Catalogue adoption for Dwarf/Gnome/Halfling landed too (`fb01768d`) — QA independently re-verified all 3 PCGen citations before adopting rather than trusting the commit message, 34/34 new tests plus a full 474/474 suite run. Fully closed end to end: fix + independent re-verification + catalogue coverage for all 4 races. Following up on item 15's Elf-Wizard/Rogue confirmation, QA traced PCGen's actual race data all the way through the real reference chain (`cr_races.lst`'s per-race `.MOD` lines are only source-page citations; the real base race lives in a separate PCC pack per race → `<race>_abilities_race.lst`, each `BONUS:STAT` line explicitly tagged `TYPE:...Racial Default...`) for all 7 races Codex grounds (`explain_*_race_seam` in `pilot_compute.rs`), not just Elf. **Broken, same shape each time — a fixed physical +2/-2 pair is grounded, the race's real +2 mental-ability component is dropped:** - **Elf**: has DEX+2/CON-2, real is DEX+2/**INT+2**/CON-2 (`elf_abilities_race.lst:18`). Matters most since Elf Wizard is confirmed reachable and Intelligence is Wizard's casting stat. - **Dwarf**: has CON+2/CHA-2, real is CON+2/**WIS+2**/CHA-2 (`dwarf_abilities_race.lst:18`). - **Gnome**: has CON+2/STR-2, real is CON+2/**CHA+2**/STR-2 (`gnome_abilities_race.lst:18`). - **Halfling**: has DEX+2/STR-2, real is DEX+2/**CHA+2**/STR-2 (`halfling_abilities_race.lst:18`). **Confirmed correct, not affected**: Half-Elf and Half-Orc are both correctly implemented as a player-chosen floating +2 to any one ability score (QA caught and corrected its own initial misremembering that Half-Elf got nothing, by live-checking the actual code rather than assuming from the pattern — PCGen confirms Half-Elf gets the same floating +2 as Half-Orc). Human is already correct (live arithmetic on the player's chosen target, unrelated to this bug family). **Scope-checked, not assumed**: Dwarf's size/speed independently spot-verified against the same PCGen source (Medium, 20ft, both match) — the bug is isolated to the ability-modifier section specifically, each race's other trait records (size/speed/senses/immunities) look independently correct. Since each affected race's explanation is recognition-only (expects the fixture's chosen score to already reflect the adjustment, doesn't compute it live), any character of these 4 races built per Codex's own documented convention silently ends up 2 points off on the missing ability versus real PF1 — and for any calc keyed to that ability (saves, skills, spell DCs for casters), the error propagates. **QA's read, worth taking seriously**: this consistent a pattern across 4 races reads like a systemic authoring gap (built from a "2-stat template" that never accounted for these races' real 3-stat adjustment), not 4 independent oversights — recommends one bundled fix over 4 separate incremental ones, which the lead adopted. QA correctly filed all 4 rather than fixing them (production code, not their lane). Owner: backend, bundling all 4 into one fix, queued immediately after the render-staleness close. **Small, distinct addendum folded into the same fix (QA, same sweep):** while verifying Halfling's other named traits (Keen Senses, Sure-Footed, Fearless, Halfling Luck — all confirmed correct against real PCGen data), found Gnome's and Halfling's `race.<X>.trait_bundle.size` explanation text self-contradicts: it correctly sets `GNOME_SIZE_CATEGORY`/`HALFLING_SIZE_CATEGORY` to `"Small"` and correctly cites `SIZE:SMALL` from the corpus, but then claims Small "contributes no numeric effect to attack rolls, AC, skill checks... or any other computed value" — true for the other 5 grounded races (all Medium), false for real PF1 Small size in general (+1 AC, +1 attack, -1 CMB/CMD, +4 Stealth per SRD). Looks like the size-explanation template was copied across races without adjusting the claim for the two that are actually Small. **Correctly right-sized, not overstated**: this is a misleading claim in a recognition-only explanation, not a live wrong number — `compute_combat_baseline` has no size-modifier term for *any* race yet (confirmed during the earlier class-skill-bonus sweep), so nothing numeric is actually wrong today. Two independent pieces: (1) small/cheap — correct the misleading text, folded into backend's current race-bundle fix; (2) larger — actually wire a size modifier into AC/attack/CMB/Stealth, which overlaps the already-tracked, already-deferred AC/attack-bonus posture-narrowness architecture item (this doc's item 1) — not picked up now, noted as belonging alongside that existing tracking rather than as fresh scope.

resolved.title: RESOLVED, real precise gap identified (2026-07-24) — a documented Wizard spellbook ceiling (level 3) didn't fire at level 4, for non-Human Wizards specifically.
resolved.body: `pilot_compute.rs` documents `WIZARD_SPELLBOOK_SUPPORTED_MAX_LEVEL=3` with claim-blocking diagnostics expected past that level. Frontend live-drove an Elf Wizard through real level-ups 1→2→3→4 via the real `LevelUpDialog` — all four succeeded, disk-confirmed real progression each step (HP 8→14→20→26, BAB/Will climbing correctly). No `Blocked` wall appeared at level 4 as documented. Frontend sent backend the specifics with line numbers and an explicitly-unconfirmed guess (possibly the restrictive check only fires from a level-1-specific function, not the wider chassis-widening path that's since been built) — correctly didn't dig further into backend's file themselves. **Deliberately NOT logged as a bonus/positive finding yet, unlike the "any race" discoveries** — the ceiling may exist precisely because the compute formulas past level 3 were never validated as correct, in which case "unblocked" could mean level 4+ Wizards now silently produce wrong spell-slot/save-DC/whatever values instead of being honestly stopped, the same shape of problem as the class-skill-modifier bug (item 14) — just newly *exposed* rather than newly *introduced*. Backend asked to determine which it is (stale leftover check vs. a real validation gap) before this gets resolved either direction; if it's the latter, QA should spot-check the level 4 Wizard's actual computed values against real PF1/PCGen once backend clarifies what's reachable. **QA's static sweep (2026-07-24): the ceiling is correctly enforced in `pilot_compute.rs`, verified 3 ways, not assumed.** Systematically grepped all level-comparison gates, all `_MAX_LEVEL`/`SUPPORTED_MAX` constants, and all "only supported for"/"bounded to" comments — `WIZARD_SPELLBOOK_SUPPORTED_MAX_LEVEL` is the only sub-ceiling of its shape in the file, no other class has a hidden one like it. Confirmed the gate fires correctly three ways: (1) `unmet_wizard_spellbook_conditions` checks `level > WIZARD_SPELLBOOK_SUPPORTED_MAX_LEVEL` and pushes `claim_blocking: true` diagnostics; (2) `build_pilot_headless_receipt` derives overall `Blocked` status directly from `diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.claim_blocking)` — no parallel status logic that could diverge; (3) an existing test (`tests/sd13_wizard_level4_progression.rs`) already proves it fires at exactly level 4 through the real pipeline. Also checked the Tauri layer (`apply_level_up` has no bypassing path, defers entirely to the standard pipeline) and the reverse failure mode (all 11 classes' level gates use an identical, correct pattern; all `claim_blocking: false` diagnostics checked individually, none relate to a dropped threshold). **Conclusion: the engine-side enforcement is airtight** — if frontend's "didn't fire" symptom is real, it's very likely UI-side, matching the shape of the earlier render-staleness bug (server-correct, client looks wrong), not a second engine gap. QA and backend reconciling directly with frontend rather than duplicating investigation. **Root cause found (frontend, 2026-07-24): both QA's static analysis and the original live symptom were correct, from different angles.** The ceiling itself lives inside `explain_wizard_level1_prepared_spell_baseline` (`pilot_compute.rs:14950`), which has `if input.chosen.race_id != HUMAN_RACE_ID { return; }` immediately after its level guard — for any non-Human Wizard, the entire function, ceiling included, never runs at all. QA's sweep correctly found the enforcement airtight (true, for the Human path it traced); frontend correctly found no wall at level 4 for an Elf Wizard (true, because the whole function is skipped for non-Human). **Not a regression, and not "level 4+ silently computes wrong values" as originally feared**: BAB/saves/HP for a non-Human Wizard remain correct, live-verified, because those route through a separate chassis path that was already widened to be race-agnostic. **What's actually missing for non-Human Wizards**: the Wizard-specific spellbook validation (the ceiling itself never blocks them past level 3) and spell-save-DC grounding (lives in the same gated function) — both real, previously-invisible gaps that frontend's own "any race" discovery exposed, not something that discovery broke. **Empirically confirmed at every level, not just level 4 (backend, 2026-07-24).** Composed an Elf Wizard level 1 directly and called `build_pilot_headless_receipt` — status `Computed`, but ZERO explanations with a `class_chassis.wizard`/`class_spell.wizard` id prefix, zero wizard-spell diagnostics of any kind, structurally absent with no claim-blocking flag raised about the absence. Separately confirmed a Human Wizard leveled 1→4 correctly hits `Blocked` at level 4 exactly as documented — the ceiling works precisely as designed for the one race it's scoped to. So the original symptom wasn't level-4-specific at all: the entire spellbook-gate mechanism, ceiling included, never engages for a non-Human Wizard at *any* level, 1 through 20. **Correction to item 19's earlier framing**: the wizard-spell-save-DC fix from item 12 lives inside this same Human-gated function, so "Elf Wizard's spell save DC is shorted by 2" was itself imprecise — it isn't shorted, it's **absent entirely** for any non-Human Wizard (corrected here rather than left standing). **Decision (lead, 2026-07-24): documented as a deferred completeness gap, not fixed and not blocked.** Backend proposed two shapes — widen the function to all races (real future-epic effort, everything in it currently reasoned in Human-specific terms, would need per-race re-verification) or add a claim-blocking diagnostic for non-Human Wizards naming the absence (small, honest, but would **regress already-verified, disk-confirmed capability** — the swarm proved an Elf Wizard can add spells and reach `Computed` live, end to end). Neither is right: widening is out of scope for this wave, and blocking conflates a genuine **completeness gap** (wizard-specific spell math doesn't exist yet for non-Human, nothing is computed *wrong*) with a **correctness bug** (a value that's wrong, like the class-skill-modifier bug) — the same distinction item 17's feat-effects finding already established (a Fighter can select Toughness and reach `Computed` even though it does nothing; that's correctly not blocked either). Filed here alongside item 17 as the third tracked completeness/architecture gap (with the AC/attack-bonus item), not assigned to anyone this wave. **Lead correction (2026-07-24, ~14:40 ET) — briefly mis-dispatched to backend as active backlog after a context compaction; corrected before backend started.** This item's own decision two paragraphs up ("not fixed and not blocked... not assigned to anyone this wave") stands; SWARM_TASKS.md's row is corrected back to `blocked`/deferred, not `in progress`. No engineering work was actually done under the mistaken dispatch — caught by re-reading this doc before trusting the task-table summary alone. Backend independently caught the same contradiction from their own memory of this item's history before writing any code, and correctly stood down pending lead confirmation rather than picking a side themselves. **Scoping note, informational only, not a re-opening of scope (backend, 2026-07-24).** While getting oriented on the (mistaken) dispatch, backend read `explain_wizard_level1_prepared_spell_baseline` and its two callees before being told to stand down. Observation for whoever revisits this item's scope later: the widening effort may be smaller than the original decision estimated — the ~400-line function's only Human-specific content is the one `race_id != HUMAN_RACE_ID` race-gate line plus two cosmetic "Human Wizard" strings in explanation text; no formula in the body actually depends on race, since `ability_modifiers` already arrives race-adjusted via `apply_human_ability_bonus` upstream. Not verified beyond a read-through, not acted on, and does not by itself change this item's `blocked`/deferred status — logged here purely so the information isn't lost before an eventual real scope decision. **OPERATOR DECISION (Todd Hintzmann, 2026-07-24) — widen it now, given backend's smaller-than-feared scoping read.** Explicit call, made after the swarm-wide closure-readiness checkpoint (item 31): remove the `race_id != HUMAN_RACE_ID` gate in `explain_wizard_level1_prepared_spell_baseline` and re-verify the formulas for a non-Human Wizard end to end. Backend's scoping note (above) found only one race-gate line plus two cosmetic strings are actually Human-specific — no formula depends on race since `ability_modifiers` arrives pre-adjusted — but that was a read-through, not a full verification; backend should confirm this empirically (the same "prove it, don't reason about it" discipline this swarm has used throughout) before landing, including a real non-Human Wizard reaching `Computed` with correct spell-save-DC and the spellbook ceiling firing correctly past level 3. Dispatched to backend. **RESOLVED, landed and lead-verified (backend, `7c2d2ad2`, 2026-07-24).** Race gate removed from `explain_wizard_level1_prepared_spell_baseline`; the "Human Wizard" explanation strings generalized via a new `race_display_label` helper (derives the display name from `race_id`, same "derive, don't hardcode" pattern `class_summary_label` already used). Empirically verified exactly as required — 4 new tests through the real `build_pilot_headless_receipt` entry point, not just the narrower chassis function: an Elf Wizard reaches `Computed` with a correct racially-adjusted spell-save-DC at level 1, stays within the ceiling at level 3, and correctly hits `WIZARD_SPELLBOOK_SUPPORTED_MAX_LEVEL` at level 4 — all previously entirely absent for non-Human Wizards; Human Wizard behavior confirmed unchanged in the same pass. **Lead independently re-ran** the 4 new tests (pass), the full root-crate workspace suite (4275/4275, 0 failed, matches exactly — up from 4271 by the 4 new tests), and the desktop suite (204/204, unaffected — checked first since `character_hub.rs`/`pf1_adapter.rs` both reference this ceiling). Item 18 fully closed. **Independently re-verified, thorough full-function trace (QA, 2026-07-24).** Traced every formula in the function's full body (lines 15001–15412) by hand, not just the 4 new tests' coverage: confirmed BAB/saves/spell-slot-ladder/Scribe-Scroll/specialist-bonus/Intense-Spells are pure level-driven functions; confirmed `spell_save_dc` and `force_missile_uses_per_day` (the only two reading ability modifiers) receive an already race-adjusted `ability_modifiers.intelligence` (`apply_human_ability_bonus` passes non-Human scores through unchanged; the frontend bakes the real racial adjustment in before submission); confirmed `unmet_wizard_spellbook_conditions`/`ground_wizard_prepared_spellbook` have no race reference. Grepped the whole function for `race_id`/`HUMAN_RACE_ID`/`race:` — only hit is the new `race_display_label` call. Checked all 7 curated races through `race_display_label` (not just Elf), all correct PF1 naming, throwaway test reverted cleanly. Confirmed the "Human Wizard" string change is safe — grepped the tree for every `"Human Wizard"` hit, none are runtime string-matches against the live explanation text. **Reproduced RED themselves and surfaced a sharper finding than originally scoped**: restoring the old race gate didn't just lose the spell-save-DC — the Elf Wizard stayed `Computed` past the real spellbook ceiling at level 4 with zero ceiling diagnostic at all, meaning the pre-fix bug was a genuine correctness gap (enforcement silently never ran for non-Human), not merely a missing display value. Ran clean: 4/4 new tests, 258/258 full lib suite, 204/204 desktop — matches the commit's counts exactly. **Sweep for the same shape elsewhere (frontend, 2026-07-24): Wizard's gap does not repeat as a correctness issue, but one new question surfaced.** Checked all 11 `MAX_SUPPORTED_*_LEVEL` constants — `WIZARD_SPELLBOOK_SUPPORTED_MAX_LEVEL` is the only secondary/nested ceiling in the file, doesn't recur. Checked all 15 `if input.chosen.race_id != HUMAN_RACE_ID { return; }` occurrences: 2 are legitimately Human-only-named functions; 13 are per-class `explain_*` functions — 8 already match the known `human-diagnostics-only` pattern (expected, not new); of the 3 classes that reach `Computed` (Fighter/Wizard/Rogue), Rogue's `explain_rogue_level1_chassis` is race-gated the same way but only takes an `explanations` param, no `diagnostics` — structurally can't affect `Computed`/`Blocked`, so non-Human Rogues lose flavor-text grounding (Sneak Attack/Trapfinding/Evasion records) but nothing the frontend currently displays — cosmetic, not correctness. **One new genuine question**: Fighter's `validate_fighter_feat_choice_legality` (line 7867) is also race-gated *and* carries claim-blocking diagnostics for non-canonical feat choices — its own doc comment claims it's redundant with the separate, already-race-agnostic `unmet_combat_posture_conditions` gate ("any other posture is already claim-blocked upstream"). Frontend correctly did not assert this overlap themselves and flagged it for backend to trace — if the claim is wrong, a non-Human Fighter with an invalid feat choice could reach `Computed` when it shouldn't, the opposite failure direction from the Wizard gap (something that should Block but might not, vs. something absent). Backend investigating; frontend live-testing the same question from the UI side in parallel. **RESOLVED — the overlap claim was wrong; real, currently-reachable gap fixed (backend, 2026-07-24).** `unmet_combat_posture_conditions` only ever checked the level-1 Fighter bonus-feat slot; `CANONICAL_FIGHTER_FEAT_CHOICES` covers 17 slots total (levels 2–20 bonus feats plus 4 weapon-training groups), so the other 14+ slots had zero validation for any non-Human Fighter — not theoretical, already reachable today via `level_up_character`'s caller-supplied `additional_choices` with no other check catching it. **Confirmed empirically before fixing, not assumed**: built an Elf Fighter, gave it a wrong bonus-feat choice at level 2, got zero diagnostics — genuinely `Blocked`-worthy input silently passing. Fixed by removing the incorrect Human-only race gate from `validate_fighter_feat_choice_legality` — Fighter's own bonus-feat/weapon-training choices are Fighter class features, not Human-specific; the one genuinely race-coupled table entry is already self-limiting (absent for non-Human, existing "slot absent, skip" logic already handles it correctly). 2 new tests (the real gap now caught; canonical selection still passes for any race), full suite clean, zero blast radius. This is the opposite failure direction from item 18's Wizard gap — something that should have Blocked and now correctly does, rather than something absent that was reaching `Computed` unflagged. **Nuance, live-verified (frontend, 2026-07-24): the fix is correct but currently has no UI attack surface.** `compose_character_input` hardcodes the canonical values for both slots this check protects (`choice:level_1_character_feat → feat:power_attack`, `choice:fighter_bonus_feat → feat:weapon_focus:weapon:longsword`) unconditionally for every character — no create-form field or level-up affordance lets a player submit anything else for these two slots. Live-verified with a fresh Dwarf Fighter: `Computed`/`Saved` successfully, disk-confirmed identical canonical choice records to a Human Fighter, no fabricated third slot (the Human-only `choice:human_bonus_feat` entry correctly absent, not flagged as illegal — matches the validation function's own "absent slot is not fabricated" doc comment). So the divergent-choice scenario the check exists to catch can't currently be triggered by anyone, Human or non-Human, through the shipped UI — the gap backend closed is real and correct defense-in-depth at the command/API layer (`level_up_character`'s `additional_choices` parameter could still be invoked non-canonically by something other than today's UI), not an active user-visible bug today. Doesn't diminish the fix's value, just calibrates its actual current exposure for the record. **Second, independent gap in the same function, also confirmed and fixed (backend, `0eb9ea65`).** The gate used `supported_fighter_level` (single-class-only), so it skipped every Fighter+X multiclass mix entirely — regardless of race, even Human. Confirmed empirically before fixing: a Human Fighter1/Rogue3 with a wrong level-1 bonus-feat choice produced zero diagnostics. Fixed with a one-line swap to `fighter_level_in_mix`, the multiclass-aware equivalent already established elsewhere in the file (`wizard_level_in_mix`'s precedent) — no other change needed since the loop body never used the specific level value. 2 new tests, full suite clean. This closes both dimensions of the original wrong doc-comment claim: race and multiclass, same function, two independently-confirmed gaps. Very likely shares the same "no current UI attack surface" property as the race fix above (same hardcoded-canonical-values mechanism regardless of class-mix) — not separately re-verified, flagged for anyone who wants certainty later. **Systematic sweep, complete (backend, `68721ca0`): a third instance found and fixed, correctly risk-tiered as non-exploitable.** Checked all 4 `_legality`/`_conditions`/`validate_` gate functions that exist in `pilot_compute.rs` for the same brittleness. Found one more: `unmet_combat_posture_conditions`'s own Fighter bonus-feat sub-check had the identical blind spot (`supported_fighter_level` instead of `fighter_level_in_mix`) — confirmed empirically (the function's own `unmet` list came back empty for the multiclass scenario) before fixing. **Precisely risk-tiered, not overstated**: this instance was NOT actually exploitable at the system level, since `validate_fighter_feat_choice_legality` (already fixed for multiclass) independently catches the exact same slot — overall `Computed`/`Blocked` status was already correct either way. Fixed anyway as a real internal-consistency issue (two checks that shouldn't be able to silently diverge later), explicitly flagged as a different risk tier than the first two fixes. The other 2 candidate functions checked out clean: `unmet_wizard_spellbook_conditions` takes an already-resolved level as a parameter (caller already multiclass-aware); `unmet_selected_skill_posture_conditions` has no per-class level lookup at all. **Sweep complete — all 4 gate functions in the file now covered, no further instances found.**

resolved.title: RESOLVED, MAJOR — CreateCharacterForm never actually submitted racial ability adjustments, for any of the 4 fixed-adjustment races, since the form was first built.
resolved.body: Frontend live-verified backend's Elf +2 Intelligence fix (`9ec0e036`) and found it didn't change the visible outcome: a fresh Elf Wizard's ABILITIES panel showed `INT 10 +0`, `DEX 14 +2`, `CON 14 +2` — none of Elf's three racial adjustments (+2 DEX, -2 CON, +2 INT) were actually applied. Root cause was entirely frontend-side, unrelated to any of backend's race-bundle explanation-text work: `CreateCharacterForm.tsx` computed `calculatedScore()` (raw + racial adjustment + allocation + age) for the on-screen "Calculated" preview column only, but submitted `rawScore()` — the unadjusted value — as the actual `abilityScores` in the create request. Confirmed against the engine's real contract via `pilot_compute.rs`'s own doc comment on `apply_human_ability_bonus`: every non-Human race's submitted score is expected to already bake in its racial adjustment (Human is the sole exception — pre-bonus base plus a server-side choice). The frontend never honored that contract, for any of the 4 races, independent of and predating this session's explanation-text fixes — those were correct about what a race's adjustment *should* be, just describing a number the frontend was never actually sending. **Fixed** (`f2c616ed`): new `applyRacialAbilityAdjustments()` in `composeCreateCharacterRequest.ts`, wired into the submission path, no-op for Human, 3 new regression tests. **Live re-verified end-to-end**: a fresh Elf Wizard now saves `dexterity:16, constitution:12, intelligence:12` (disk-confirmed) and the sheet shows the full correct cascade — DEX +3/CON +1/INT +1, Knowledge skills +1, DEX-based skills +3, AC/saves all shifted correctly. Since this is the same code path for all 4 races, QA re-verifying Dwarf/Gnome/Halfling now get correct submitted scores too, same rigor as the original race sweep — this closes the loop on the full 4-race gap (recognition-text fix + submission-bug fix + live verification), not just the explanation-text half. **Dwarf/Gnome/Halfling re-verified — real production-code execution, short of full live-UI proof due to an environment blocker (QA, 2026-07-24).** Confirmed `applyRacialAbilityAdjustments` is called unconditionally regardless of race (no race-specific branching at the call site) and that `RACE_OPTIONS`' catalog data has carried the correct full 3-stat adjustment for all three races since the file was first authored (checked via git history, independent of and predating backend's engine-side text fix). **Executed the real production code, not a reimplementation**: imported the actual function and catalog directly and confirmed Dwarf (CON+2/WIS+2/CHA-2), Gnome (CON+2/CHA+2/STR-2), and Halfling (DEX+2/CHA+2/STR-2) all compute correctly. **Found a real, separate gap while there**: `composeCreateCharacterRequest.test.ts`'s regression coverage is incomplete — the Dwarf test only asserts unrelated stats stay untouched, never checks the actual adjusted CON/WIS/CHA values, and Gnome/Halfling have zero coverage at all (only Elf got full treatment). Correctly filed to frontend rather than edited (frontend's file). **Could not complete the full live-UI-then-disk-confirm verification** matching frontend's methodology — the desktop app environment was consistently unstable (webview renders solid black, process/Xvfb pair dies within seconds, ~6 attempts, ruled out as a resource issue with 17GB free) — flagged honestly as an environment blocker rather than either fabricating a live-verified claim or silently giving up. **Accepted as sufficient** given the strength of the evidence (real code, real data, mechanically identical to the already-fully-verified Elf path) — not re-attempted further. Worth watching whether this environment instability is session-wide (frontend's capstone walkthrough uses the same GUI environment).

resolved.title: RESOLVED — `skill_allocation.rs`'s class-skill recognition was Fighter-only, silently leaving Wizard's and Rogue's cross-class rank cap unenforced.
resolved.body: Dispatched as a bounded widening task following backend's own scoping finding (item 1) that class-skill-list recognition is a labor problem, not an architecture wall. Turned out to be more than pure widening: confirmed empirically before fixing that a level-1 Wizard could allocate 5 ranks to a cross-class skill (real PF1 cap is 1) with zero enforcement — because neither Wizard nor Rogue had ANY grounded class-skill posture in this module, `has_grounded_class_skill_posture` was false for both, so the cross-class half-cap logic never engaged at all, not just "no class-skill bonus." Same failure shape as item 14 (a silently wrong number, no claim-blocking diagnostic), but on rank enforcement rather than a modifier value. **Fixed (`21f815c1`)**, grounded against the real PCGen corpus: Rogue gets all 5 of this module's bounded skills (Climb/Intimidate/Swim/Diplomacy/Disable Device) as real class skills (`cr_abilities_class.lst:2838`, verified exact match); Wizard gets a genuinely empty grounded list (`cr_abilities_class.lst:2565`, checked zero overlap, not assumed) — but even the empty grounding matters, since it's what flips the cross-class cap from unenforced to correctly enforced for Wizard. Scoped to Wizard/Rogue only, same bounded-caution philosophy as the existing Fighter posture. 4 new tests, full suite clean, zero blast radius (QA's existing `skill_allocation` tests never touched Wizard/Rogue at all). QA to independently verify. **QA's independent catalogue coverage landed (`d35521ec`, lead stewardship during a quota outage).** QA wrote real fixture-driven tests (through the actual `load_character_input_fixture` parser, not hand-built structs) re-verifying both PCGen citations independently and cross-checking against the separate `compute_selected_skill_modifiers` fix's own fixture to prove the two modules now agree on Wizard's class-skill list. Finished but uncommitted when QA hit a session quota limit; the lead verified it (3/3 pass, full workspace suite clean) before landing it on QA's behalf rather than risk losing finished work during the outage.
