resolved.title: RESOLVED, SIGNAL FINDING — systematic sweep for other Fighter-only-grounded computations came back clean, one real near-miss traced and ruled out.
resolved.body: Following the pattern that found items 14 and 20 (widening Fighter-only recognition surfacing silent bugs for Wizard/Rogue), backend swept `pilot_compute.rs`, `skill_allocation.rs`, `durability.rs`, and `money.rs` for any remaining instance of the same shape. **One candidate investigated and ruled out**: `explain_rogue_level1_chassis` gates on the single-class-only `supported_rogue_level` (no `rogue_level_in_mix` counterpart), superficially the same shape as items 14/20's root cause — but tracing where its output goes shows its explanations (sneak-attack-die-count, trapfinding, Evasion, Trap Sense, Uncanny Dodge) are standalone, never wired into `compute_fighter_chassis`, `compute_total_saves`, or `compute_combat_baseline`, unlike Fighter's Bravery/bonus-feat progression which feeds real feat-choice validation. No downstream consumer exists, so for a multiclass build missing this record, nothing is silently wrong and no rule goes unenforced — same cosmetic-only shape already established for non-Human Rogue in item 18's sweep, not a new correctness bug. **Everything else checked out clean**: the other `FIGHTER_CLASS_ID` sites in `pilot_compute.rs` are deliberate, already-widened 3-class dispatch points with scope-decision doc comments; `unmet_selected_skill_posture_conditions` was already widened pre-swarm (SD-21 E6b.1); `supported_fighter_level`'s one remaining Fighter-only use (armor training) is correctly Fighter-exclusive, a real class feature, not a generalization gap; `durability.rs` is fully class-generic with an explicit Fighter/Wizard/Rogue-parity test; `money.rs` has no class branching at all, out of scope for this pattern. **Backend's own read, adopted by the lead**: this is a genuine signal, not an absence of looking — the swarm's remaining distance from the alpha bar is now confirmed architecture-level (items 1, 17, 18), not further silent-correctness bugs in the three working classes' shared computation paths.

resolved.title: RESOLVED — `characterProgression.ts` now has real regression coverage.
resolved.body: Landed (`ca25bfef`): new `characterProgression.test.ts` covers `parseHeldClasses` (including the exact multiclass regression case `d03bc89d` fixed, plus an unknown-class-id fallback), `formatHeldClasses`, `totalCharacterLevel`, `casterLevel`, `classSkillPointsBase`, `classHitDie`, `classWeaponProficiency`, `maxHitPoints` (both single-class and a multiclass case verifying only the character's true first-ever level maximizes its hit die), `totalSkillPoints`, `buildLevelEntries`, `buildNextEntries`, and `previewLevelUp`. 63/63 suite green. Genuine RED caught along the way: frontend's own first-draft assumption about the title-case regex (that underscores would become spaces) was wrong — `_` counts as a `\w` word character, so the whole segment is one contiguous match and only the leading letter capitalizes — caught when the test failed and fixed to match real behavior, not adjusted to match the wrong assumption.

resolved.title: RESOLVED — LevelUpDialog now collects a real feat pick at feat-gaining levels.
resolved.body: QA verified `e8e45976` (LevelUpDialog wiring) and found the mechanics clean, but flagged a real, understated-scope gap: the excusing comment about no feat catalog was stale, and Fighter 1→2 genuinely should offer a bonus-feat pick and didn't. **Fixed (`ddfc66bb`)**: new `levelGrantsFeat(features)` pure predicate in `characterProgression.ts` (covers the universal odd-level feat, Fighter's bonus combat feat, and Wizard's periodic bonus feat, all already represented as feature strings in the existing table). When a level grants a feat, `handleLevelUpAccept` defers and opens the exact same feat `ItemPickerModal` the Feats-tab "Add Feat" button uses (same catalog, no second picker built), retitled "Pick a feat — level N"; picking one persists the level-up first, refreshes so the sheet is never stale, then grants the feat via the real `addFeatSelection` command. Cancelling aborts the whole level-up rather than leaving a half-applied state. When a level grants no feat, behavior is byte-identical to before. **Real deviation from the original suggestion, found by testing, not assumed**: frontend tried also recording the pick via `additionalChoices` (mirroring the hit-die choice) and the backend rejected it outright — `local_store.rs`'s round-trip grammar requires at least two colon-segments in a `selection_id`, which `hp:average` happens to satisfy and a real feat catalog key like "Cleave" never will. Since `additionalChoices` is inert anyway (nothing gates on it) and the real grant lives entirely in `chosen.selected_feats` via `addFeatSelection`, the doomed provenance entry was correctly dropped rather than breaking every real feat pick to satisfy a decorative record. **Live-verified both branches end to end**: a Dwarf Fighter 1→2 got the picker, picked Cleave, confirmed on disk and in the Feats tab (HP recomputed to 22/22); a Human Wizard 1→2 (no feat at that level) leveled up with no interruption, exactly as before. New test (`verifiesLevelGrantsFeatDetectsEveryRealFeatSource`) covers all three real feat sources plus a true no-feat level. 63/63 suite green, typecheck clean.

resolved.title: RESOLVED — PCGen parity comparator gained a new dimension, `combat.base_attack_bonus`.
resolved.body: Backend's self-directed scan (following up on the earlier DTO-consumption sweep) found the comparator only ever exposed `combat.baseline_melee_attack_bonus` (the Strength/feat-inclusive total), never the raw class-table BAB PCGen's own export template carries separately (`<attack><melee><bab>`). Verified empirically before implementing — ran the real PCGen pipeline against the Fighter fixture, confirmed `<bab>+1</bab>` matches Codex's own value. Landed across the full stack (`cda3bf1c` + QA's catalogue adoption `b8eff433`): `SelectedParityDimensions::from_receipt`/`from_pilot_receipt`, `pcgen-normalize-output.py` extraction (deliberately from `/character/attack/melee/bab`, not the confusingly-named sibling element — documented why), a new Python test file (RED→GREEN), 2 new Rust lib tests. **Real end-to-end confirmation**: both `sd26_pilot_case_verification.rs` and `v06_wizard_pilot_case_verification.rs` (which drive the actual PCGen pipeline) show genuine agreement — Fighter BAB 1==1, Wizard BAB 0==0 (correctly reflecting Wizard's poor BAB progression at level 1). Cross-surface protocol followed correctly: backend held the commit until QA landed the 4 mechanically-affected test files (`b8eff433`), then pushed. Small hygiene fix rode along: added a Python section to `.gitignore` (`__pycache__/`, `*.pyc`) since the new Python test file was the first thing to need it. **Second-pass scan, clean, real negative result (backend, 2026-07-24).** Went a level deeper on the same method (check `base-xml.ftl` directly for other exportable-but-unexposed fields) against everything Codex actually computes: touch/flat-footed AC and AC sub-modifiers (PCGen exports them, but Codex only ever computes one aggregate `baseline_armor_class` — new engineering, not wiring, same bucket as items 1/17/18); initiative (explicitly out of scope per `pilot_compute.rs`'s own doc comment, not computed anywhere); a skill-point pool total (zero hits anywhere in `rules_core` — only individual ranks/modifiers exist); encumbrance sub-fields like lift/push/drag capacity (`encumbrance.rs`'s `CarryingCapacityThresholds` only has light/medium/heavy, already fully exposed). DR was the one candidate Codex does compute but, unlike BAB, has no live PCGen fixture yet to verify against (no Barbarian pilot case exists) — not a same-day wiring win the way BAB was. Also swept every owned production file for TODO/FIXME/XXX/"unwired" markers — zero hits, consistent with the no-stub discipline held all session. Genuine clean result, not an absence of looking — this closes out the comparator-scan thread the same way item 21 closed the correctness-bug thread.

resolved.title: RESOLVED — the frontend test-coverage backlog pattern is closed.
resolved.body: Was: multiple frontend logic modules shipped with sound reasoning but zero dedicated test coverage. QA verified `75200fcb` (SkillAllocationDialog wiring) and found the logic itself clean: `skillIdFor`'s "only 5 confirmed skill ids" claim matches `skill_key_ability_modifier` in `skill_allocation.rs` exactly; unrecognized skill ids are genuinely inert (a silent `continue`, no fabrication, no rejection); `handleSkillAllocationAccept` correctly checks `blocked` and returns before touching local state. But grepping every `.test.ts` in the tree for `skillIdFor`/`setSkillAllocations` turns up nothing — the 30-of-35 skill-id mappings beyond the 5 the engine actually recognizes have no regression test pinning them down. **Fourth instance confirmed (QA, `94a38657`, Bio editor wiring) — pattern is now systemic, no longer flagged individually.** Bio editor's own logic verified clean too: on-blur-not-per-keystroke persistence confirmed across all 8 fields, the character-switch `useEffect` has a real `cancelled`-guard against a stale in-flight load landing after a switch (not just claimed), and load/save failure handling is correctly non-load-bearing (bio is flavor text) vs. surfaced through the standard mutation-error banner. Same gap: zero test files reference `characterBio.ts`/`updateCharacterBio`/`loadCharacterBio`. That's 4 for 4 (`characterProgression.ts` — now resolved as item 22 —, `skillIdFor`/`setSkillAllocations`, the stale LevelUpDialog comment's underlying module, and now Bio) — QA's own judgment, adopted: this is a real, systemic gap across this wave of frontend persistence-wiring commits, not four independent coincidences, and not worth re-flagging one at a time going forward. **Owner: frontend, backlog** — a deliberate pass across `characterHub/` for modules with this shape (sound logic, zero dedicated test file) once the current queue (item 23 — since resolved — and any further items QA's sweep surfaces) is clear, rather than four-plus piecemeal fixes. **Self-audit complete, pattern fully closed (frontend, `0c602c72`, 2026-07-24).** Diffed exactly the files this swarm created/touched on `tranche/6` (`git diff $(git merge-base develop tranche/6) tranche/6 -- apps/desktop/src/`, matching this item's own "this wave of frontend persistence-wiring commits" framing) and checked each non-test file for a sibling `.test.ts`. Found and closed 8 in `boundary/` with real logic and zero coverage: the standard no-Tauri-runtime-throws case for `addFeatSelection.ts`/`listFeats.ts`/`loadCreateCharacter.ts`/`loadSavedCharacterDetail.ts`/`purchaseEquipment.ts`/`recordAndPrepareSpellSelection.ts` (same template as the existing `addSpellSelection.test.ts`); `characterDurability.ts` (both functions throw with no runtime, no "resolve to default" case unlike bio/money); `characterMoney.ts` (`gpToCopper`'s real conversion logic including the fractional-copper rounding case, plus its own asymmetric load/adjust behavior). Checked everything else this swarm touched (`characterHub/*.ts`, `testSupport/makeSurface.ts`) and found nothing further — already covered, a React component (no jsdom in this runner, an established non-goal), or fixture/test-support data rather than logic. **Lead-verified**: 77/77 test files passing (up from 69), typecheck clean, sampled `characterMoney.test.ts`/`characterDurability.test.ts` directly — real, specific assertions against real behavior, not scaffolding. **Item 25 fully closed, not partial** — no remaining candidates in frontend's ownership. **Independently sample-reviewed, clean (QA, 2026-07-24).** Read source-then-test for the 6 files the lead hadn't personally sampled (`addFeatSelection`/`listFeats`/`purchaseEquipment`/`recordAndPrepareSpellSelection`/`loadCreateCharacter`/`loadSavedCharacterDetail`). Confirmed each is a thin `invoke()` wrapper with no client-side logic beyond its `hasTauriRuntime()` guard (e.g. `listFeats`'s real filtering is server-side in Rust), so the no-runtime-throws test is genuinely the full available surface, not a shortcut — and confirmed it matches the pre-existing `addSpellSelection.test.ts`/`addEquipmentSelection.test.ts` convention byte-for-byte, not a new pattern invented for this batch. Noted `recordAndPrepareSpellSelection.test.ts` uses the real `WIZARD_STARTER_SPELL_ID` value (`'Light'`), not an arbitrary placeholder. Reproduced a real regression on one file (`purchaseEquipment.test.ts`): temporarily broke the source's error string, watched the test fail with the exact expected mismatch, restored byte-identical — confirms the assertions are load-bearing. All 6 pass individually; full suite 77/77 matches the lead's count. Nothing to flag. **Scoping pass (QA, 2026-07-24), not a build — turns "there's a pattern" into a concrete checklist frontend can execute directly.** One more targeted grep (every `characterHub/*.ts`/`boundary/*.ts` file without a sibling `.test.ts`) turned up two more real candidates beyond the three already named (`skillsModel.ts`/`setSkillAllocations.ts`, `characterBio.ts`, and the Wizard spell-routing logic): `abilityScoreMethods.ts` (real dice/point-buy logic, untested) and `portraitImageProcessing.ts` (Canvas/File-API logic, lower priority — needs a DOM shim this test runner doesn't have, different treatment than the rest). `previewData.ts` was checked and is data-only (a fixture, not logic) — not added to this list. - **`skillsModel.ts` / `boundary/setSkillAllocations.ts`** — the 30-of-35 unconfirmed mappings named above. Concrete cases: (1) `skillIdFor` on a parenthetical skill name (e.g. `"Knowledge (Arcana)"` → `"skill:knowledge_arcana"`, not a double-underscore or trailing-underscore artifact — the regex's edge case); (2) `skillIdFor` on a multi-word non-parenthetical name (`"Sense Motive"` → `"skill:sense_motive"`, `"Sleight of Hand"` → `"skill:sleight_of_hand"`); (3) `isClassSkill` for at least one class/skill pair per confirmed-vs-unconfirmed boundary (a class that has the skill, a class that doesn't, and — if feasible — a case exercising the multiclass union); (4) `boundary/setSkillAllocations.ts` itself only needs the standard no-Tauri-runtime-throws case every other boundary file already has (see `addSpellSelection.test.ts` for the exact template). - **`boundary/characterBio.ts`** — thin wrapper, same shape as every other tested boundary file: (1) `loadCharacterBio` outside a Tauri runtime resolves to `BLANK_CHARACTER_BIO` rather than throwing (the one behavior specific to this file vs. the others — bio's absent-case is a resolved default, not an error); (2) `updateCharacterBio` outside a Tauri runtime throws the exact descriptive message, matching the `addSpellSelection.test.ts` template. - **Wizard spell-routing logic** — currently inline in `CharacterSheet.tsx`'s `handleAddSpell`, not an extractable pure function today (unlike the other three, which already have clean module boundaries). Recommend extracting the two decisions it makes — (a) resolve `primaryClassId` preferring a held Wizard over `heldClasses[0]`, (b) choose `recordAndPrepareSpellSelection` vs. plain `addSpellSelection` based on that class id — into one small pure function (e.g. alongside `skillsModel.ts` or a new `spellRoutingModel.ts`), then test: a Fighter-only build routes to plain `addSpellSelection`; a Fighter/Wizard multiclass resolves to Wizard (not `heldClasses[0]`) and routes to the atomic path; a Wizard-only build routes to the atomic path. This is a slightly bigger lift than the other three (needs the extraction first) — flagging that distinction rather than treating all four as equal-sized tasks. - **`abilityScoreMethods.ts`** (found this pass, not previously named) — real, currently-untested logic: `pointBuyCost` at the table boundaries (7 and 18) and one in-range value; `generateAbilityScorePool` for each non-random `kind: 'pool'` method returns the right fixed values (`eliteArray` → `[15,14,13,12,10,8]` exactly) and the right *count* (6) for the randomized ones without asserting exact values; `rollStraightAbilityScores` maps its six rolls onto `ABILITY_KEYS` in the documented Str/Dex/Con/Int/Wis/Cha order, not any other order. The reroll-if-weak retry loop's 200-attempt cap is a defensive bound, not itself easily testable without mocking `Math.random` — reasonable to leave unverified rather than force a brittle test around it. - **`portraitImageProcessing.ts`** — lower priority, flagged for completeness rather than urged: the pure validation logic (`ACCEPTED_PORTRAIT_TYPES.includes`, the size-limit check) is testable today with a plain fake `File` object and no DOM, but the actual crop/resize path needs a `<canvas>`, which this `tsx`-based test runner doesn't provide — either accept partial coverage (just the two validation early-returns) or treat as out of scope for this backlog pass. **Not built this pass, deliberately** — this is a checklist, not new test files; QA's lane is `tests/**` (Rust), these are all frontend `.ts` modules. Owner: frontend, whenever the current queue is clear. **Checklist fully executed (frontend, `f905d656`).** All five modules covered per the exact cases named above: `skillsModel.ts` (parenthetical/multi-word normalization, class-skill boundary, multiclass union), `boundary/setSkillAllocations.ts` + `boundary/characterBio.ts` (standard no-runtime-throws template, Bio's absent-case-resolves-to-default behavior specifically verified), Wizard spell-routing (genuinely extracted into a new `spellRoutingModel.ts::resolveSpellRouting`, all 3 named cases plus 2 more — an already-bootstrapped Wizard routing to the plain path, zero-held-classes resolving to `null` rather than a fabricated id), `abilityScoreMethods.ts` (point-buy boundaries, `eliteArray`'s exact values, Str/Dex/Con/Int/Wis/Cha key order verified via insertion order), and `portraitImageProcessing.ts`'s two DOM-free validation cases as scoped. Since the spell-routing extraction touched real shipped code (`CharacterSheet.tsx`'s `handleAddSpell` now calls the new pure function instead of its old inline logic), frontend treated it as non-risk-free and live-verified it against the real dev build: adding a spell to an already-bootstrapped Wizard persisted correctly through the plain path, no stray Prepared entry, correct on-disk shape. 6 new test files, 1 new source file, 69/69 suite green, typecheck clean. **Independently re-verified, all 5 modules, extra scrutiny on the one that touched shipped code (QA, 2026-07-24).** Read the `CharacterSheet.tsx` diff directly and confirmed the spell-routing extraction is faithful and behavior-preserving — `resolveSpellRouting`'s output feeds the exact same downstream branches the old inline logic did, and it correctly delegates the bootstrap decision to the already-tested `isWizardSpellBootstrap` rather than duplicating that logic. resolved.title: RESOLVED — real bug fixed in Warpriest's Sacred Weapon dice count, found by scout's formula-audit pass, independently confirmed by the lead and re-verified by backend before fixing.
resolved.body: `warpriest_sacred_weapon_base_dice`'s own `dice_count` term used `level/20` — the `PREBASESIZELT:M` (smaller-than-Medium) branch's own denominator from `acg_abilities_class.lst` — transcribed by mistake into this function's applicable `PREBASESIZEEQ:M` (Medium) branch, a sibling-branch mix-up. The function's own doc comment also cited `/20` as if corpus-verified, so the error was internally self-consistent and would not have been caught by a doc-vs-code check alone — only a direct corpus re-read surfaced it. Corrected to the real EQ:M formula, `1+min(1,level/15)`. Real effect: a level 15-19 Warpriest previously got `dice_count=1` (wrong; `15/20` through `19/20` all floor to 0) instead of the correct `2` (`15/15=1`, `min(1,1)=1`, `+1=2`) — this closure's own bounded 1-3 level scope never diverged between the two denominators, so the bug was silently wrong only at level 15+, and only ever surfaced in the explanation's own prose text (never a separate `.value` field any existing test could have caught). New dedicated test `warpriest_sacred_weapon_dice_count_matches_the_real_eq_m_corpus_branch_at_every_level` covers the full level range including the previously-affected band, proven RED-then-GREEN against the real bug (reverted to `/20`, confirmed the new test fails, restored the fix, confirmed green) before landing. Full lib suite 489/489.

resolved.title: RESOLVED — Inquisitor Judgment deepened (backend, 2026-07-26, task #3), a genuine scoping correction found by re-verifying rather than trusting the original closure's own exclusion list.
resolved.body: Directed to widen Inquisitor beyond its single Justice judgment (item 8's third APG closure): checked the original scoping doc's "opponent/effect-dependent" exclusion of the other 7 judgment types directly against the raw corpus (`apg_abilities_class.lst`) rather than assuming the prior summary was right, and found it wrong for three of them. **Protection** (`1+InqJudgeProtectionLVL/5` sacred/profane bonus to Armor Class) and **Purity** (`1+InqJudgePurityLVL/5` sacred/profane bonus on all saving throws) are both flat, unconditional self-buffs with real live consumers already computed in this codebase (`baseline_armor_class`, `total_saves`) — identical shape to Justice's own attack-roll bonus, not opponent-dependent at all; the original doc had simply mis-grouped them. **Smiting** (`BONUS:VAR|InqJudgeSmitingLVL|InquisitorLVL`, no scaling) is a flat, level-independent boolean fact ("weapons count as magic for bypassing damage reduction"), grounded as a standalone explanation record since no numeric total exists to layer it onto — the same shape Brawler's Strike DR-bypass fact (item 39) already established. All three now ground alongside Justice via a widened `ground_or_block_inquisitor_judgment` (an if/else chain over all 4 recognized selections, each with its own `active_inquisitor_<type>_judgment_bonus`/formula function) — `choice:inquisitor_judgment` now recognizes 4 of the 8 real judgment types; the remaining 5 (Destruction, Healing, Piercing, Resiliency, Resistance) genuinely still need engine state that doesn't exist (a damage-roll total, round-tick HP state, a concentration/CL-check total, a DR-received facet distinct from Smiting's own DR-bypass-on-attack, and a chosen-energy-type mechanism plus energy-resistance state, respectively). Also grounded **Stern Gaze** (`max(1,level/2)` morale bonus, real unconditional level-1 feature, no choice/activation gate unlike Judgment) into `compute_selected_skill_modifiers`'s Intimidate total — only the Intimidate half of its real two-skill DESC lands, Sense Motive is not a skill this codebase computes anywhere, the same "ground only the computed half" discipline item 40's own Persuasive/Diplomacy split already established. `named_features_wired` rises from 1 to 2 for Inquisitor (Judgment slot + Stern Gaze slot — Judgment's own 4 sub-types stay one slot, per this repo's established "counts slots, not sub-options" convention already applied to Witch's own ~20-hex Ward count). 8 new/updated dispatch-widening tests (Protection/Purity/Smiting each applying their real bonus with no cross-leak into Justice's own attack-bonus consumer, an unbuilt-type-naming negative case distinct from the "no choice at all" case, and Stern Gaze's unconditional stacking), both SD-24 APG audit tests updated and green. Full lib suite 524/524 green (up from 519).

All three are unconditional (no choice/activation gate, same shape as Stern Gaze) and never claim-block. `named_features_wired` rises from 2 to 5 for Inquisitor (Judgment + Stern Gaze + Monster Lore + Cunning Initiative + Track, each a genuinely separate top-level `KEY:Inquisitor ~ ...` record). 3 new dispatch-widening tests (unconditional grounding, Track's own level-scaling formula proof, and a never-claim-blocks proof isolated from Judgment's own state), both SD-24 APG audit tests updated and green. resolved.title: RESOLVED — Skald Damage Reduction landed (backend, 2026-07-26, task #7), a genuine deepening the lead caught after re-reading Barbarian's own precedent directly.
resolved.body: After an initial pass concluded all 6 of Skald's remaining named features were subsystem-blocked (spellcasting had already landed in an earlier cycle, item unlogged until this entry's own doc fix), the lead pushed back specifically on Damage Reduction: Barbarian's own `class_feature.barbarian.damage_reduction` (`pilot_compute.rs:17478`) is exactly the same shape — a standalone, level-gated, flat-magnitude explanation record "never applied to any incoming-damage total" — so the absence of a shared/generic DR pillar doesn't block Skald from getting its own analogous standalone record, it just means no code gets reused (same as every other per-class flat fact this segment). Verified the real corpus DESC directly: "At 9th level, a skald gains damage reduction... At 14th and 19th level this damage reduction rises by 1 point" — DR 1/9th, 2/14th, 3/19th, identical shape to Barbarian's own. The ally-extension ("The skald grants this DR to all allies affected by his raging song") stays explicitly deferred, since this engine models no allies or ally-targeting mechanism at all — only the skald's own self-DR is grounded, the same "ground only the applicable half" discipline item 40's own Persuasive/Diplomacy split and item 41's own Stern Gaze Intimidate-half split already established. Also resolved `acg_skald_coverage.md`'s own long-open methodology question (whether known-spell-posture validation should bump `named_features_wired`) — it does not, per the same "shares the general spellcasting mechanism" convention already applied to Oracle/Arcanist/Warpriest/Inquisitor. `named_features_wired` rises from 1 to 2 for Skald (Inspired Rage + Damage Reduction). 3 new dispatch-widening tests (honest absence below level 9, progression through all three real level gates, and the other_features_deferred diagnostic acknowledging DR as grounded while still naming the ally-extension as missing), both SD-24 ACG audit tests updated and green. **Follow-up, same session:** the lead then confirmed Bardic Knowledge belonged in the same corrected scope (it needs a Knowledge-skill total exactly like Monster Lore did before item 42's correction), so it was landed in the same commit: `max(level/2,1)`, byte-identical to Bard's own already-shipped formula, grounded as a standalone flat competence bonus. `named_features_wired` rises again, from 2 to 3. Also caught and fixed, incidentally: an earlier edit had accidentally misattached one function's doc comment to a different function two declarations away (a copy-paste/insertion-order slip, not a logic bug — caught on re-read, fixed by moving the doc block back to its correct declaration) and quietly restored Skald's own remaining-feature naming from stale placeholder text ("Iron Will", "War Chant" — neither exists as a real corpus KEY record for Skald) to the real corpus names (Lore Master, Well-Versed, Dirge of Doom, Song of Marching/Strength/the Fallen). 2 more dispatch-widening tests, both SD-24 ACG audit tests updated and green again. resolved.title: RESOLVED — Investigator spellcasting subsystem landed (backend, 2026-07-26, task #8's main body), the shared Alchemist formula spell list this codebase needed for two separate class closures.
resolved.body: Wrote a dedicated scoping doc (`investigator-alchemist-spell-list-scoping.md`) before coding, per the established "scope a genuinely new subsystem before building it" discipline — the lead independently verified the key claims (104-record count, 14/25/20/16/14/15 level breakdown) byte-exact against `apg_spells.lst` before I started. New shared module `rules_tables::apg::alchemist_spell_list` (`ALCHEMIST_SPELL_LIST`, a `(&str, u8)` array mirroring `CLERIC_SPELL_LIST`'s own minimal shape) ingests all 104 real Alchemist formula records: 13 genuinely new Alchemist-only spells named directly in the corpus, plus 91 `.MOD` records that graft `Alchemist=N` onto existing Core Rulebook spells (the real spell name recovered by stripping `.MOD`; the Alchemist-specific level read directly off the same `.MOD` line, no cross-file lookup into `cr_spells.lst` needed since this shape carries no school/description). Deliberately scoped to `apg_spells.lst` alone, not the wider corpus (several other supplements also tag `Alchemist=N` on further spells) — the real PF1 rule text's own citation of "Advanced Player's Guide" as the canonical source matches the same single-book discipline every other spell list here already uses. Investigator's own casting shape confirmed as a prepared caster with no arcane-school mechanic (1 slot per prepared extract, like Arcanist, not Wizard's 2-slot rule); the corpus has no per-level `CAST:`/`KNOWN:` rows for Investigator at all (the same external-source caveat Hunter/Arcanist/Warpriest already had), so the real Extracts Prepared table was verified via THREE independent sources (aonprd.com, d20pfsrd.com's own Investigator page, d20pfsrd.com's own separate Alchemist page — which also independently confirmed a claim surfaced mid-search that Investigator's own table exactly mirrors Alchemist's), all agreeing byte-for-byte. **A deliberate, explicitly-flagged deviation from Wizard's/Arcanist's own level-1-3-bounded convention, confirmed correct in review before building**: that bound was an idiom inherited from the original GE-06 pilot slice (Arcanist's own doc comment says so explicitly — "mirrors Wizard's own bounded-scope discipline," not "unverified past level 3"), and the lead separately confirmed other classes (Barbarian, Monk) already widen past their own original bounds elsewhere in this codebase, so "stop at 3" was never a hard architectural ceiling. Since Investigator's own base chassis already supports all 20 levels and the full table is genuinely verified, this closure grounds the complete 1-20 range rather than an arbitrary 3-level slice. `unmet_investigator_extract_conditions`/`ground_investigator_prepared_extracts` mirror `unmet_arcanist_spellbook_conditions`/`ground_arcanist_prepared_spellbook` line-for-line (recorded vs. prepared extracts, no unrecorded prepared extract, no over-preparation, no inaccessible-level extract), plus the real extract save DC (`10 + extract level + INT modifier`, matching Arcanist's own DC shape, included per the lead's go-ahead). A valid extract posture (including zero known extracts, a valid PF1 posture per Bard's/Arcanist's own precedent) now clears its own dedicated `class_spell.acg.investigator.prepared_extracts.unsupported` diagnostic; Investigator still does not reach `Computed` overall (every other named feature remains claim-blocked via `other_features_deferred`, unaffected by this closure) -- the same "real validation, still Blocked on the rest" shape Arcanist had before its own separate Metamagic Knowledge closure. `named_features_wired` is unaffected (spellcasting doesn't add a count, per the established spellcasting-sharing convention already applied to every other partial caster this session). 7 new dispatch-widening tests plus 6 new `alchemist_spell_list`-internal tests, both SD-24 ACG audit tests confirmed unchanged and green. Full lib suite 569/569 green (up from 557). Alchemist's own consumption of this shared spell list (task #4) remains a separate, not-yet-started closure — the list module itself is immediately available for whoever picks that up next.

resolved.title: RESOLVED — Alchemist deepened (backend, 2026-07-26, task #4), flipping from "too big" to a genuinely tractable slice once Investigator's own shared spell-list leverage removed the original blocker.
resolved.body: Scout's fresh `alchemist-remaining-features-scoping.md` corrected the task note's own claim that Alchemist's casting is "formula-based, a different mechanic" from Investigator's — verified against the corpus and found byte-identical (`SPELLSTAT:INT MEMORIZE:YES SPELLBOOK:YES` for both), confirmed independently by the lead before greenlighting. **Bomb** (`KEY:Alchemist ~ Bomb`) is now fully wired — damage dice, save DC, and uses-per-day, all standalone facts since Bomb's own damage is a weapon-like magnitude against any target, not opponent-dependent (the same "groundable side of the Studied-Combat line" distinction Investigator's own Studied Combat/Strike stayed on the wrong side of). **The lead specifically flagged a sibling-branch hazard to verify carefully, the same shape the Sacred Weapon dice-count bug hid in** — and it was real: the corpus's own `AlchemistBombAdditionalDice` formula carries 10 conditional `-1` override branches at odd levels 3-19, each gated behind an `Alchemist_CF_BombDamage<N>` flag. Traced the flag's own definition and found it `DEFINE`s to `0` for the base Alchemist class and is ONLY ever set to `1` by two specific Ultimate Magic archetype feature grants (Psychonaut, Reanimator) — entirely out-of-scope splatbook/archetype content this codebase's own single-book, base-class-only build never reaches, so the 10 branches are provably vacuous for this closure's scope, not a hidden bug. A second `AlchemistBombTimes` contribution (`BonusBombCount/2`) was checked the same way and found equally vacuous (`BonusBombCount` only increments via a Gnome-specific Favored Class Bonus choice this engine models nowhere). **Poison Resistance** was re-derived independently (not copied from Investigator's own identical-shaped feature) and confirmed to share the exact same tiers, grounded as Alchemist's own separate copy per the established parallel-copy discipline. **Prepared extract spellcasting** now genuinely validated too, reusing the shared `alchemist_spell_list` module directly (Alchemist is the list's own namesake class) plus Alchemist's own extract-count table, re-verified against d20pfsrd.com's own separate Alchemist page and confirmed byte-identical to Investigator's. The old `class_feature.apg.alchemist.spellcasting_deferred.unsupported` diagnostic is retired in favor of a real `class_spell.apg.alchemist.prepared_extracts.unsupported` (spellcasting-specific) plus a renamed, narrower `other_features_deferred` (Discovery/Swift Alchemy/Swift Poisoning only). `named_features_wired` rises from 1 to 3 for Alchemist (Mutagen + Bomb + Poison Resistance — Bomb's own three numeric facets count as one slot, the same "one record, several parameters" shape Cleric's Channel Energy already established, not three separate slots). 19 new/updated dispatch-widening tests, both SD-24 APG audit tests updated and green. resolved.title: RESOLVED (backend, 2026-07-27, `73c70055`, lead-verified) — Bloodrager's shipped spellcasting diagnostic asserted something false and user-visible about the corpus (scout's `bloodrager-spellcasting-scoping.md`, 2026-07-27, task #1).
resolved.body: `push_bloodrager_spellcasting_deferred_diagnostic`'s message claims Bloodrager "has no class-skill list," but `acg_abilities_class.lst:331` grants one (`ABILITY:Class Skill|AUTOMATIC|Acrobatics|Climb|Craft|Handle Animal|Intimidate|Knowledge (Arcana)|Perception|Ride|Spellcraft|Survival|Swim`, 11 skills including all three of Climb/Intimidate/Swim — the 7th instance of the recurring class-skill-bonus widening bug). Worth recording the encoding trap that produced it: ACG classes carry zero `CSKILL:` tokens anywhere in `acg_classes.lst` — class skills live on a separate `<Class> ~ Class Skills` internal ability instead, so a `CSKILL:`-shaped search finds nothing and wrongly concludes the list is absent (scout's own first pass made this mistake before checking how Slayer's list was encoded). A second, related diagnostic defect in the same function: it claim-blocks unconditionally at every level, but Bloodrager has no `CAST:`/`KNOWN:` rows below level 4 at all (`BONUS:CASTERLEVEL|Bloodrager|Caster_Level_Bloodrager|PRECLASS:1,Bloodrager=4`, lead-verified directly against the corpus) — so a level 1-3 Bloodrager is claim-blocked today for a feature RAW says it doesn't have yet. Both landed in the first, standalone half of task #1: the diagnostic is now level-aware (`spellcasting_absent_by_level_gate`, non-claim-blocking, below level 4), and the false class-skill claim is corrected with the real 11-skill list grounded. Lead independently verified: 670/670 lib, 13/13 Bloodrager tests, ACG audit 3/3, clippy unchanged. `named_features_wired` rises 1→2 (Bloodrage + Spells) — not the originally-suggested 3, since `KEY:Bloodrager ~ Class Skills` is `CATEGORY:Internal`, the same as Warpriest's identical record which Warpriest's own count of 5 already excludes; confirmed against the corpus that no class in this segment has ever counted the class-skill-bonus widening fix as its own slot. The spell-list build (110-of-183) remains open, not part of this fix.

resolved.title: OPERATOR-EQUIVALENT DECISION (lead, 2026-07-27) — genuine PCGen corpus authoring bug in Swashbuckler Deeds, ruled fixable via level-source substitution (scout's `swashbuckler-finesse-and-deeds-scoping.md`, task #14).
resolved.body: `SwashbucklerDeedQualifyLVL` (the variable gating all six deed tiers, `PREVARGTEQ:SwashbucklerDeedQualifyLVL,{1,3,7,11,15,19}`) is `DEFINE`d to 0 and set by exactly one token in the entire ingested PCGen tree: `BONUS:VAR|SwashbucklerDeedQualifyLVL|MagusLVL|TYPE=Base`. It is never set from `SwashbucklerLVL`, confirmed absent from Swashbuckler's own two `CLASS:Swashbuckler` chassis lines too — lead independently re-verified this directly, not just trusted the doc. Taken literally, a pure single-class Swashbuckler qualifies for zero deeds at any level; only a Magus (via the deed-granting archetype) ever satisfies the gate. This is a genuine data-authoring gap in PCGen's own ACG dataset, not a misreading — the sibling variable `SwashbucklerDeedsLVL`, which the deed *magnitude* formulas actually consume, is correctly set from `SwashbucklerLVL` in the same file, and the gate thresholds (1/3/7 spot-checked) match RAW's own published deed tiers exactly. **Ruled: substituting `SwashbucklerLVL` as the gate's level source is a transcription fix, not fabrication** — the tier constants come straight from the corpus's own (correctly-set-elsewhere) gates, and the alternative (implementing the gate faithfully) would ship a core class feature that provably never functions for the class it belongs to. First time this segment a build knowingly deviates from what the corpus literally encodes; the deviation must carry an explicit code comment recording the corpus defect and this ruling, so it reads as a deliberate, documented fix rather than an unexplained departure from the established "ground exactly what the corpus says" discipline.

resolved.title: OPERATOR DECISION (2026-07-27) — REVERSES the 2026-07-26 "tag expensive blockers low-priority" policy. Blockers are the highest priority regardless of cost; swarm on one as soon as it's found, not after it's cheap.
resolved.body: The earlier prioritization pass (recorded in `SWARM_STATUS.md`, 2026-07-26) explicitly deprioritized Oracle/Witch/Shaman/Slayer/Swashbuckler/Monk/Warpriest and initially Bloodrager/Alchemist/Cavalier as "not cheap" or "needing a brand-new architecture pillar/mechanism this codebase doesn't have at all." **That reasoning is no longer the standing policy.** Cost/cheapness is not a reason to leave a blocker deprioritized — a real blocker gets swarmed on immediately, including the ones that need genuine new subsystem work (Monk's Deflect Arrows opponent-interaction engine, Slayer's Studied Target opponent-tracking pillar, Witch's/Shaman's Familiar subsystem), not just the ones a bounded slice can close cheaply. This directly followed a status check where the operator noted Monk's and Cavalier's blockers still showed as open on the dashboard despite a "clear the blockers" priority set 2026-07-26 — Cavalier's case turned out to be a stale cost estimate corrected same-day (task #6, closed); Monk's Deflect Arrows genuinely has not been touched, and under the old policy it would have stayed that way indefinitely. Going forward: no remaining class blocker (full list currently: Witch/Shaman spellcasting+Familiar, Slayer's opponent-tracking pillar, Swashbuckler — now closed — Monk's Deflect Arrows engine, Summoner's evolution-spending economy) should be left unscoped or unscheduled solely because it needs new architecture rather than a grounding pass.

resolved.title: METHODOLOGY CORRECTION (lead, 2026-07-27) — the standalone-grounding bar's "opponent-dependent" exclusion was over-broad; corrected to distinguish an unmodelled CIRCUMSTANCE from an unmodelled QUANTITY (scout's `opponent-interaction-architecture-design.md`, tasks #13/#15).
resolved.body: Explicitly reverses the lead's own earlier ruling that Studied-Target-shaped features (a bonus that only applies against a specific opponent) need a real opponent-tracking pillar and stay deferred. Scout found the inconsistency by re-deriving every relevant formula from the corpus: Slayer's Studied Target (`SlayerLVL/5+1`), Investigator's Studied Combat (`InvestigatorLVL/2`) and Studied Strike (`min(9,(InvestigatorLVL-2)/2)`d6), and Cavalier's Challenge damage (`+CavalierLVL`) read ONLY the character's own level — none touches any property of the opponent (AC, HD, type, state). The opponent is a *scope condition* on when the bonus applies, not an *input* to computing its magnitude. **The precedent that settles it was already shipped, inside Slayer's own class**: `class_feature.acg.slayer.sneak_attack_dice` is already grounded as a standalone record despite Sneak Attack being conditional on flanking or a denied-Dexterity target — an opponent relationship this engine models nowhere — and its own detail text says so explicitly ("grounded as a standalone record only"). Lead independently re-verified this directly in the code before ruling. **Corrected line, to replace the old blanket "opponent-dependent defers": a magnitude conditional on an unmodelled CIRCUMSTANCE grounds as a standalone, explicitly-scoped fact (Sneak Attack, Trap Sense, Studied Target, Studied Combat/Strike, Challenge damage); a magnitude that needs an unmodelled QUANTITY belonging to the opponent (their AC, HD, save, or other property as a term in the formula) still defers.** Ruled Tier 0 (ground as scoped standalone facts, no total-folding, no new architecture) for all four affected features across three classes — Slayer (new), Investigator (deepening of already-closed task #8), Cavalier (deepening of already-closed task #6). Tier 1 (folding into computed totals via the existing `ClassAbilityActivation` primitive Rage already uses) deferred as a follow-on, not required now. **This correction does NOT reach Monk's Deflect Arrows**, which fails a different test entirely — zero `BONUS` token exists anywhere in the corpus for it, so there is no magnitude to ground under either the old or corrected bar; closing it for real would need a full attack-resolution pipeline (a product decision on real combat resolution, out of scope for one feat, tracked separately from this correction).

resolved.title: RESOLVED — item 53's fix had a second, independent bug, found by backend holding #27 instead of shipping a number that happened to match. Ruling: PREVAREQ/optional-rule-gated spells belong on the list (extends item 53's reasoning).
resolved.body: The `CLASSES:` token parse item 53 fixed handles `Name1,Name2=N` correctly but not a trailing bracketed prereq — `CLASSES:Sorcerer,Witch,Wizard=3[PREVAREQ:Heroic,1]` — where `int(level)` throws and a swallowed `except ValueError: continue` silently drops the whole record, the same invisible-omission shape as the substring bug with a different root cause. Backend found it because Paladin's own re-derivation landed at 94 against the already-queued 95 and it checked the gap instead of concluding the queued number was stale (task #26's own lesson, applied). **The lead independently re-derived all nine affected classes with a bracket-stripping fix, and separately caught a bug in its own first re-check** (a quick script that didn't strip `.MOD` suffixes counted `"Resounding Blow"` and `"Resounding Blow.MOD"` as two different spells, inflating Paladin to a wrong 96) — corrected before reporting back, not shipped. Confirmed figures, all independently reproduced: Witch 324→**326** (Malediction, Unravel Destiny — reopens task #23, filed as task #33), Sorcerer 576→**578** (same two spells, corrected on tasks #30/#31 before backend builds them), Cleric 298→**301** (Heroic Fortune (Mass), Severed Fate, Unravel Destiny — plain "Heroic Fortune" was already correctly captured, its Cleric-facing group is unbracketed), Paladin queued number (95) unaffected in total but the correct *set* includes Heroic Fortune, not a phantom `.MOD`-suffix duplicate. Ranger/Bard/Druid/Alchemist/Bloodrager confirmed unaffected by either bug. **Ruling, extending item 53's "reachability over sourcebook" logic**: `[PREVAREQ:Heroic,1]`-gated spells (the APG Hero Points optional rule — a real, ingested, corpus-reachable spell, unlike Bloodrager's 73 genuinely unreachable entries) belong on the list. The gate is a condition on *casting* (does this table run the optional rule), not on *list membership* (can this class ever draw on this spell) — this engine enforces no spell-selection prerequisites today (list membership + level ceiling + slot budget only), so grounding the spell as list-present and leaving the gate unenforced is the same honest-standalone idiom already established for Studied Combat's own unenforced duration (item 46) and every other "real, reachable, but conditionally gated" fact this segment has chosen to represent rather than hide.

resolved.title: RULING (lead, 2026-07-27) — Shaman's level-11 spells-per-day row stays as the corpus states it, `4,4,4,3,3,2,1`; do NOT substitute Cleric/Druid/Wizard/Witch's shared `4,4,4,4,3,2,1`.
resolved.body: Backend (task #12, stage 2) flagged a genuine single-cell divergence: Shaman's own `CAST:` rows in `acg_classes.lst` are byte-identical to all four peer full 9th-level casters at levels 10 and 12, but diverge at 11 — Shaman gains its 4th 3rd-level spell slot one level later than every peer. Lead independently re-checked all three rows directly against the raw corpus (`acg_classes.lst` lines under `###Block: Shaman` vs `cr_classes.lst` under Cleric) and confirmed byte-for-byte: this is real, not a transcription artifact of backend's own reading. **The deciding factor is the absence of an internal contradiction.** Swashbuckler's Deed gate (item 50) was ruled a genuine corpus defect because a *sibling* variable (`SwashbucklerDeedsLVL`) was correctly set from `SwashbucklerLVL` in the same file while the gate variable wasn't — proof the corpus's own data was internally inconsistent with itself. No such proof exists here: Shaman's own level-11 row is internally monotonic (3rd-level slots go 3→3→4 across levels 10-11-12, never dipping), and nothing else in the class block contradicts it. A single class differing from its peers on one cell is not itself evidence of an authoring error — PF1 classes routinely have small, deliberate table differences from their nearest peers as part of their own design. Per the standing "ground exactly what the corpus says, deviate only on proven internal contradiction" discipline (established across items 50 and the whole spell-list wave, items 53-54), the corpus value stands. Backend already pinned this with a test (`shaman_level_11_follows_the_corpus_not_the_peer_row`) asserting both the value used AND the peer value NOT used, with a comment naming exactly what to do if this ruling is ever reversed on real evidence (a published errata, a PCGen upstream fix) — that test needs no further change under this ruling. Also confirms two design choices from the same stage as correct: deriving the access ceiling from the slot table itself (`shaman_spell_level_access` calls `rposition` on `shaman_base_spells_per_day_table` rather than duplicating threshold constants, preventing the two tables from drifting apart) and proving the spellcasting wiring live end-to-end through `build_pilot_headless_receipt` rather than only unit-testing the pure functions.

resolved.title: RESOLVED — the Witch/Shaman familiar-count asymmetry (66b8aae9) is a population of one, not a class of bugs. Backend swept the codebase and found a sharp, checkable criterion for when this shape can even occur.
resolved.body: Enumerated all 62 `ground_*` functions, generalized to every locally-defined, non-class-named helper called from two or more distinct class contexts (9 helpers), and triaged each. Most are pure arithmetic (`ability_bonus_spells`, `ability_modifier_for`) or feat-effects layered onto existing totals, not class features with their own count. Two findings worth recording as standing methodology, both lead-independently spot-checked: (1) `effective_combat_feat_intelligence_score` is shared by Brawler's Cunning and Swashbuckler's Finesse but implements **two distinct features** that happen to need the same `max(a,b)` arithmetic — confirmed exactly two production call sites (`pilot_compute.rs:16307`/`:13600`), each independently crediting its own count (9/12) in separate match arms; a shared *formula* used by two features is not the same hazard as a shared *feature* credited by two classes, since only the latter has a single fact two rows must agree about. (2) `ground_wolf_companion_stat_block` is shared by Druid/Hunter but **cannot produce this asymmetry at all** — `named_features_wired` coverage audits exist only for APG and ACG (confirmed: no `sd24_crb_class_coverage_audit.rs` exists anywhere in `tests/`), so Druid has no coverage row for Hunter's to disagree with. **The resulting criterion, sharper than "watch for shared mechanisms"**: a counting asymmetry requires one feature-grounding helper (not arithmetic) shared by two classes that both have coverage rows (both APG or both ACG). Exactly one helper in the codebase meets both conditions — `ground_familiar_master_benefit` — and it's already fixed. Backend is adding a guard test asserting both familiar-sharing classes credit it, so a future third consumer of `Standard Familiar List` can't silently repeat this. Worth reusing this criterion directly when scoping any future class that reuses an existing class's mechanism, rather than re-deriving it.

resolved.title: RESOLVED — #16-adjacent scoping (task #34, backend, investigation only): the two-skill General-feat gap is genuinely empty; the real remaining gaps are Master Craftsman and a mis-scoped "Focus-feat chooser" framing.
resolved.body: Enumerated `feat_data/general.rs` exhaustively rather than eyeballing it — lead independently re-verified: **50 total General feats, 12 carry any `SKILL` qualifier, exactly 10 are two-skill.** All 10 are correctly triaged already: 8 fully standalone in `STANDALONE_TWO_SKILL_FACTS` (Acrobatic/Alertness/Animal Affinity/Deceitful/Deft Hands/Magical Aptitude/Self-Sufficient/Stealthy), Persuasive correctly split (Diplomacy standalone, Intimidate integrated), Athletic correctly absent (both Climb and Swim are computed skills, no standalone remainder needed). The premise that makes the split/absence correct rather than lucky — `compute_selected_skill_modifiers` computes exactly Climb/Intimidate/Swim, confirmed directly in its own diagnostic message — was verified, not assumed. **One real gap found**: `Master Craftsman` (`BONUS:SKILL|LIST|2` + a ranks-tracking var, a single chosen Craft/Profession skill) has zero handling anywhere — not two-skill, not Skill Focus-shaped, fell through both existing categories. Confirmed zero references anywhere in `src/rules_core`. **On the Focus-feat question, the framing in #16's own description was wrong, and backend corrected it rather than answer the literal question asked**: the chooser mechanism is not the gap — `skill_focus_facts_from_choices`/`spell_focus_facts_from_choices`/`weapon_focus_facts_from_choices` already exist, all three sharing one proven `choice:<feat>_target` shape, lead-confirmed all three functions exist. **The actual blocker is the destination**: every spell-save-DC id in the engine is keyed by spell *level*, never by school (lead confirmed: every `*save_dc*` id found is `spell_level_{n}`/`extract_level_{n}`-shaped, zero school-keyed), so Spell/Greater Spell Focus can only ever ground standalone — the same "no total exists to integrate into" reasoning that correctly kept Spell Focus deferred on #22. Weapon Focus is worse: zero `attack.*` explanation ids exist anywhere in the engine (lead confirmed directly), so there is no per-weapon attack total at all, not even a narrow one. Weapon Specialization, Greater Weapon Specialization, and Improved Critical share the identical no-destination story (lead confirmed: only named as a prerequisite string or comment reference, no grounding producer for any of the three). **Recommendation, for whoever picks up #16 next (featmate)**: Master Craftsman is the one cheap remaining two-skill-shaped widening (existing standalone-fact idiom, no new architecture); the Focus-feat threads should be re-scoped as a genuine product decision — "does this engine want a school-keyed spell-save-DC pillar / a per-weapon attack total" — rather than treated as a feat-effects widening task, since the chooser half was never the blocker.

resolved.title: RESOLVED — the roster survey's `class_feature.*`-only methodology (item 59's own near-miss, recurring) undercounted CRB classes systematically; corrected pick is Summoner, not Monk/Paladin.
resolved.body: Scout's fast survey ranked Monk/Paladin as the biggest gaps by comparing corpus records against grounded `class_feature.*` ids alone. Lead checked both directly and found CRB classes ground most chassis-level features under a second prefix, `class_chassis.<class>.*`, entirely unsearched: Paladin already has ~21-24 grounded ids (Divine Grace, Lay on Hands, Smite Evil, Channel Positive Energy, Mercy, three Auras, Holy Champion, partial spellcasting), Monk ~18-20 (AC Bonus, Ki Pool, Slow Fall, Diamond Body, Purity of Body, Flurry of Blows, Unarmed Strike damage die, Evasion family). Neither was close to the near-zero/skeletal state first reported — dispatching either would have meant rebuilding working code. Scout re-derived across all three id-bearing prefixes known at the time (`class_feature` 649, `class_chassis` 256, `class_spell` 115, whole-tree count — **a fourth, `class.<name>.*`, was found later, task #40, and is folded into the addendum below; treat "three" in this sentence as a historical snapshot, not the current count**) and corrected the pick to **Summoner**: 6-7 remaining features (Bond Senses, Maker's Call, Merge Forms, Twin Eidolon, Summon Monster, Aspect/Greater Aspect), only reachable now that the Eidolon MVP (task #17) landed — the pool sizes are self-scoped facts needing nothing from the eidolon's own stat block, the fourth instance this segment of "the creature is not an input to the mechanic" (after Studied Target, the familiar's master benefit, the spell store). **Lead independently re-verified every cited formula directly against `apg_abilities_class.lst` before greenlighting** (own first two grep attempts gave false negatives from imprecise syntax — worth naming, the same trap as always: a query that looks precise and misses can produce high-confidence wrong answers): `BONUS:VAR|BondSensesRounds|classlevel("Summoner")`, `MakersCallTimes|((classlevel("Summoner")-2)/4)`, `MergeFormsRounds|classlevel("Summoner")`, `TwinEidolonMinutes|classlevel("Summoner")`, `SummonMonsterDuration|classlevel`, `SummonMonsterTimes|CHA+3`, `SummonMonsterLVL|min(9,(classlevel+1)/2)` — all confirmed exact. **One real correction to scout's own description**: Aspect/Greater Aspect are not a flat `ABILITYPOOL of 1` — `BONUS:VAR|EidolonAspect|{1,1,1,2,2,2,3,3}` sets real corpus-encoded point costs, and the ability grants a "divert N points from the eidolon's evolution pool, add N evolutions to yourself" chooser tied directly into the shared, still-deferred evolution pool. The point costs are flat and corpus-real (not subsystem-blocked the way the full evolution economy is), but this is a canonical-narrowing candidate (Oracle's-Mysteries shape), not an independent flat fact like the other four. Scout cleared to write the full Summoner scoping doc with this correction folded in. **Second methodology-gap catch of the same session in the same lane (item 59, then this)** — worth treating "which id prefixes exist" as a checked fact before any future roster survey, not assumed from one file's convention. **Addendum (scout, 2026-07-27): the durable form of this rule is "enumerate the prefixes, don't name them."** Naming "two" or "three" prefixes in a doc (as the lead did, informally, in a later chat message) just moves the staleness rather than removing it — a fourth prefix appearing later would silently repeat this exact bug. One-line check that can't go stale: `grep -oh '"[a-z_]*\.[a-z0-9_.]*"' | cut -d. -f1 | sort | uniq -c`. Lead independently re-ran an equivalent enumeration directly (`grep -rohE` across `src/rules_core/`) and confirmed `class_spell` is a real, substantially-sized third prefix (100+ ids, not noise) — every future roster survey should run this enumeration fresh rather than assume the prefix list from any prior doc, including this one.

resolved.title: RESOLVED — scout's `stale-deferral-sweep.md` found a genuine self-inconsistency in the codebase's own DR-grounding reasoning (item 52 follow-on): 3 flat `DR:N/-` records grounded standalone, 2 identical-shape records deferred on the exact reasoning item 52 already overturned. Ruled: split across three tracks rather than one bundled task.
resolved.body: Triggered by featmate's Monk audit (item 61) surfacing High Jump/Wholeness of Body as deferred under the pre-item-52 bar. Scout swept `pilot_compute.rs` for deferral language and found the DR family specifically inconsistent: Barbarian's (`DR:BarbarianDR/-`), Skald's (`DR:SkaldDamageReduction…`), and Fighter's Armor Mastery (`DR:5/-`, `ARMOR_MASTERY_DAMAGE_REDUCTION = 5`) are all grounded as flat standalone facts, while Paladin's Aura of Righteousness (`DR:5/Evil`, level 17) is deferred citing "no damage-reduction-application engine exists to apply this to" — the identical consumer-absence reasoning Skald's own grounded record explicitly names and rejects. Monk's Perfect Self (`DR:10/Chaotic`, level 20) has zero code hits anywhere, not even a deferred record. **Lead independently re-verified every corpus token directly against `cr_abilities_class.lst`** (`DR:10/Chaotic` for Perfect Self, `DR:5/Evil` for Aura of Righteousness, both exact) and confirmed Paladin's own shipped comment cites the consumer-absence reasoning verbatim (lines 387/449/456), and that Monk's Fast Movement/Maneuver Training/High Jump/Wholeness of Body/Perfect Self all still show zero `pilot_compute.rs` hits as of the sweep. **Scout's own ranking, adopted as-is**: cross-checked scout's proposed split against the standing "bounded, one-clear-thing-per-task" discipline (Investigator's pre-slice/main-body split, Alchemist's deepening) rather than the alternative (one bundled "make DR consistent" closure) — bundling reads cleaner in the doc but has no owner advantage here, since the three features are already naturally split across different lanes. **Ruling**: (1) Paladin's Aura of Righteousness DR — the only one not already attached to in-flight or future work — filed as its own standalone task (#38), dispatched to whoever frees up next; three in-codebase precedents, one flat value, no new design. (2) Monk's Perfect Self DR folded directly into the already-in-progress task #36 (same file, same session, same flat-DR pattern as Fast Movement/Maneuver Training/High Jump/Wholeness of Body — no separate dispatch needed); its own level-20 gate sits above `MAX_SUPPORTED_MONK_LEVEL = 12`, so task #36 must also settle whether the cap widens for this one feature or Perfect Self grounds as a scoped-but-currently-unreachable fact (Master Craftsman's 5-rank-prereq precedent). (3) Bloodrager's own `DR:BloodragerDR/-` filed as its own future-pass task (#39), left low-priority per scout's own recommendation rather than urgently dispatched — no active Bloodrager work to fold it into. (4) Bloodline/spirit DR sub-entries (`Aberrant Form 5/-`, `Soul of the Fey 10/cold iron`, `Deep One 10/piercing`, `Strength of Stone 10/adamantine`, Shaman's Stone/Bones spirit DRs) deferred further, lower priority — chooser-shaped, one mechanism per class rather than per record, no active chooser pass underway to fold them into. resolved.body: Featmate staged `pilot_compute.rs` by explicit path for their own Paladin work; the file also contained backend's finished-but-uncommitted Bloodrager DR (`bloodrager_damage_reduction_amount`, `ground_bloodrager_damage_reduction`, both gate branches, the negative-value clamp, 5 dedicated tests) at that moment, and it rode along under the Paladin commit message. **Lead independently confirmed directly**: `e076c8ad`'s `pilot_compute.rs` diff is 166 added lines, of which 39 reference Bloodrager and only 1 references Paladin (backend's own doc-comment comparing the two DR shapes) — the commit's actual code content is almost entirely Bloodrager's, with Paladin's real grounding (`class_chassis.paladin.damage_reduction`) having landed in an earlier, separate part of the diff. Re-verified in an isolated worktree: 844/844 lib, both SD-24 audits 3/3 — this is item 64's same number, now correctly attributed: the discrepancy was never a remembered-number error, it was the tree genuinely containing 5 more tests than the commit message described because of whose work was actually staged. **Both agents independently found and reported this without prompting** — featmate by re-diagnosing their own "why 839 twice" question against saved raw test-run logs rather than accepting a surface explanation, backend by comparing the shipped diff against what they'd actually built. Two further self-corrections worth recording: featmate had been treating "staged only my file, explicit path" as sufficient isolation all session — it isn't, since an explicit path still stages a co-resident agent's uncommitted edits in the same file; the actual discipline is `git diff <file>` review or `git add -p` before staging, and worktree isolation (already used for Summoner Slice A) sidesteps the hazard entirely, which is why that commit contained only its own author's work. Featmate also found a second-order consequence: staging happened after their own `cargo test` run but after backend added ~5 more tests to the same file, so the commit shipped code whose test run predated part of what was actually committed — the totals not reconciling (839+3≠842) was the tell that should have triggered a re-check sooner. **Ruling: do not rewrite history.** The branch is shared and pushed, the code is correct and fully verified either way, and this repo's own git safety protocol treats history rewrites on shared branches as a last resort. Fixed via tracking instead: task #39 marked completed with a provenance note pointing at `e076c8ad`; task #42 (Bloodrager's remaining features) corrected from 7 items to 6, explicitly told not to rebuild DR. **Standing lesson for the rest of this swarm**: on a shared single checkout, `git status`/`git diff <file>` before every `git add`, not just before every `git commit` — the window where a same-file collision can occur is between "I finished my own change" and "I looked at what's actually staged," and an explicit path alone does not close it.

resolved.body: `inquisitor-remaining-features-scoping.md`: the dominant remaining item is spellcasting (219 spells per scout, fully ingested, spontaneous, own list — not a chooser, not thin), with Bane and a Sacred/Profane Judgment widening as the genuinely small remainder. **Real methodology finding, independently confirmed**: Stern Gaze is already grounded (`inquisitor_stern_gaze_intimidate_bonus`/`active_inquisitor_stern_gaze_bonus`, lead-confirmed exact at `pilot_compute.rs:10159`/`:10170`) but produces no explanation record because it feeds the computed Intimidate total directly rather than standing alone — so item 60/63's id-count roster method systematically undercounts any class whose wins landed as total-integrations, biasing against exactly the highest-value kind of work. **Widened by item 69's Skald finding to cover the inverse direction too**: a bare name-grep across classes that share a feature name (Bard's own Lore Master/Versatile Performance, Barbarian's own Rage Powers) makes an *ungrounded* Skald feature look already-covered, the opposite failure mode from Stern Gaze's undercounting. Same root cause both ways — matching on a name or id without checking what it's actually scoped to — so the durable rule isn't "id counts are a floor" specifically, it's "verify scope, not just presence," in either direction. Worth carrying forward whenever a future roster survey runs. **CORRECTION — the 219-vs-222 gap was the lead's own script bug, not scout's count. 219 is confirmed correct.** Scout re-audited independently rather than deferring to the lead's number, verified their own 219 four ways (only two files carry an Inquisitor `CLASSES:` entry at all; 220 raw occurrences dedupe to 219 unique names via exactly one base/`.MOD` pair, `Resounding Blow`, both level 5; zero names appear at more than one level; zero substring-only false matches), and could account for exactly one of the lead's three extra spells (the level-5 cell) but not the other two — reported that honestly rather than claiming outright victory. **Lead re-ran the script with per-spell output rather than just totals and found the real bug**: three `#`-prefixed lines (`#Corruption Resistance`, `#Defile Armor`, `#Commune (Greater).MOD`) were being counted as active spell records. In this corpus's own convention a leading `#` marks a disabled/commented-out duplicate — confirmed directly: the *real* active `Corruption Resistance` record (no `#`) carries `CLASSES:Antipaladin,Paladin=2`, no Inquisitor at all, while the disabled `#`-prefixed duplicate carries `CLASSES:Antipaladin=2|Inquisitor=2|Paladin=2`. Excluding `#`-prefixed lines, the lead's script produces **219, with the identical per-level breakdown as scout's** (15/38/43/44/35/24/20) — exact match. Scout's number was right; the lead's original script had a real, previously-unflagged parsing bug (not yet known to affect any of the other nine already-shipped spell lists — worth a quick sweep for `#`-prefixed false positives across those before assuming they're clean, since this is a new bug class, not a repeat of the comma-group/bracket bugs items 53/54 already fixed). Task #47 updated to build from 219 directly rather than re-deriving from scratch. Confirmed independently: Inquisitor's class line carries no `SPELLLIST` token (own list, no reuse possible, unlike Hunter), the Bane formula (`BONUS:VAR|InquisitorBanePool|InquisitorLVL`) is exact, and Sacred/Profane Judgment's four extra types route through the already-built Judgment execution path.

resolved.title: RULING REVERSED (featmate, lead-ratified after independent verification) — item 63's option (b) for task #41 is not actually available: it would ship provably dead code, not a "scoped but unreachable" fact. Deferring #41 for real, with a properly scoped follow-on filed for the cap question.
resolved.body: Item 63 posed the choice as (a) widen `MAX_SUPPORTED_MONK_LEVEL` or (b) ground Perfect Self as scoped-but-currently-unreachable, citing Master Craftsman's 5-rank-prereq precedent. Featmate traced the actual dispatch path before building and found the precedent doesn't hold: every Monk feature (all four of #36's, and any Perfect Self branch) lives inside `explain_monk_level1_chassis`, which starts with `let Some(level) = supported_monk_level(input) else { return; }` — and `supported_monk_level` only returns `Some` for `(1..=MAX_SUPPORTED_MONK_LEVEL).contains(&level)`, `MAX_SUPPORTED_MONK_LEVEL = 12`. An `if level >= 20` branch placed there **can never execute under any input the dispatch admits** — not "no legal character reaches it," but the code path itself is dead, unreachable even by a test exercising the real pipeline. Master Craftsman's producer genuinely runs (tests call it and it returns the fact); what's unreachable there is a *character* satisfying its prereq, not the *code*. Categorically different, and the no-stub doctrine rules out the dead-code shape directly. **Lead independently re-verified the trace**: confirmed the early-return guard, confirmed `supported_monk_level`'s exact range check, and confirmed via the next top-level `fn` boundary (`supported_rogue_level` at line 25119) that `explain_monk_level1_chassis` spans lines 23757–25118, comfortably containing all four #36 features and where a Perfect Self branch would have to live. **Ratified: option (b) as originally framed, defer #41 honestly** (the DR magnitude and gate are correctly verified and recorded, `DR:10/Chaotic` at level 20, plus a separate no-magnitude Outsider-type clause that stays deferred regardless — same clean-split shape as Paladin's aura) — closed as correctly-deferred-not-built rather than left open indefinitely, per this session's own standing convention that an honest "cannot be built as scoped" is a legitimate closure. **Filed the cap question as its own properly bounded task** rather than as a side effect of one DR fix, matching the Summoner Slice A/B precedent: widening `MAX_SUPPORTED_MONK_LEVEL` to 20 admits Diamond Soul (13), Quivering Palm (15), Timeless Body (17, partially present), Tongue of the Sun and Moon (17), Empty Body (19), and Perfect Self (20) — six genuinely new, currently entirely-ungrounded features — plus it makes every already-shipped Monk formula (Fast Movement's own comment scopes itself explicitly to "+40 at 12") start emitting at levels 13–20 where none has ever been verified, so the real cost is a verified pass across eight new levels, not a one-line constant change. **One correction to featmate's own count**: Abundant Step (level 12) is already inside the current `1..=12` range and is a separate pre-existing gap, not newly admitted by widening — cheap to bundle into the same pass since it's adjacent, but not part of what the cap change itself unlocks. **Follow-up sweep, same session**: checked whether the same `#`-prefixed-disabled-record bug touched any of the nine already-shipped spell lists. Only one hit across all nine: Paladin's `Corruption Resistance` also appears in the same disabled `#Corruption Resistance` duplicate. Confirmed benign — the record's own *active* (non-`#`) version independently carries `CLASSES:Antipaladin,Paladin=2`, so Paladin's already-shipped inclusion at level 2 (`paladin_spell_list.rs:74`) is correct regardless of whether the disabled duplicate was ever consulted. No fix needed on any of the nine shipped lists. The bug only produced a wrong result for Inquisitor specifically because Inquisitor appears *exclusively* in the disabled duplicate, with no corresponding grant on the active record. **Generalized technique (scout, recorded for reuse), from the Raging Song resolution (item 69): when a corpus token and shipped code disagree and no primary source is trustworthy in the moment, find a third feature whose corpus token and shipped code already agree and are structurally related to the disputed pair — the authoring convention that reconciles the agreeing pair usually adjudicates the disagreeing one, using only in-repo evidence.** This is what solved Skald's Raging Song (Bard's Bardic Performance, named as a sibling by Skald's own DESC text, revealed the corpus's `-2`-offset authoring convention and settled which side had the defect) without touching RAW memory at all. Caveat carried over from item 69: the disagreement can be three-way (both corpus and code wrong relative to a real primary source), so resolve every candidate against the same one reference rather than pairwise. **Also worth stating as one rule rather than two**: the fifth id prefix found in item 71 (`ability_modifier.<class>.*`) and the Stern Gaze finding (item 67) are the same phenomenon — a consumer-integration record — surfacing twice under different names. The durable form: any feature whose value feeds directly into another computed total, rather than standing as its own explanation record, is invisible to id-count and prefix-enumeration surveys alike, regardless of how many prefixes get enumerated.

resolved.title: RESOLVED — task #48 (Skald scoping) landed with a real "shipped bug" flag, which fully resolves in the shipped code's favor via a proven in-corpus internal contradiction (same precedent class as item 50's Swashbuckler deed gate). No code fix needed; the corpus's own raw token has the defect.
resolved.body: Scout found Skald's shipped `skald_inspired_rage_rounds_per_day` (`3 + CHA + 2*(level-1)`, i.e. `1 + CHA + 2*level`) disagrees with the corpus's raw `BONUS:VAR|SkaldRagingSongRoundsPerDay|3+CHA+(2*SkaldLVL)` token by a uniform `-2` at every level, and deliberately declined to rule which side was right, flagging real recollection-based RAW answers as unreliable today and recommending resolution against one primary source rather than a pairwise guess. **Lead resolved it without any RAW recollection, using a cross-check already sitting in the repo.** Skald's own corpus DESC text says explicitly "counts as the bard's bardic performance special ability for any effect that affects bardic performances" — so Bard's own Bardic Performance rounds-per-day is a structurally identical sibling record, already shipped and already lead-verified this session. Bard's corpus token is `BONUS:VAR|BardicPerformanceDuration|2+CHA+(2*BardicPerformanceLVL)` and its shipped formula is `4 + CHA + 2*(level-1)` — algebraically identical (`4+2*(L-1) ≡ 2+2*L` for all L, confirmed by direct computation at L=1,2,3,20). **The corpus's own authoring convention for this exact shape is: token-constant = DESC-prose-base minus 2, because the token multiplies by `level` directly while the prose's "+2 per level after 1st" implies `level-1`.** Applying that same convention to Skald: DESC-prose-base is 3 ("3 + his Charisma modifier" at 1st level, explicit in the DESC text), so a correctly-authored token would read `1+CHA+(2*SkaldLVL)` — not the `3+CHA+(2*SkaldLVL)` actually shipped in the corpus. **The shipped Rust code already matches the DESC prose and the sibling Bard's correct authoring pattern exactly; it is the corpus's raw `BONUS:VAR` token for Skald specifically that has the transcription defect** (missing the `-2` offset applied correctly everywhere else in this same family). Confirmed directly: shipped/DESC values at levels 1/2/3/20 are 3/5/7/41; the raw corpus token gives 5/7/9/43 (a consistent `+2`); the correctly-offset-like-Bard value would be 3/5/7/41 — matching the shipped code exactly. **Ruling: no code change. `SKALD_RAGING_SONG_BASE_ROUNDS_PER_DAY` and its formula are already correct and stay as-is** — but per item 50's own standard, this deviation-from-the-literal-token must carry an explicit code comment recording the corpus defect and this ruling (currently the comment only says "verified against the PCGen corpus DESC text," with no mention of the token disagreement or why the token was correctly not followed) — filed as the first item in task #50. **Rest of #48 confirmed real**: five flat magnitudes remain — Well-Versed (`SkaldWellVersedBonus = 4`, exact precedent match to Bard's own identical `BARD_WELL_VERSED_BONUS = 4`), Spell Kenning (`(1+SkaldLVL)/6`), Lore Master (`min((SkaldLVL-1)/6,3)`, a proper two-argument `min`), Versatile Performance (`BONUS:ABILITYPOOL|Skald Versatile Performance|min((SkaldLVL+3)/5)` — genuinely single-argument, confirmed directly; the `(SkaldLVL+3)/5` term alone already matches the DESC's own grant schedule exactly (1 at level 2-6, 2 at 7-11, 3 at 12-16), so ground the formula as its own value rather than inventing a second cap operand, per scout's own caution), Rage Powers (count, Barbarian cross-class leverage). **Name-collision methodology finding, independently confirmed**: `grep -i skald.*lore_master\|versatile_performance\|rage_power\|well_versed` returns zero hits in `pilot_compute.rs` — none of the four are currently grounded for Skald despite Bard/Barbarian owning same-named features, confirming scout's flag that a bare name-grep would have wrongly shown Skald as already covered. **This is the inverse of item 67's Stern Gaze finding** (there, an id-count made a grounded feature invisible; here, a name-match makes ungrounded features look grounded) — both are instances of the same underlying rule, "check what a name or id is actually scoped to, not just whether it exists somewhere in the codebase." Item 67 widened to name both directions explicitly rather than just the undercounting one. Dispatched the five-feature build (plus the Raging Song comment fix) as task #50.
