resolved.title: RESOLVED — task #53 (Rage Powers canonical-narrowing scoping) landed, every claim lead-verified exactly, including a subtle caution about class credit that turned out precisely right.
resolved.body: `rage-powers-canonical-narrowing-scoping.md` recommends Raging Climber (`BONUS:VAR|RagingClimberBonus|RagePowersLVL`, `BONUS:SKILL|Climb|RagingClimberBonus|PREVAREQ:Raging,1`) — lead-confirmed byte-exact. Wins on every criterion this session has used: simplest formula on the roster (no arithmetic, no divisor/offset transcription risk — the exact failure shape items 69's Raging Song and Sacred Weapon's own dice-count bug both had), purely passive, and lands on a computed total (Climb is one of the three tracked selected-skill modifiers). **A real selection constraint the brief didn't anticipate, lead-confirmed verbatim in Skald's own DESC**: "This cannot be a rage power that requires the creature to spend a standard action or rounds of rage to activate it. For example, the skald cannot choose terrifying howl... but can choose knockback." A pick that isn't Skald-legal would have collapsed the two-class leverage that motivated the whole task — Terrifying Howl (otherwise an attractive flat-DC candidate) is corpus-confirmed excluded by name, as are Renewed Vigor/Powerful Blow/Surprise Accuracy/Strength Surge (once-per-rage or standard-action shaped). **One correction to scout's own earlier survey, caught and precisely hedged rather than overclaimed**: `RagePowersLVL` is set by three sources, not two — Barbarian, Skald, and `Bloodrager Archetype ~ Primalist`. Lead independently confirmed the third is **archetype-only**, not base Bloodrager, matching this session's standing convention that archetype records aren't ingested/counted (the same shape as the `Monk_CF_*`/`Bloodrager_CF_*` suppression-flag family) — so the two-class credit (Barbarian `/2`, Skald `/3`, both confirmed) stands as scout scoped it, not three. **Ruling on the doc's own open question — ground both Raging Climber and Raging Swimmer, not just one.** Raging Swimmer is confirmed an exact structural twin (`BONUS:VAR|RagingSwimmerBonus|RagePowersLVL`, `BONUS:SKILL|Swim|RagingSwimmerBonus|PREVAREQ:Raging,1`, byte-for-byte the same shape targeting Swim instead of Climb — also one of the three tracked computed skills). This deliberately deviates from the strict one-canonical-pick-per-chooser precedent (Oracle's Mystery, Hunter's Animal Focus, Cavalier's Order) — recorded explicitly rather than silently: that precedent exists to bound a chooser's *design* complexity, not to cap at exactly one entry when a second is a genuine zero-risk twin (same formula shape, same gate, same computed-total integration, differing only in which of the three tracked skills it targets). Doubles the computed-total integration value scout flagged for nearly free. Superstition (`2+RagePowersLVL/4` on saves, Skald-legality confirmed by explicit DESC naming) stays the documented fallback, not built — carries arithmetic and a narrower scope, no reason to prefer it over two zero-arithmetic twins. Dispatched as task #54, sequenced alongside/after #50 per scout's own note (Skald's own rage-power pool count is already in #50's scope).

resolved.title: RESOLVED — task #55 (Arcanist Exploits scoping) landed, every claim lead-verified exactly, and the class-specific constraint pattern from item 72 repeats a third time.
resolved.body: `arcanist-exploits-canonical-narrowing-scoping.md` confirms 46 active Exploit records (lead-confirmed exact count) with a real class-specific legality/cost constraint the brief explicitly asked scout to check for rather than assume absent: **36 of 46 reference the Arcane Reservoir** (lead-confirmed via case-insensitive DESC search, exact match) — most Exploits cost a spendable resource this engine doesn't model, so "purely passive" is the exception here, not the default, same shape as Skald's rage-power activation restriction (item 72) and a third instance of "verify the class-specific constraint, don't rank on formula quality alone" this session. Exactly four Exploits carry neither a Reservoir cost nor a `PRE` gate: Metamagic Knowledge (already grounded), Familiar, Item Crafting, and Bloodline Development (deferred as a chooser-in-chooser). **Ruling: Familiar is the canonical pick, not Item Crafting.** Lead independently confirmed `BONUS:VAR|FamiliarMasterLVL|ArcanistLVL` byte-exact and confirmed `ground_familiar_master_benefit` (`pilot_compute.rs:11793`) already exists, emitting `class_feature.familiar.master_hit_point_bonus` — genuinely namespaced `familiar.`, not `witch.`/`shaman.`, confirming it was built as shared class-agnostic machinery from the start. This is the decisive fact scout's recommendation turns on: Familiar reuses an already-shipped mechanism and lands on `durability.rs`'s computed max-HP total (the Toad canonical's own `+3 max HP`), extending the familiar thread already serving Witch and Shaman to a third class — cross-class *reuse*, not new design. Item Crafting is structurally near-identical to the already-grounded Metamagic Knowledge (same `ABILITYPOOL|...Feat|1` shape) and genuinely lower-risk to build, but grounds a bare count with no computed consumer — correctly ranked second by scout, and not built alongside Familiar the way Rage Powers' exact twins were (item 72): unlike Raging Climber/Swimmer, Familiar and Item Crafting are not twins, and this task's own honest framing (single-class, no status change, lower value than Rage Powers) doesn't justify building two Exploits when one already captures the real win. Dispatched as task #56.
resolved.call_text: **Ruling: Familiar is the canonical pick, not Item Crafting.** Lead independently confirmed `BONUS:VAR|FamiliarMasterLVL|ArcanistLVL` byte-exact and confirmed `ground_familiar_master_benefit` (`pilot_compute.rs:11793`) already exists, emitting `class_feature.familiar.master_hit_point_bonus` — genuinely namespaced `familiar.`, not `witch.`/`shaman.`, confirming it was built as shared class-agnostic machinery from the start.

resolved.body: All lead-independently re-confirmed: (1) Rage Power records are keyed `KEY:Rage Power ~ <Name>` (mechanism-namespaced), not a bare `KEY:<Name>` — a naive grep would return zero hits and look like the records don't exist, the same trap the Witch 324-vs-326 spell-count saga hit; backend caught it on their own by re-checking plain text before reporting a false negative. (2) `RagePowersLVL` has a fourth setter beyond the three already known (Barbarian, Skald, Bloodrager's archetype-only Primalist): `KEY:Viking ~ Viking Rage Power`, a **Fighter archetype** — lead-confirmed the `FighterLVL` setter directly. Same exclusion reasoning applies (archetype-only, not base Fighter), so the two-class credit (Barbarian, Skald) from item 72 stands unchanged, but the full setter list is now on record so a future search doesn't rediscover it and wonder. (3) An `Unchained Rage Power ~` duplicate exists in `pathfinder_unchained`, lead-confirmed **not ingested anywhere in this repo's corpus** — a looser search pattern than the exact `KEY:Rage Power ~` prefix would match both and double-count. All three findings written directly into task #54's own description rather than left in chat, so the next agent gets a head start with no re-derivation needed. **Task #54 released back to pending/unassigned** — backend judged a shared-checkout integration build (Climb/Swim computed-total wiring, activation-gated) wasn't safe to start with limited remaining context, correctly citing the earlier #39-inside-#38 incident (item 66) as the failure shape to avoid repeating. resolved.title: RESOLVED — featmate found a real worktree-verification hazard: a shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` between two working trees of the same package can produce a false-green test run on a genuinely broken build.
resolved.body: Featmate appended a test module referencing functions that don't exist yet in a worktree, expecting a compile failure, and got `0 passed; 849 filtered out`, exit 0 — a stale-fingerprint cache serving cached artifacts rather than recompiling, because they'd been passing `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<main repo>/target` from the worktree to skip a cold build. **A missing symbol is normally the single most reliable RED signal there is; this made it silently pass.** Fix in use: a dedicated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per worktree, one cold build's cost for a trustworthy signal. **Lead independently checked whether this affects any of this session's own worktree verifications (every teammate-claim check this entire session has used `git worktree add /tmp/verify-<sha> <sha>` + `cargo test`) — it does not.** Confirmed directly: no `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is set anywhere in the lead's environment (checked `env`, `~/.cargo/config.toml`, and the repo's own `.cargo/config.toml` — none set it), and a fresh worktree's `cargo build` places `target/` inside the worktree itself by cargo's own default behavior when the env var is absent, confirmed by building in a real throwaway worktree and reading the actual resolved path. So every isolated-worktree verification credited in this doc so far was genuinely isolated, not silently sharing a cache — the hazard is specific to featmate's own speed optimization, not a property of the worktree technique itself. **Scope of doubt, as featmate stated it plainly rather than let it stand ambiguous**: Summoner Slice A's authoritative verification was the post-cherry-pick run in the main repo (833/833), not the worktree run, so unaffected. The one commit verified only in the affected worktree (an early Perfect Self attempt, `c86cd6fb`/`fe42a430`) never landed regardless — #41 closed as correctly-deferred-not-built (risks item 68) with zero code shipped, confirmed by the lead via direct grep on the real committed HEAD, which this cache issue cannot have touched since it checks actual git history, not a test run. **Recommendation for the worktree-verification discipline going forward (item 66's addendum): never share `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` across two trees of the same package; if speed matters, accept the one cold build per worktree rather than the cache-sharing shortcut.**
resolved.call_text: So every isolated-worktree verification credited in this doc so far was genuinely isolated, not silently sharing a cache — the hazard is specific to featmate's own speed optimization, not a property of the worktree technique itself.

resolved.title: RESOLVED — task #59 (Bloodlines scoping) landed with two real corrections to scout's own prior work, both self-caught and stated plainly rather than glossed over.
resolved.body: `bloodlines-canonical-narrowing-scoping.md`: **Bloodlines is the richest family surveyed, not thin** — 149 magnitude-bearing records (Sorcerer 112, Bloodrager 37) against Arcanist Exploits' 21, Rage Powers' 18, Rogue Talents' 10. Scout's own post-#57 "the vein is exhausted, each family is thinner" call is corrected on the spot: three descending samples were an ordering artifact, not a trend. **Bigger correction, reaching back to #51's own classification**: Bloodlines is not actually a shared family. Lead independently confirmed Sorcerer's records are keyed `KEY:<Name> Bloodline ~ <Power>` and Bloodrager's are `KEY:<Name> Bloodrager Bloodline ~ <Power>` — genuinely distinct record sets; ten bloodline *names* overlap (Draconic, Abyssal, etc.) but the underlying powers and records are entirely separate, so there is no two-classes-from-one-build leverage the way Rage Powers had. **This is the shared-name-≠-shared-thing trap landing on scout's own earlier survey classification** — the same shape as `EidMaxAttacks` and the Cavalier decoy, now caught in scout's own prior output rather than the corpus. Also confirmed: the narrowing unit here is a whole ~6-power bloodline ladder (auto-granted as a package via `PREABILITY`), not one power, making this structurally bigger than the previous three families' single-power picks; only 4 of 149 magnitude records land on a computed total (lead-confirmed Draconic's Dragon Resistances → `BONUS:COMBAT|AC|...NaturalArmorBonus`, exact), the rest ground standalone. **Ruling: agreed with scout's own recommendation — do not squeeze Bloodlines into the quick-canonical-pick pattern.** Filed as its own future dedicated workstream rather than a fifth quick-pick task, matching the treatment Summoner's own Slice A/B split got rather than a bounded single-pick shape. **Adopted scout's reframing of the "is the vein exhausted" question**: the *shared*-chooser vein specifically is exhausted (only Rage Powers turned out genuinely shared across classes of the four surveyed), but a new, larger seam exists — class-specific power ladders, of which Bloodlines is the biggest known instance. Worth surveying for siblings (other ladder-shaped class features: Cleric Domains, Wizard Arcane Schools, similar) as its own future task.

resolved.title: RESOLVED — task #60 (Draconic Bloodline ladder scoping) landed, the anchor (Dragon Resistances) confirmed exactly including a subtle two-line stacking detail, and a genuine third nesting level found.
resolved.body: `draconic-bloodline-ladder-scoping.md`: seven real records at gates 1/1/3/9/15/20 (Bloodline Arcana, Bloodline Powers, Claws at 1; Dragon Resistances at 3; Breath Weapon at 9; Wings at 15; Power of Wyrms at 20), lead-confirmed via the corpus's own `Power LVL 0N` type tags and `PREVARGTEQ:...ProgressionLVL,N` gates. **Dragon Resistances' natural armor progression needs both of its two `BONUS:VAR|...NaturalArmorBonus` lines, not just the first** — lead independently recomputed the exact corpus formula (`min(floor((LVL-3)/6)+1,3)` plus a separate flat `+1` gated `PREVARGTEQ:...,15`) and got 1/2/4 at levels 3/9/15+ exactly matching scout's table; reading only the first line gives a wrong 3 at level 15. **Notable for once being the inverse of this session's usual finding**: the corpus is correct and a naive single-line read would be wrong, rather than the corpus having the defect (Sacred Weapon, Raging Song) or the naive read missing a real precedent (Brawler's Maneuver Training). **A genuine third nesting level, lead-confirmed real**: Dragon Resistances' energy type isn't fixed by the bloodline choice — it branches on four `Sorcerer_DraconicDamageType_{Acid,Cold,Electricity,Fire}` flags set elsewhere (the dragon-type sub-choice under Bloodline Powers), each gating its own `{Acid,Cold,Electricity,Fire}ResistanceBonus` grant. So the full chooser depth is Sorcerer → Draconic → dragon type → energy type, one level deeper than any prior narrowing this session. **The magnitudes themselves are type-agnostic** (5/10 resistance, 1/2/4 natural armor regardless of which dragon type is chosen) — this is what makes the open question tractable. **Ruling on scout's own open question: ground the magnitudes, defer the energy-type label.** Matches the standing "ground the magnitude, name the unmodelled circumstance/choice" idiom already used repeatedly this session (Monk's Fast Movement encumbrance condition, Paladin's aura's ally-scoped clause, etc.) — the resistance and natural-armor numbers are real and computable regardless of dragon type, while which specific energy type applies is a further canonical-narrowing-within-canonical-narrowing choice that doesn't need resolving to ground a correct number. Claws (needs a natural-attack routine, same category as the Eidolon's attack surface) and Bloodline Arcana (modifies unmodeled spell damage) correctly stay deferred; Breath Weapon splits on the Bomb precedent (ground dice/DC/uses, defer the effect). Dispatched Dragon Resistances alone as the build (task #61) — the one power with a real computed AC consumer.

resolved.body: `class-ladder-families-triage.md`: scout derived the family set empirically (grouped every `KEY:<prefix> ~ <power>` record by its trailing noun) rather than checking only the brief's named candidates, surfacing four families the brief didn't name (Hexes, Spirits, Favored Enemy, Favored Terrain) — the same "enumerate, don't assume the list" discipline as the id-prefix rule (items 60/63), now applied to family discovery itself rather than prefixes. **Domain: 292 records, 159 magnitude-bearing** — bigger than Bloodlines (244/149) on both counts. Extending to Inquisitor and Druid needs a real generalization pass first, which is exactly what turns this from a one-class widening into three-class leverage — the reason it needs a dedicated scope rather than a quick canonical pick. **Also confirmed as a side finding**: Favored Enemy (31/31) and Favored Terrain (18/18) are the only two families with zero tokenless filler — 100% magnitude coverage — but both are Ranger-only and already well covered, so cleanest-small-target rather than open-opportunity. **Ruling: file Cleric Domains as its own major future workstream, same treatment as Bloodlines got before Draconic's own dedicated scoping pass.** Not immediately dispatched as a build — the generalization-pass question needs resolving first. resolved.title: RESOLVED — task #63 (Cleric Domains generalization scoping) landed with strong structural verification, but its headline "five classes, not three" claim doesn't survive an archetype check. Corrected: three base classes, matching the original #62 count.
resolved.body: `cleric-domains-generalization-scoping.md` found `DomainLVL` fed by six paths across the ingested corpus (lead independently re-derived the same six, scoped correctly to only the four ingested books — confirmed two more paths exist in the wider PCGen reference tree, `MediumLVL`/`VigilanteLVL`, but their source books, `adventurers_guide`/`ultimate_intrigue`, are confirmed not ingested anywhere in this repo's `data/corpus/`, so scout's own search was already correctly scoped there). **But of the six ingested-book paths, only three are base-class**: `ClericLVL` (`Cleric ~ Domains`), `DruidLVL` (`Nature's Bond ~ Druid Domain`), `InquisitorLVL` (`Inquisitor ~ Domains`) — all lead-confirmed genuine base class features. **The other three are archetype-only**, lead-confirmed directly: `HunterLVL-2` is `KEY:Divine Hunter ~ Domain`, explicitly typed `TYPE:...ArchetypeAbility...`; `PaladinLVL` is `KEY:Temple Champion ~ Domain Granted Power`; `PaladinLVL-3` is `KEY:Sacred Servant ~ Spells` — Temple Champion and Sacred Servant are both known Paladin archetypes. Same exclusion this session has already applied consistently (Bloodrager's Primalist, Fighter's Viking Rage Power) — this repo doesn't ingest archetype records as base-class credit. **So the real answer is three classes, matching the original #62 triage's count, not five.** Had this gone unchecked, a generalization pass targeting Hunter and Paladin would have wired functionality this repo has no path to reach (no archetype ingestion) rather than genuine base-class coverage. **Everything else in #63 checks out exactly.** The per-class level-offset finding stands and matters even at three classes: Cleric/Druid/Inquisitor all use their bare class level directly (no offset needed among the three real ones — the two offset paths, `HunterLVL-2`/`PaladinLVL-3`, were both archetype-only anyway), so the generalization is simpler than scout initially worried, not more complex. Lead independently confirmed the three coupling points exactly: `cleric_touch_of_good_bonus(level) -> (level/2).max(1)` has zero Cleric coupling (bare level parameter); the only hardcoding is in `active_cleric_touch_of_good_bonus`'s level lookup (`CLERIC_CLASS_ID`) and its choice-set filter (`CLERIC_DOMAIN_CHOICE_ID`) — both confirmed at their exact cited locations. No canonical domain pick needed — the chooser is already handled, only the class dispatch isn't, a genuine contrast with Bloodlines' package-arrival shape. **Ruling on the namespace question: shared `class_feature.domain.*`, not per-class ids** — agreed with scout's own recommendation, matching the Familiar precedent (`class_feature.familiar.master_hit_point_bonus`) that made Arcanist's Exploit reuse near-free in #56. Dispatched as task #64, scoped to the three real base classes (Cleric, Druid, Inquisitor) only.

resolved.title: RESOLVED — task #65 (Wizard Arcane Schools) confirms genuine shared leverage, and scout applied the #63 archetype-check lesson proactively this time, catching its own #62 inflation before the lead had to.
resolved.body: `arcane-schools-shared-verification-scoping.md`: `ArcaneSchoolLVL` is fed by exactly two paths, lead-confirmed exact — `WizardLVL` and `ArcanistLvl` — and both screened for archetype status before crediting (unlike the Domains near-miss): `Arcanist Exploit ~ School Understanding` is `TYPE:ArcanistExploit.SpecialQuality`, genuinely base Arcanist, not an archetype. So the two-class credit isn't available independently — grounding Schools gets Wizard immediately, Arcanist only once School Understanding is separately recognized. **Ruling**: agreed with scout's own recommendation — sequence after Domains (#64) rather than compete with it, and don't build Schools' Wizard half while implicitly promising Arcanist credit that isn't real yet. Apply the same shared-namespace ruling as Domains (`class_feature.domain.*` precedent) once built. Filed as a future task, not urgently dispatched — queued behind #64.

resolved.title: RESOLVED — task #67's backlog pre-verification pass found a real, non-blocking correction (Domains' count understated by ~60%) and, more valuably, scout named the actual pattern behind three same-day misses.
resolved.body: Scout pre-checked Domains' count before #64 could build against it, since it had flagged Domains as at-risk after the Schools inflation. **The archetype-contamination risk was unfounded — zero archetype-typed records in the actual Domain power-record namespaces, lead independently confirmed** (a broad "Domain + CATEGORY:Archetype" grep first looked concerning, three hits, but all three turned out to be archetype records that merely *mention* domains in unrelated fields — e.g., an Ecclesitheurge/Divine Hunter/Temple Champion archetype description referencing domain access — not actual `KEY:<Name> Domain ~ <Power>`-shaped records; a precise re-check scoped to the real power-record key patterns returned zero). **#63/#64's three-class credit is clean on this axis.** **But #62's own Domain count only matched one of four coexisting key formats** (`<Name> Domain ~ <Power>`) and missed `Domain Power ~ <Power>`, `Bonus Domain Times ~ <Power>`, and `Domain Base ~ <Power>` wrappers — the exact trap #63's own hazard section named ("a sweep matching only one shape sees a partial family") applied to everyone else's work but not checked against scout's own #62 count. Real family is meaningfully bigger than 292/159 — lead independently confirmed all four key shapes exist and sum well above the original count (exact reconciliation differs between scout's and the lead's own quick recount, worth a script-based reconciliation before any exact number ships as a hard total, but the direction — bigger, not smaller — is solid and doesn't change task #64's premise, which only depends on one already-directly-verified power, Touch of Good). **The more valuable finding is the pattern scout named plainly rather than just reporting the number**: three same-day instances (Hunter/Paladin domain credit, Schools' #62 inflation, now this key-format miss) share one root cause — scrutiny aimed outward at the corpus and at others' claims, not turned on scout's own prior output. Worth carrying as a standing self-check for any future audit work: apply the same skepticism to one's own already-shipped numbers as to a fresh corpus read. **Scout concluded the backlog is now clean** (checked #61 and #66 specifically as the two remaining tasks resting on scout's own family-size claims, both confirmed safe by independent verification already) and recommended stopping rather than manufacturing further checks — agreed, task #67 closed on that basis.

resolved.title: INCIDENT — featmate hit its session limit mid-#49 commit-2, with real uncommitted work sitting in a session-scoped `/tmp` worktree path (not durable, not visible to other teammates). Preserved by the lead rather than lost.
resolved.body: The worktree (`/tmp/claude-1000/.../scratchpad/wt-perfectself`) held two things beyond its own committed history: a 14GB `target-iso` build directory (not gitignored under that name, caused `git add -A` to hang — staged the real source files explicitly instead) and a genuine in-progress diff (`MAX_SUPPORTED_MONK_LEVEL` already bumped to 20, a new `tests/sd49_monk_level20_capstone.rs` suite plus its fixture, one existing test file modified). Lead committed this diff verbatim — no authorship, no interpretation of intent, no attempt to finish or fix anything in it — with an explicit "not yet verified, completeness unknown" caveat in the commit message, and pushed it to `wip/sd49-monk-widening-featmate` so it survives regardless of any single session's lifetime. Task #49 hard-handed to backend with the full state (three commits: an already-known-superseded Perfect Self attempt, the three formula fixes featmate self-reported as 847/847 clean but the lead hasn't re-verified, and the uncommitted commit-2 snapshot of unknown completeness) and an explicit instruction to re-derive from scratch in a fresh isolated worktree rather than trust any of it, same discipline as any other in-flight commit. **Standing lesson for future sessions**: a teammate's local worktree under its own session's `/tmp` scratchpad is not a shared resource — if a session ends mid-work there, the work is invisible to everyone else until someone finds it, commits it to a real branch, and pushes. Worth checking for stranded worktrees (`git worktree list`) whenever a teammate goes silent or hits a session limit, not just when explicitly told about one.

resolved.title: RESOLVED — task #67's full six-claim audit came back clean, but found the archetype-screening method itself has a confirmed false-negative rate: TYPE-based screening misses some archetypes entirely, KEY-prefix screening doesn't.
resolved.body: All six queued class-credit claims verified: #54 (Barbarian+Skald), #56 (Arcanist-only, correctly excluding `Unlettered Arcanist ~ Familiar`'s own separate archetype), #61 (Sorcerer-only), #64 (Cleric+Druid+Inquisitor, all three archetype exclusions correct) all clean; #58 (Rogue+Investigator) partially verified, Investigator's own leg flagged as needing its own separate check (uses a different variable, not covered by this screen). **The methodology finding, lead independently confirmed**: scout's `CATEGORY:Archetype`/`TYPE:*Archetype*` screen has a real gap — `KEY:Sacred Servant ~ Spells` (a genuine Paladin archetype already correctly excluded from #63/#64) is typed `TYPE:ClassFeatures.PaladinClassFeatures.SpecialQuality.CF`, lead-confirmed verbatim, **indistinguishable from base Paladin content by TYPE alone**. It was only caught because scout's earlier `KEY:` inspection happened to show the archetype name; a pure TYPE-based screen would have missed it entirely, the same way it would miss any future archetype whose author didn't bother marking `TYPE:...Archetype...`. **The reliable signal is the `KEY:<Name> ~ …` prefix, not TYPE** — base features use `KEY:<ClassName> ~ …` or a named base-family prefix (e.g. `KEY:Arcanist Exploit ~ …`); archetypes use `KEY:<Archetype Name> ~ …`. Structural rather than name-recognition, so it generalizes to archetypes nobody's specifically checked for by name, and the same logic extends to prestige classes (scout flagged `Dragon Disciple ~ Blood of Dragons` as passing a TYPE screen too, currently harmless where it appears but a real risk for a different future claim). **Recorded as the durable rule going forward: screen by KEY prefix, not TYPE, when checking base-class-vs-archetype status.** **Two residual items, both resolved by the lead rather than left open**: (1) #58's Investigator leg — not chased further this pass, stays flagged for whoever builds #58. (2) Cleric's own `DomainLVL` setter appeared missing from scout's setter-path list — lead found it: `BONUS:VAR|DomainLVL|ClericLVL` lives on the `CLASS:Cleric` line itself in `cr_classes.lst`, not in the abilities file where Druid's/Inquisitor's grafted-on domain access lives (`Nature's Bond ~ Druid Domain`, `Inquisitor ~ Domains`) — Cleric's domain access is baked into the class definition as the "native" path, the other two classes graft it on via separate ability records. Not a gap, just a different file than where the search was scoped; #64's Cleric leg is confirmed genuinely wired, no action needed. Backlog confirmed clean; task #67 closed on scout's own recommendation to stop rather than manufacture a third sweep.
resolved.call_text: Not a gap, just a different file than where the search was scoped; #64's Cleric leg is confirmed genuinely wired, no action needed.

resolved.title: INCIDENT — dispatching 10 fresh Agent-tool subagents with `isolation: worktree` produced a nondeterministic base-branch bug: 5 of 10 worktrees were created from the wrong base commit (effectively `develop`'s HEAD area, not `tranche/6`), with no error or warning.
resolved.body: All 10 agents were told in their prompts they were "working on branch tranche/6," but the actual worktree base is determined by the tool infrastructure at creation time, not by prompt text. Caught by checking `git worktree list` and comparing each worktree's base commit against known `tranche/6` history immediately after the first agent (#61) reported completion — its worktree's `git log` showed unrelated `develop`-area commits (a LICENSE update, unrelated PR merges), and diffing its `pilot_compute.rs` against real `tranche/6` showed a ~50,000-line difference, confirming the file version was completely different from what the agent was told to build against. Checking all 10 worktrees' base commits found the same defect in 4 more (#49, #54, #64, #66) and confirmed the other 5 (#44, #47, #50, #56, #58) were correctly based on real `tranche/6` commits (`6748cb50`, `27afbb82`, both independently confirmed present in `tranche/6`'s own history). **No pattern in which 5 got it wrong** — not simply "first N dispatched" or "last N dispatched," consistent with a race condition in the underlying worktree-creation mechanism rather than a deterministic ordering bug. **Fix applied**: sent a corrective message to each of the 5 affected agents (including resuming the one that had already completed) instructing them to `git fetch origin tranche/6` and `git reset --hard origin/tranche/6` before redoing their work, with an explicit verification step (grep for known tranche/6-era code) to confirm the fix took before proceeding. The other 5 agents were left running unattended since their base was confirmed correct. **Standing lesson for future multi-agent dispatch waves**: when using `isolation: worktree` for a batch of parallel Agent calls, verify each worktree's actual base commit (`git worktree list`, cross-check against the target branch's own `git log`) before trusting any of them to be working against the right code — do not assume the prompt's stated branch name reflects the tool's actual worktree base. This is a different, more fundamental hazard than item 76's shared-`CARGO_TARGET_DIR` issue (that one caused false-green *test results* on the right code; this one puts agents on entirely wrong *source code* from the start), and both should be checked whenever dispatching isolated-worktree agents. **Follow-up to item 86**: task #56's own agent independently hit and self-corrected the identical wrong-base problem before doing any real work, then proactively broadcast the finding to the lead rather than stay silent about it. This revealed a gap in the lead's own diagnosis: checking `git worktree list`'s reported HEAD only shows each worktree's *current* state, not its *original* base — an agent that self-detects and self-fixes the problem (as #56 did) looks identical, after the fact, to one that was correctly based from the start. Spot-checking the four other presumed-correct worktrees (#44/#47/#50/#58) found all four genuinely on real tranche/6 commits with no develop-area history, so this instance didn't change the outcome — but the lesson stands: a "looks correct now" check on worktree state doesn't distinguish "was always correct" from "silently self-corrected," and an agent that DIDN'T notice and self-correct could look identical to one that started correctly right up until its diff turns out wrong. Worth explicitly asking each agent to report its own worktree's starting state in future dispatch waves, not just checking after the fact.
resolved.call_text: Spot-checking the four other presumed-correct worktrees (#44/#47/#50/#58) found all four genuinely on real tranche/6 commits with no develop-area history, so this instance didn't change the outcome — but the lesson stands: a "looks correct now" check on worktree state doesn't distinguish "was always correct" from "silently self-corrected," and an agent that DIDN'T notice and self-correct could look identical to one that started correctly right up until its diff turns out wrong.

resolved.title: INCIDENT — a subagent's blanket `pkill -9 -f "cargo test"` / `pkill -9 -f "cargo build"` (used to clear its own stuck file-lock) killed other agents' unrelated cargo processes on the shared host, since `pkill -f` matches by command-line substring host-wide, not scoped to the caller's own cwd or process tree.
resolved.body: Task #61's agent hit a "Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory" from its own overlapping `cargo test`/`cargo build` invocations, used a blanket pattern-kill to clear it, then immediately noticed (via `pgrep -af cargo`) that the kill had also caught processes it never issued — including a `cargo build --lib` run with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=.../scratchpad/sd49-target`, confirmed by the lead to belong to task #49's own agent (the Monk cap-widening build), not #61's own work. **Self-caught and honestly reported rather than left silent** — the agent didn't know which other agent(s) were affected and said so plainly, named the exact time window (07:08–07:12) for anyone whose build silently vanished around then to check, and correctly diagnosed its own root cause (pattern-based host-wide kill vs. scoped-to-self process management) before being asked. **Lead checked the flagged victim (#49) directly rather than assume it was fine or broken**: confirmed multiple live cargo processes currently running (clippy, build --lib, build --tests) and real uncommitted progress across five files, indicating the agent had already recovered and was actively retrying on its own — no intervention needed. **Standing lesson for any future multi-agent dispatch on a shared host**: never use `pkill`/`killall` with a bare command-name or pattern match to clear a stuck local process — it isn't scoped to the caller and can silently kill sibling agents' legitimate work with no error surfaced to either party. Use a scoped mechanism instead (kill by specific PID after confirming ownership via `pgrep` filtered to the caller's own cwd/worktree path, or the harness's own task-stop mechanism for anything the caller itself launched as a tracked background task).

resolved.title: INCIDENT — `origin/tranche/6` went RED for the first time this session: task #54 (`0290ce1d`) silently broke Barbarian's level-21 and multiclass negative controls, unnoticed by the lead's own merge-time verification and only caught by a returning teammate's own pre-flight suite run before starting new work.
resolved.body: `tests/sd13_barbarian_level10_progression.rs`'s `barbarian_level_21_is_not_promoted_by_this_slice` and `multiclass_barbarian_level10_is_not_promoted_by_this_slice` both fail on current `origin/tranche/6` — lead independently reproduced in a fresh isolated worktree, confirmed clean. **Root cause git-bisected exactly** (checked out `0290ce1d~1` and re-ran the same test: 10/10 passing, confirming the trigger commit precisely rather than inferring it): `ground_or_block_barbarian_rage`'s "not raging" branch used to push its one recognition record (`class_feature.barbarian.rage_execution.not_raging`, itself deliberately unconditional on level/single-class status per risks item 8's gate-ordering fix, and explicitly allow-listed by name in the test's own assertion) and then `return;` immediately. Task #54 replaced that `return;` with a call to the new `ground_raging_climber_and_swimmer()`, which falls through rather than returning — so its two new records (`class_feature.barbarian.raging_climber`/`raging_swimmer`) inherited the same unconditional-on-level/class treatment as the deliberately-universal record next to them, despite being real skill-bonus magnitudes that should stay bounded like every other `class_feature.barbarian.*` record, not execution-state recognition. **Same shape confirmed present in `ground_or_block_skald_inspired_rage`, currently untested** (no equivalent Skald negative control exists to have caught it). **Why the lead's own merge-time verification missed this**: task #54's own re-verification (full lib suite, both SD-24 coverage audits, clippy) never ran this specific integration test file, since it isn't gated by either coverage audit (CRB Barbarian has no `named_features_wired` mechanism) and wasn't named in the task's own scope as a file to check — a real gap in "run the relevant class-specific tests," since "relevant" was inferred from the task's own framing (ACG Skald, Rage Powers) rather than enumerated by grepping for every test file referencing the touched function (`ground_or_block_barbarian_rage`). **Assigned to featmate (task #74) as the discoverer, with the precise fix specified**: gate the 4 `ground_raging_climber_and_swimmer` call sites (Barbarian x2, Skald x2) behind each class's own bounded-scope check, without reverting the real feature for genuinely in-scope raging/singing characters — the bug is the calls being unconditional, not the feature being wrong. **Follow-up: the lead's own full `--no-fail-fast` sweep against the pre-fix HEAD found the true blast radius was 13 distinct test files, not the 1 originally flagged** — every Barbarian level-widening progression file from level 9 through level 20 carries the identical two negative-control shapes, all failing via the same shared `ground_or_block_barbarian_rage` root cause. Relayed to featmate before their own verification completed, so their "clean" result would be checked against the real scope rather than the single file first reported. **Featmate found the fix needed 6 call sites, not the 4 originally specified** — three branches per class (no-activation-record, activation-present-but-inactive, and actively-raging/singing), not two — and centralized the bounded-scope guard inside `ground_raging_climber_and_swimmer` itself rather than at each call site, so a future seventh call site can't silently reopen the same leak. **Related — a second, unrelated shared-checkout hazard surfaced while diagnosing this incident**: a teammate mid-#72 (weapon-ingestion pillar) ran `git stash push` to isolate a suspected-own test failure; it failed on an untracked new file, and the follow-up `git stash pop` popped `stash@{0}` — which belonged to a *different* agent's own preserved work (`worktree-agent-a499dea88cc95db89`'s task-64 wrong-base-branch stash), briefly landing it in the wrong tree and conflicting `pilot_compute.rs`. **No work was lost**: the pop reported a conflict so git kept the stash entry rather than dropping it (verified still listed afterward), and the affected file was reset to HEAD rather than attempting to resolve someone else's conflict. **Standing lesson, same family as the pkill incident (item 87) but for git's stash stack specifically**: on a shared checkout, `git stash` operates on one global stack that isn't scoped to the calling agent — `git stash pop`/`git stash apply` can silently grab another agent's entry. Use a worktree, or `git diff > patch.diff` / `git diff --stat` to inspect without touching the shared stash stack at all. **Third instance of the same trap, with a new detail worth recording separately**: mid-#77, a bare `git stash push` (no pathspec) run from `apps/desktop/src-tauri/` stashed all 18 modified files repo-wide, not just that subtree — three agents' worth of unrelated in-progress work went into one stash entry. Recovered cleanly (popped by name, `wip77-clippy-baseline-check`, verified the other three agents' entries intact and in original order) and re-ran everything after the round-trip rather than trust a before/after comparison across it. **The new information**: the earlier two incidents both involved the pathspec form (`git stash push -- <paths>`); this confirms the *bare* form is repo-wide regardless of current working directory, including from deep inside a subdirectory that looks scoped. Running directory does not scope `git stash` at all — only an explicit pathspec does, and even that failed once already (item 88's stash incident) on an untracked file. The only fully safe options on a shared checkout remain a worktree or `git diff`.
resolved.call_text: **Assigned to featmate (task #74) as the discoverer, with the precise fix specified**: gate the 4 `ground_raging_climber_and_swimmer` call sites (Barbarian x2, Skald x2) behind each class's own bounded-scope check, without reverting the real feature for genuinely in-scope raging/singing characters — the bug is the calls being unconditional, not the feature being wrong.

resolved.title: RESOLVED 2026-07-29 (commit `04dea038`) — the -4 nonproficiency penalty is now applied on both compute paths, magnitude read from `miscinfo.lst:193` `WEAPONNONPROFPENALTY:-4`, proficiency read per class from the corpus (12 of 27 proficient with the baseline Longsword, 15 not). Wizard 3's melee corrected 1 -> -3, exactly as predicted below; Cleric and Inquisitor likewise corrected. The Bard trap was handled — it IS Longsword-proficient via an explicit `AUTO:WEAPONPROF` grant despite being Simple-tier-only, so it is correctly NOT penalized. The PCGen parity harness was updated in the same commit with the export defect named explicitly: the residual gap is -3, the sum of two independent omissions (Weapon Focus +1 and the -4) that partly cancelled, which is precisely how the second stayed hidden. Original finding follows.
resolved.body: ORIGINAL: **CORRECTNESS BUG, live on a Computed class — the most severe finding of this session's whole reconciliation effort, and genuinely different in kind from every #76/#79/#84 finding before it.** Those were all stale *text* describing real code accurately or inaccurately. This is a real *number*, silently wrong, on a class users can build and save today. `combat.baseline_melee_attack_bonus` hardcodes a Longsword and computes a full attack bonus for every class dispatched into it, including classes with zero proficiency in that weapon — the corpus's own nonproficiency penalty (-4 to attack) is not modeled anywhere in the codebase (confirmed: zero "nonproficient" mechanics hits anywhere in `pilot_compute.rs`, only equipment-description prose in `arms_armor.rs`). **Lead independently verified the headline case**: Wizard's own corpus proficiency grant (`cr_abilities_class.lst:2566`, `AUTO:WEAPONPROF|Club|Dagger|Crossbow (Heavy)|Crossbow (Light)|Quarterstaff`) excludes Longsword entirely, yet `tests/sd21_wizard_chassis_computes.rs:225-228` asserts a Wizard 3's melee bonus as `BAB(1) + STR(-1) + Weapon Focus(1) = 1` — real PF1 RAW is `-3`, a silent 4-point overstatement the shipped test itself locks in as correct. **Why the PCGen-parity harness didn't catch it**: `v06_wizard_pilot_case_verification.rs` asserts one known Codex-vs-PCGen mismatch (+1, attributed to Weapon Focus) but PCGen's own compared export field evidently omits the same nonproficiency penalty, so both sides agree while both are wrong — an oracle sharing a blind spot with the thing it validates, discovered by a teammate's investigation rather than assumed safe because parity passed. **Scope, corrected from the original task framing twice**: (1) "a real corpus record on every class" was false — of the 82 entities carrying a `Weapon and Armor Proficiency`-shaped record, only Barbarian/Cleric/Sorcerer/Wizard among CRB base classes have one; Fighter/Monk/Rogue/Druid/Paladin/Ranger/Bard have none, so this is a missing *mechanic* gap, not an unwired-record gap. (2) Blast radius is every dispatched non-Martial class, not roster-wide — Fighter/Barbarian/Paladin/Ranger are genuinely fine (real proficiency); Wizard is confirmed wrong; Sorcerer/Cleric/Monk/Druid/Rogue are strongly suspected but not yet individually verified. **Two adjacent findings from the same investigation**: Monk's own Catch Off-Guard explanation text asserts the baseline "uses a real proficient weapon," which is false for Monk itself (folded into the swarm's task #88, the separate explanation-detail-string sweep — not this risks doc's own item 88 above, which is the red-branch incident); and `defense.baseline_armor_class` gives every character a Chain Shirt +4 including Wizard (who is proficient with no armor at all) with arcane spell failure and armor check penalty unmodeled — a separate bug sharing the same hardcoded-posture root, not yet its own task. **Sequencing**: entangled with task #80 (generalize the melee-bonus function off its Longsword hardcode) — proficiency cannot be modeled honestly while the weapon itself is fixed, and generalizing the weapon without also modeling proficiency just relocates the silent error to a wider surface. **Immediate action, assigned as top priority**: a claim-blocking diagnostic naming the omission for non-Martial classes computing the baseline, so the number stops presenting as silently correct, ahead of #80's fuller fix.
resolved.call_text: ORIGINAL: **CORRECTNESS BUG, live on a Computed class — the most severe finding of this session's whole reconciliation effort, and genuinely different in kind from every #76/#79/#84 finding before it.** Those were all stale *text* describing real code accurately or inaccurately.

resolved.title: RESOLVED, no history rewrite (same ruling class as item 66) — commit `7b8249b5` on `tranche/6` is genuinely mislabeled: title says "widen proficiency table to the full 27-class roster (#80/#86)", actual contents are 100% Inquisitor task #47 material (889 lines of `pilot_compute.rs`, the new `inquisitor_spell_list.rs`, `apg/mod.rs`, `sd24_apg_class_coverage_audit.rs` — zero touch to `weapon_tables.rs` or any proficiency file), lead-confirmed directly via `git show --stat`.
resolved.body: Root cause, per backend's own real-time report: backend ran `git commit` + `git pull --rebase` in the shared checkout without checking for an in-progress rebase first; a `git add -A` on their end swept up the lead's own concurrent, unrelated mid-rebase conflict-resolution state (rebasing task #47's worktree branch `worktree-agent-a96478aa467c81f41` onto `origin/tranche/6`) instead of backend's real proficiency-widening diff. Backend's actual roster-widening work was never committed anywhere and needs to be redone (backend has the values in working notes, ~30 min of deterministic corpus-derived data, no re-verification needed). **The lead's own rebase completed successfully and independently**: 4 real conflict hunks against task #64's already-landed Touch-of-Good fact, hand-resolved, full suite re-verified post-merge (983/983 lib, both SD-24 audits 3/3, clippy 80/0), pushed as `8f1300e5` — confirmed intact, correctly attributed, and its diff against `098393d0` matches the lead's own merge exactly. **Ruling: do not rewrite `7b8249b5`/`8f1300e5` or any commit downstream of them** (`8451cf49`/`27cfd930`/`554f15a4` all already pushed on top) — same reasoning as item 66: the branch is shared and actively being built on by multiple concurrent sessions, the code itself is correct and fully verified regardless of the parent commit's message, and a squash/rebase now would force-push over three more already-pushed commits than backend's own proposal accounted for. Fixed via this tracking note instead: `7b8249b5`'s message does not describe its contents; treat its actual diff as an intermediate/superseded snapshot of task #47, fully superseded by `8f1300e5`. Backend cleared to redo the real roster-widening now that the tree is clean, and to delete the two additive recovery refs (`RECOVERY-task47-inquisitor-rebase-state`, `PRESERVE-task47-final-8f1300e5`) once satisfied, since neither points at anything not already safely on `tranche/6`. **Separately confirmed at least two concurrent Claude Code sessions (the operator's own parallel session, surfacing as "backend"/"featmate") are writing to this same branch alongside the lead's session** — a real collision surface this swarm's single-lead-orchestrator design did not anticipate; flagged to the operator directly rather than resolved unilaterally.

doneness_meaning.done: The evidence this unit has meets the bar its wiring_class requires. Nothing further is owed. For `static`/`derived` specifically, this requires the literal/evaluator check the class has always named -- `static` cleared by `corpus_literal_sweep`'s byte-equality compare, `derived` cleared by `derived_evaluator_fixture_check`'s evaluator-vs-fixture compare -- carried in the record as `status` `literal-verified`/`fixture-verified`. Ordinary `ingested-magnitude`/`grounded`/`text-complete` evidence on a `static`/`derived` unit does NOT clear this bar and stays `held` (SD-32 decisions.md §2, operator directive 2026-08-13).
doneness_meaning.held: The engine holds the record with its real data. For `static`/`derived` the check that would confirm the bar now EXISTS -- `corpus_literal_sweep` for `static`, `derived_evaluator_fixture_check` for `derived` -- but this particular unit has not yet been swept/checked and found to pass (it carries ordinary `ingested-magnitude`/`grounded`/`text-complete` evidence rather than `literal-verified`/`fixture-verified`). A unit that HAS cleared its check reads `done`, not `held` (SD-32 decisions.md §2, operator directive 2026-08-13). For `ambiguous` and `display` (specifically `display`+`grounded`, where a real consumer delta contradicts the no-magnitude classification) the bar is not even known yet -- both need a working wiring-class classifier before there is a bar to check against at all. Also where a unit of any `kind` listed in `NO_GROUNDING_PROBE` would otherwise land `in-progress`: that kind has no consumer-delta probe at all, so its bar can never be confirmed reachable by an instrument that exists. As done as the current instruments can prove, and deliberately not counted as done (SD-29 decisions.md §46.4). `NO_GROUNDING_PROBE` is empty as of SD30-E0-F2 (2026-08-14) -- `spell` and `companion`, the two kinds it used to name, both have a landed probe reaching a nonzero `grounded` count under `computed` (46 and 416 respectively, re-derived that cycle), so this clause is currently vacuous by construction, not dead code -- a future kind with a genuinely unreachable bar has somewhere to be listed.
doneness_meaning.in-progress: Really part way: ingested, short of its own class's bar, and the bar is reachable with an instrument that exists. Dominated by `computed` units holding their numbers with no consumer delta yet observed. Would never be assigned to a `kind` listed in `NO_GROUNDING_PROBE` -- currently empty (SD30-E0-F2, 2026-08-14; see that constant's declaration) -- since for such a kind no instrument that could reach the bar would exist at all.
doneness_meaning.not-started: No record in the engine -- `engine-does-not-hold` (the book is in play, this unit is not) or `not-started` (the book has not been worked).
doneness_meaning.unmeasurable: `status` came back `unknown`: the record itself gives no evidence at all, regardless of wiring_class, so there is nothing to place on the ladder. A work item against the instruments, not a statement about the content, and never counted toward or against coverage.
doneness_meaning.deferred: Ruled out of scope with a recorded reason. Not pending work.

classifier_reclassified_units.predicate: kind=='class_feature' and wiring_class=='display' and status=='grounded' and evidence=='explanation_id_observed_in_a_real_computation', EXCLUDED_BOOKS dropped

status_vocabulary.grounded: A real computed magnitude was OBSERVED reaching a consumer: a feat whose presence changes what compute_pilot_base_chassis returns; a class/race that reaches a real receipt; a class feature whose explanation id appears in a real computation; a monster that resolves to a real stat block through monster_resolve.
status_vocabulary.literal-verified: A `static` unit whose shipped `data/corpus` record was byte-compared, this run, against the upstream corpus literal it cites, by `corpus_literal_sweep --json-out`, and the WHOLE sweep came back CLEAN. Strictly stronger than `ingested-magnitude`/`grounded`/ `text-complete`, which it supersedes for a unit the sweep actually reached: only the producer's `static`/`derived` doneness rung (operator directive 2026-08-13) maps this to `done`. A unit the sweep did not reach, or a sweep that found any mismatch anywhere, leaves every unit at its ordinary status -- this word is never assigned on trust. Meaningful only on a `static`/`derived` unit; if a later reclassification leaves it on any other class the producer reads it as `held`, and the next regen re-derives the status from the class.
status_vocabulary.fixture-verified: A `derived` unit whose engine evaluator was run, this run, over the real corpus record through `compute_equipment_effects` and matched a pinned, independently-derived fixture value exactly, by `derived_evaluator_fixture_check --json-out`. Strictly stronger than `ingested-magnitude`/`grounded`/`text-complete`, which it supersedes for a unit the fixture actually covers: only the producer's `static`/`derived` doneness rung (operator directive 2026-08-13) maps this to `done`. Coverage is 94 of 2,879 held `derived` units by the fixture's own design, not a sample -- a unit outside that coverage, or one the check ran and failed, keeps its ordinary status and stays `held`. Meaningful only on a `static`/`derived` unit; if a later reclassification leaves it on any other class the producer reads it as `held`, and the next regen re-derives the status from the class.
status_vocabulary.ingested-magnitude: The engine holds the record WITH its real numeric fields, but this generator observes no consumer delta for this kind (spells, equipment). Strictly weaker than `grounded` and deliberately a separate word: calling it grounded would be the same over-claim this inventory exists to prevent.
status_vocabulary.text-complete: The engine holds the record, the corpus record carries NO magnitude token at all (so there is no number to compute), AND its token closure carries a real, non-empty, non-.CLEAR/.CLEARALL, non-PI-redacted DESC: value (so there is real prose to show a player). Per Decision 7 (`docs/release/SD-31-corpus-closure-grind/decisions.md`) all three are required; the third was unchecked before SD31-D7-PROSE-001 and 634 units were found `done` on the live board with a null corpus description as a result.
status_vocabulary.deferred-with-reason: A claim-blocking diagnostic the engine itself emits names this unit. `reason` is that diagnostic's message VERBATIM and `reason_id` is its id -- never re-narrated.
status_vocabulary.engine-does-not-hold: The book IS ingested but the engine holds no record matching this unit's identity. A real gap inside a started book, distinct from a book nobody has begun.
status_vocabulary.not-started: The book has no compiled rule set at all. Nothing about this unit has been attempted.
status_vocabulary.unmeasurable: Could not be classified without guessing. `reason` states, per unit, exactly what is missing or ambiguous -- an honest unmeasurable beats a confident wrong entry, and is never a stand-in for work not yet attempted.
status_vocabulary.oracle-agree: A `literal-verified`/`fixture-verified` unit whose id carries a real `agree` verdict in AT-34-E3-005's consolidated bucket-V oracle ledger (`docs/release/SD-34-book-completion/artifacts/epic-3-core-rulebook/bucket-v/bucket-v-consolidated.oracle-results.json`) -- a genuine PCGen oracle round-trip, this run's or a reused, freshness-confirmed prior one, matched the engine's own computed value exactly.
status_vocabulary.oracle-unverifiable: A `literal-verified`/`fixture-verified` unit whose id carries a real `unverifiable` verdict in AT-34-E3-005's consolidated bucket-V oracle ledger. `reason` carries that ledger row's own reason text VERBATIM (e.g. `no_bonus_chain`, `oracle_export_no_spellname_line`, or AT-33-E1-003's `no_probe_surface` census finding) -- never re-narrated. A `disagree` verdict is NEVER mapped here or to `oracle-agree`; it leaves the unit's status untouched so it stays outstanding in bucket V.
